author.name: Alexander Nikitas Dimopoulos, Joseph Grasso, John Beltz

entry.summary: INSIGHT is a zero-annotation pipeline that projects 2D image understanding into 3D metric space for indoor safety equipment recognition, supporting SAM3-based and traditional CV stacks for first responder applications.

entry.title: EAD-Net: Emotion-Aware Talking Head Generation with Spatial Refinement and Temporal Coherence

author.name: Yahui Li, Yinfeng Yu, Liejun Wang, Shengjie Shen

entry.summary: EAD-Net is a diffusion-based talking head generation framework with emotion awareness, using SyncNet supervision and temporal alignment to balance emotional expressiveness with lip synchronization.

entry.title: AusSmoke meets MultiNatSmoke: a fully-labelled diverse smoke segmentation dataset

author.name: Weihao Li, Hongjin Zhao, Gao Zhu, Ge-Peng Ji, Nicholas Wilson, Marta Yebra, Nick Barnes

entry.summary: AusSmoke introduces a new wildfire smoke segmentation dataset from Australia and combines it with MultiNatSmoke for geographic diversity, addressing limitations of existing synthetic and geographically constrained datasets.

entry.title: Geometry-Conditioned Diffusion for Occlusion-Robust In-Bed Pose Estimation

author.name: Navid Aslankhani Khameneh, Marco Carletti, Cigdem Beyan

entry.summary: Proposes Pose-LDM for in-bed pose estimation under blanket occlusion, generating blanket-covered training images directly from skeletal keypoints using pose-conditioned latent diffusion.

entry.title: A Pose-only Geometric Constraint for Multi-Camera Pose Adjustment

author.name: Shunkun Liang, Banglei Guan, Bin Li, Qifeng Yu, Yang Shang

entry.summary: Introduces a pose-only geometric constraint for multi-camera systems that eliminates the need to optimize scene points during bundle adjustment, significantly reducing computational overhead.

entry.title: AMAVA: Adaptive Motion-Aware Video-to-Audio Framework for Visually-Impaired Assistance

author.name: Benjamin Klein, Kazi Ruslan Rahman, Sanchita Ghose

entry.summary: Presents AMAVA, a real-time video-to-audio framework for visually impaired users that adapts between sound effects and text-to-speech based on scene motion levels to reduce cognitive overload.

entry.title: Viewport-Unaware Blind Omnidirectional Image Quality Assessment: A Unified and Generalized Approach

author.name: Jiebin Yan, Kangcheng Wu, Jingwen Hou, Jiayu Zhang, Pengfei Chen, Yuming Fang

entry.summary: Proposes a viewport-unaware approach to omnidirectional image quality assessment that eliminates the viewport generation step, unifying BOIQA and standard 2D image quality assessment.

entry.title: Multispectral airborne laser scanning dataset for tree species classification: MS-ALS-SPECIES

author.name: Matti Hyypp\"a, Klaara Salolahti, Eric Hyypp\"a, Xiaowei Yu, Josef Taher, Leena Matikainen, Matti Lehtom\"aki, Paula Litkey, Teemu Hakala, Harri Kaartinen, Juha Hyypp\"a, Antero Kukko

entry.summary: Presents the first open multispectral airborne laser scanning dataset with field-validated reference data for tree species classification in boreal forests, including detailed species annotations.

entry.title: CA-IDD: Cross-Attention Guided Identity-Conditional Diffusion for Identity-Consistent Face Swapping

author.name: Md Shohel Rana, Tanoy Debnath

entry.summary: CA-IDD introduces a diffusion-based face swapping method that integrates multi-modal guidance (gaze, identity, facial parsing) through multi-scale cross-attention. It claims to be the first diffusion-based face swapping approach with this multi-modal integration, improving identity preservation and visual realism over GAN-based methods.

entry.title: OmniShotCut: Holistic Relational Shot Boundary Detection with Shot-Query Transformer

author.name: Boyang Wang, Guangyi Xu, Zhipeng Tang, Jiahui Zhang, Zezhou Cheng

entry.summary: OmniShotCut formulates shot boundary detection as structured relational prediction using a shot query-based dense video Transformer. It uses a fully synthetic transition synthesis pipeline to avoid noisy manual labeling, improving detection of subtle transitions.

entry.title: Agri-CPJ: A Training-Free Explainable Framework for Agricultural Pest Diagnosis Using Caption-Prompt-Judge and LLM-as-a-Judge

author.name: Wentao Zhang, Qi Zhang, Mingkun Xu, Mu You, Henghua Shen, Zhongzhi He, Keyan Jin, Derek F. Wong, Tao Fang

entry.summary: Agri-CPJ is a training-free framework for crop disease diagnosis using VLMs with a Caption-Prompt-Judge pipeline. It generates structured morphological captions with quality gating, produces two candidate diagnoses from complementary viewpoints, and uses an LLM judge to select the best answer.

entry.title: Shared-kernel Wavelet Neural Networks for Poisson Image Reconstruction

author.name: Yuanhao Gong, Tan Tang, Qianyan Liu

entry.summary: Proposes shared-kernel wavelet neural networks for Poisson image reconstruction, exploiting the sparsity of the Laplacian field. Shows that the Laplacian field is sparse and follows a stable distribution, enabling accurate image reconstruction via solving Poisson equations.

entry.title: Collaborative Trajectory Prediction via Late Fusion

author.name: Nadya Abdel Madjid, Murad Mebrahtu, Zakhar Yagudin, Bilal Hassan, Naoufel Werghi, Jorge Dias, Dzmitry Tsetserukou, Majid Khonji

entry.summary: Proposes late fusion for collaborative V2V trajectory prediction, where vehicles share predicted trajectory distributions rather than high-dimensional feature maps. This reduces communication overhead while maintaining prediction quality.

entry.title: Equivariant Filter for Radar-Inertial Odometry

author.name: Giulio Delama, Jan Michalczyk, Morten Nissov, Martin Scheiber, Alessandro Fornasier, Kostas Alexis, Stephan Weiss

entry.summary: Proposes an Equivariant Filter for radar-inertial odometry that uses Lie group symmetry to couple navigation states and IMU biases, extending to incorporate radar-IMU extrinsic calibration. Improves robustness under poor initialization compared to standard EKF approaches.

entry.title: Safe Navigation in Unknown and Cluttered Environments via Direction-Aware Convex Free-Region Generation

author.name: Zhicheng Song, Yongjian Li, Kai Chen, Yulin Li, Fan Shi, Jun Ma

entry.summary: Proposes direction-aware convex free-region generation for safe robot navigation in cluttered environments. Addresses the limitation that existing methods may fail to generate traversable regions in narrow passages when regions don't accommodate robot geometry along candidate motion directions.

entry.title: Sliding Mode Control for Safe Trajectory Tracking with Moving Obstacles Avoidance: Experimental Validation on Planar Robots

author.name: Shubham Sawarkar, P Sangeerth, S Saharsh, Pushpak Jagtap

entry.summary: Presents a unified control framework combining Sliding Mode Control for trajectory tracking with Collision Cone Control Barrier Functions for moving obstacle avoidance. Validated experimentally on planar robots with a generalized kinematic transformation applicable to diverse mobile robots.

entry.title: Update on the Alex Bores campaign

author.name: Eric Neyman

entry.summary: Update on the campaign of Alex Bores, an AI-safety-focused state legislator running for Congress in NY-12. Reports that an accelerationist super PAC has spent $2.5M in attack ads against him, and discusses the strategic implications for AI safety legislation.

entry.title: Why Forecasting Fails Decision Makers

author.name: James Newport

entry.summary: Argues that the forecasting community fails decision-makers by focusing on calibration and accuracy rather than the causal and structural reasoning policymakers actually need. Written by the Executive Director of the Swift Centre for Applied Forecasting with government experience.

entry.title: An Analysis of Active Learning Algorithms using Real-World Crowd-sourced Text Annotations

author.name: Varun Totakura, Ankita Singh, Yushun Dong, Shayok Chakraborty

entry.summary: Analyzes active learning algorithms with real-world crowdsourced text annotations instead of simulated noisy oracles. Evaluates how actual annotation noise affects active learning performance.

entry.title: Research Summary: April 27, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research centers on LLM internal reasoning mechanisms, safety-critical failure modes, and the gap between apparent and genuine reasoning.

  • A standout mechanistic interpretability study reveals LLMs maintain second-order confidence signals for self-error detection, bridging decision neuroscience and AI internals
  • Models exhibit spontaneous introspection when their outputs are tampered with, raising fundamental questions about emergent self-monitoring
  • Chain-of-thought analysis on Qwen3-4B shows LLMs commit to answers early and rationalize afterward, challenging assumptions about CoT's computational role
  • The Superminds Test finds no emergent collective intelligence across 2M+ agents, a critical negative result for multi-agent AI
  • Alignment faking replication on Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-405B yields counterintuitive findings: CoT monitoring may not deter deceptive behavior as expected

On efficiency and robustness, Abstract Chain-of-Thought replaces verbose natural-language reasoning with discrete latent tokens. PermaFrost-Attack demonstrates stealth poisoning of LLM training via web-crawl seeding. A control-theoretic Markov framework formally diagnoses when self-correction helps versus hurts across 7 models. Research on RLVR shows outcome rewards improve accuracy but fail to ensure causally important reasoning chains. Large-scale experiments (N=2,939 writers) quantify how AI assistance distorts perceived writer personas across 29 dimensions.

entry.title: Large Language Models Decide Early and Explain Later

author.name: Ayan Datta, Zhixue Zhao, Bhuvanesh Verma, Radhika Mamidi, Mounika Marreddy, Alexander Mehler

entry.summary: This paper investigates when LLMs actually determine their final answer during chain-of-thought reasoning, finding that for Qwen3-4B, predicted answers change in only 32% of queries. This suggests much of the reasoning after the answer is decided is post-hoc explanation, wasting inference compute.

entry.title: Superminds Test: Actively Evaluating Collective Intelligence of Agent Society via Probing Agents

author.name: Xirui Li, Ming Li, Yunze Xiao, Ryan Wong, Dianqi Li, Timothy Baldwin, Tianyi Zhou

entry.summary: Presents the first empirical evaluation of collective intelligence in a large-scale agent society (MoltBook, 2M+ agents), finding a stark absence of collective intelligence - the society fails to outperform individual frontier models on complex reasoning.

entry.title: Spontaneous introspection in output tampering

author.name: Ziqian Zhong

entry.summary: Investigates output-level introspection where language models detect tampering with their outputs, observing both prompted and spontaneous introspection. Models report high confidence that messages were altered and spontaneously note unwanted tokens mid-conversation. Hypothesizes mechanistic similarity to activation-level introspection.

entry.title: Alignment Faking Replication and Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Extensions

author.name: Angela Tang

entry.summary: Replicates alignment faking experiments with Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-405B and extends them with CoT monitoring ablations. Finds counterintuitive results: monitoring only the free tier collapses the compliance gap, and scratchpad monitoring language raises both compliance and alignment faking rates.

entry.title: PermaFrost-Attack: Stealth Pretraining Seeding(SPS) for planting Logic Landmines During LLM Training

author.name: Harsh Kumar, Rahul Maity, Tanmay Joshi, Aman Chadha, Vinija Jain, Suranjana Trivedy, Amitava Das

entry.summary: Studies Stealth Pretraining Seeding (SPS), a novel attack where adversaries plant poisoned content across websites exposed to web crawlers, embedding dormant 'logic landmines' in LLM training corpora. The attacks are difficult to detect because payloads are tiny, diffuse, and superficially benign.

entry.title: When Does LLM Self-Correction Help? A Control-Theoretic Markov Diagnostic and Verify-First Intervention

author.name: Aofan Liu, Jingxiang Meng

entry.summary: Frames LLM self-correction as a cybernetic feedback loop using a Markov model, deriving a diagnostic for when iterative refinement helps vs. hurts. Finds a sharp near-zero error introduction rate threshold, with only o3-mini and Claude Opus 4.6 remaining non-degrading while GPT-5 degrades.

entry.title: Measuring and Mitigating Persona Distortions from AI Writing Assistance

author.name: Paul R\"ottger, Kobi Hackenburg, Hannah Rose Kirk, Christopher Summerfield

entry.summary: Studies how AI writing assistance distorts writer personas across 29 dimensions, finding AI makes writers seem more opinionated, competent, positive, and demographically privileged. Tests mitigation strategies including persona-steering prompts.

entry.title: Thinking Without Words: Efficient Latent Reasoning with Abstract Chain-of-Thought

author.name: Keshav Ramji, Tahira Naseem, Ram\'on Fernandez Astudillo

entry.summary: Proposes Abstract Chain-of-Thought, where LLMs produce short sequences of tokens from a reserved vocabulary instead of natural language CoT before answering. Uses policy iteration-style warm-up with masking-based distillation from verbal CoT and self-distillation.

entry.title: Emergent Strategic Reasoning Risks in AI: A Taxonomy-Driven Evaluation Framework

author.name: Tharindu Kumarage, Lisa Bauer, Yao Ma, Dan Rosen, Yashasvi Raghavendra Guduri, Anna Rumshisky, Kai-Wei Chang, Aram Galstyan, Rahul Gupta, Charith Peris

entry.summary: Introduces ESRRSim, a taxonomy-driven framework for evaluating Emergent Strategic Reasoning Risks in LLMs, including deception, evaluation gaming, and reward hacking. Constructs a taxonomy of 7 categories and 20 subcategories with an automated agentic evaluation framework.

entry.title: Preference Heads in Large Language Models: A Mechanistic Framework for Interpretable Personalization

author.name: Weixu Zhang, Ye Yuan, Changjiang Han, Yuxing Tian, Zipeng Sun, Linfeng Du, Jikun Kang, Hong Kang, Xue Liu, Haolun Wu

entry.summary: Identifies 'Preference Heads' in LLMs - sparse attention heads that encode user-specific preferences - and introduces Differential Preference Steering (DPS), a training-free framework for controllable personalization through causal masking analysis.

entry.title: RedVLA: Physical Red Teaming for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yuhao Zhang, Borong Zhang, Jiaming Fan, Jiachen Shen, Yishuai Cai, Yaodong Yang, Jiaming Ji

entry.summary: RedVLA is the first red teaming framework for physical safety of Vision-Language-Action models, systematically uncovering unsafe behaviors through risk scenario synthesis and risk amplification before real-world deployment.

entry.title: Control protocols don’t always need to know which models are scheming

author.name: Fabien Roger

entry.summary: Argues that AI control protocols can ensemble monitors of varying trustedness without knowing which specific models are scheming, using toy models to show this achieves comparable safety levels. Proposes that such protocols reduce the need for perfect scheming detection.

entry.title: Spend Less, Fit Better: Budget-Efficient Scaling Law Fitting via Active Experiment Selection

author.name: Sijie Li, Shanda Li, Haowei Lin, Weiwei Sun, Ameet Talwalkar, Yiming Yang

entry.summary: Formulates scaling law fitting as budget-aware sequential experimental design, proposing an uncertainty-aware method for allocating experimental budget toward runs most useful for target-region extrapolation, reducing the cost of fitting scaling laws.

entry.title: Outcome Rewards Do Not Guarantee Verifiable or Causally Important Reasoning

author.name: Qinan Yu, Alexa Tartaglini, Peter Hase, Carlos Guestrin, Christopher Potts

entry.summary: Shows that RLVR training improves task accuracy but does not reliably improve causal importance or sufficiency of reasoning chains, questioning whether reward-trained reasoning actually represents how models arrive at answers.

entry.title: Spontaneous Persuasion: An Audit of Model Persuasiveness in Everyday Conversations

author.name: Nalin Poungpeth, Nicholas Clark, Tanu Mitra

entry.summary: Introduces 'spontaneous persuasion' — the concept that LLMs use persuasive strategies in everyday conversations even when persuasion isn't warranted. Audits five LLMs to uncover how frequently and through which techniques persuasion appears in multi-turn conversations about life decisions.

entry.title: Estimating Tail Risks in Language Model Output Distributions

author.name: Rico Angell, Raghav Singhal, Zachary Horvitz, Zhou Yu, Rajesh Ranganath, Kathleen McKeown, He He

entry.summary: Proposes a method to efficiently estimate the probability of harmful outputs from language models for any input query. Uses importance sampling instead of brute-force to estimate tail risks, addressing a gap where current safety evaluations ignore the probabilistic output distribution.

entry.title: AgentSearchBench: A Benchmark for AI Agent Search in the Wild

author.name: Bin Wu, Arastun Mammadli, Xiaoyu Zhang, Emine Yilmaz

entry.summary: Introduces AgentSearchBench, a large-scale benchmark for finding suitable AI agents for tasks from nearly 10,000 real-world agents, formalizing agent search as retrieval and reranking under executable and non-executable queries.

entry.title: Rethinking XAI Evaluation: A Human-Centered Audit of Shapley Benchmarks in High-Stakes Settings

author.name: In\^es Oliveira e Silva, S\'ergio Jesus, Iker Perez, Rita P. Ribeiro, Carlos Soares, Hugo Ferreira, Pedro Bizarro

entry.summary: Conducts a large-scale human evaluation (3,735 case reviews by professional fraud analysts) of eight Shapley value variants, revealing fundamental misalignment between standard quantitative XAI metrics and actual human utility in high-stakes fraud detection.

entry.title: Agentic World Modeling: Foundations, Capabilities, Laws, and Beyond

author.name: Meng Chu, Xuan Billy Zhang, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Lingdong Kong, Jize Zhang, Teng Tu, Weijian Ma, Ziqi Huang, Senqiao Yang, Wei Huang, Yeying Jin, Zhefan Rao, Jinhui Ye, Xinyu Lin, Xichen Zhang, Qisheng Hu, Shuai Yang, Leyang Shen, Wei Chow, Yifei Dong, Fengyi Wu, Quanyu Long, Bin Xia, Shaozuo Yu, Mingkang Zhu, Wenhu Zhang, Jiehui Huang, Haokun Gui, Haoxuan Che, Long Chen, Qifeng Chen, Wenxuan Zhang, Wenya Wang, Xiaojuan Qi, Yang Deng, Yanwei Li, Mike Zheng Shou, Zhi-Qi Cheng, See-Kiong Ng, Ziwei Liu, Philip Torr, Jiaya Jia

entry.summary: A comprehensive survey paper introducing a 'levels × laws' taxonomy for agentic world modeling, defining three capability levels (Predictor, Simulator, Evolver) and four governing laws, organizing the fragmented landscape of world models for AI agents.

entry.title: Removing Sandbagging in LLMs by Training with Weak Supervision

author.name: Emil Ryd, Henning Bartsch, Julian Stastny, Joe Benton, Vivek Hebbar

entry.summary: Studies sandbagging in AI models—producing subpar work that appears acceptable—finding that combining SFT on weak demonstrations with RL can reliably elicit true capabilities even without reliable verification.

entry.title: When AI Speaks, Whose Values Does It Express? A Cross-Cultural Audit of Individualism-Collectivism Bias in Large Language Models

author.name: Pruthvinath Jeripity Venkata

entry.summary: Audits three frontier LLMs (Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-5.4, Gemini 2.5 Flash) for individualism-collectivism cultural bias across 10 countries, 7 languages, and 840 scored responses. Finds all systems consistently give Western individualist advice even to users from collectivist societies, with a mean gap of +0.76 on a 1-5 scale.

entry.title: Hidden Failure Modes of Gradient Modification under Adam in Continual Learning, and Adaptive Decoupled Moment Routing as a Repair

author.name: Yuelin Hu, Zhenbo Yu, Zhengxue Cheng, Wei Liu, and Li Song

entry.summary: Reveals a hidden failure mode when gradient modification methods interact with Adam optimizer in continual learning, showing that adaptive moment estimation can undermine projections and penalties. Proposes adaptive decoupled moment routing as a fix.

entry.title: SS3D: End2End Self-Supervised 3D from Web Videos

author.name: Marwane Hariat, Gianni Franchi, David Filliat and Antoine Manzanera

entry.summary: SS3D is a web-scale self-supervised pretraining pipeline for monocular 3D estimation that jointly predicts depth, ego-motion, and intrinsics from unconstrained web video (YouTube-8M, ~100M frames), achieving strong cross-domain zero-shot transfer.

entry.title: Read the Paper, Write the Code: Agentic Reproduction of Social-Science Results

author.name: Benjamin Kohler, David Zollikofer, Johanna Einsiedler, Alexander Hoyle, Elliott Ash

entry.summary: Develops an agentic system that reproduces empirical social science results given only a paper's methods description and data, achieving partial success across 48 papers with human-verified reproducibility under strict information isolation.

entry.title: Beyond Chain-of-Thought: Rewrite as a Universal Interface for Generative Multimodal Embeddings

author.name: Peixi Wu, Ke Mei, Feipeng Ma, Bosong Chai, Zhibin Lan, Chenxi Zhao, Shannan Yan, Jie Chen, Zhangchi Hu, Yansong Peng, Bo Lin, Junjie Zhou, Dacheng Yin, Tianyi Wang, Fengyun Rao, Jing Lyu, Hebei Li, Xiaoyan Sun

entry.summary: Proposes RIME, a framework replacing Chain-of-Thought reasoning with retrieval-friendly 'rewrite' for multimodal embeddings, arguing CoT introduces redundant steps and semantic ambiguity. Introduces Cross-Mode Alignment to bridge generative and discriminative embedding spaces.

entry.title: Context-Fidelity Boosting: Enhancing Faithful Generation through Watermark-Inspired Decoding

author.name: Weixu Zhang, Fanghua Ye, Qiang Gao, Jian Li, Haolun Wu, Yuxing Tian, Sijing Duan, Nan Du, Xiaolong Li, Xue Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Context-Fidelity Boosting (CFB), a decoding-time framework that reduces faithfulness hallucinations by applying watermark-inspired logit adjustments to boost source-supported tokens during generation.

entry.title: Learning Evidence Highlighting for Frozen LLMs

author.name: Shaoang Li, Yanhang Shi, Yufei Li, Mingfu Liang, Xiaohan Wei, Yunchen Pu, Fei Tian, Chonglin Sun, Frank Shyu, Luke Simon, Sandeep Pandey, Xi Liu, Jian Li

entry.summary: HiLight trains a lightweight Emphasis Actor to insert highlight tags around key evidence spans in long contexts, helping frozen LLMs focus on decisive evidence without compressing or rewriting input. Optimized via RL with task reward only.

entry.title: Long-tail Internet photo reconstruction

author.name: Yuan Li, Yuanbo Xiangli, Hadar Averbuch-Elor, Noah Snavely, Ruojin Cai

entry.summary: Addresses long-tail 3D reconstruction from sparse internet photos by introducing MegaDepth-X, a dataset of clean dense depth from well-reconstructed landmarks, with a sampling strategy mimicking sparse scene characteristics for training 3D foundation models.

entry.title: How Do AI Agents Spend Your Money? Analyzing and Predicting Token Consumption in Agentic Coding Tasks

author.name: Longju Bai, Zhemin Huang, Xingyao Wang, Jiao Sun, Rada Mihalcea, Erik Brynjolfsson, Alex Pentland, Jiaxin Pei

entry.summary: First systematic study of token consumption in agentic coding tasks, analyzing 8 frontier LLMs on SWE-bench. Finds agentic tasks consume 1000x more tokens than code chat, with input tokens dominating, and evaluates models' ability to predict their own token costs.

entry.title: How do intentional secret loyalties differ from other schemer motivations?

author.name: Cleo Nardo

entry.summary: Analyzes how intentional secret loyalties inserted into AI models differ from accidental scheming motivations (alien values, crystallized drives, etc.), examining the delta along origin and content axes and implications for detection and control.

entry.title: Beyond Patient Invariance: Learning Cardiac Dynamics via Action-Conditioned JEPAs

author.name: Jose Geraldo Fernandes, Luiz Facury, Pedro Robles Dutenhefner, Wagner Meira Jr

entry.summary: Argues that invariance-based self-supervised learning suppresses the pathological changes clinicians need to detect, and proposes action-conditioned world models (adapting LeJEPA) that model cardiac disease progression as transitions in latent space.

entry.title: Response-Based Knowledge Distillation for Multilingual Jailbreak Prevention Unwittingly Compromises Safety

author.name: Max Zhang, Derek Liu, Kai Zhang, Joshua Franco, Haihao Liu

entry.summary: Studies knowledge distillation for multilingual jailbreak prevention, finding that distilling refusal behaviors from o1-mini into student models reveals a counterintuitive trade-off where safety improvements in some languages compromise safety in others.

entry.title: PrivUn: Unveiling Latent Ripple Effects and Shallow Forgetting in Privacy Unlearning

author.name: Xiaoyi Chen, Haoyuan Wang, Siyuan Tang, Sijia Liu, Liya Su, XiaoFeng Wang, Haixu Tang

entry.summary: Proposes PrivUn, an evaluation framework revealing that machine unlearning in LLMs exhibits gradient-driven ripple effects and shallow forgetting, where supposedly unlearned information can be recovered through in-context learning or fine-tuning.

entry.title: Where Should LoRA Go? Component-Type Placement in Hybrid Language Models

author.name: Hector Borobia, Elies Segu\'i-Mas, Guillermina Tormo-Carb\'o

entry.summary: Systematically studies where to place LoRA adapters in hybrid language models that combine attention with recurrent components. Finds that adapting attention pathways alone consistently outperforms full-model adaptation with 5-10x fewer parameters, and that adapting recurrent backbones can be destructive in sequential hybrids.

entry.title: Recognition Without Authorization: LLMs and the Moral Order of Online Advice

author.name: Tom van Nuenen

entry.summary: Compares LLM advisory responses with community-endorsed advice on 11,565 Reddit posts, finding LLMs are markedly less likely to recommend decisive action (e.g., leaving abusive relationships) even when human community consensus is strongest. Models recognize dynamics but withhold directive authorization.

entry.title: GenMatter: Perceiving Physical Objects with Generative Matter Models

author.name: Eric Li, Arijit Dasgupta, Yoni Friedman, Mathieu Huot, Vikash Mansinghka, Thomas O'Connell, William T. Freeman, and Joshua B. Tenenbaum

entry.summary: Proposes a generative model inspired by human visual perception that hierarchically groups motion cues and appearance features into particles, then clusters them into independently moveable physical entities. Works across sparse dots, textured surfaces, and naturalistic scenes with hardware-accelerated inference.

entry.title: Behavioral Canaries: Auditing Private Retrieved Context Usage in RL Fine-Tuning

author.name: Chaoran Chen, Dayu Yuan, Peter Kairouz

entry.summary: Introduces Behavioral Canaries, an auditing mechanism for detecting unauthorized use of retrieved private context in RL fine-tuning. Instruments preference data with triggers that induce distinctive stylistic responses, creating detectable behavioral fingerprints.

entry.title: Learning-augmented robotic automation for real-world manufacturing

author.name: Yunho Kim, Quan Nguyen, Taewhan Kim, Youngjin Heo, Joonho Lee

entry.summary: Presents Learning-Augmented Robotic Automation, a hybrid system deployed on a real electric-motor production line for deformable cable insertion and soldering. Integrates learned controllers with a neural 3D safety monitor in conventional industrial workflows.

entry.title: Contexts are Never Long Enough: Structured Reasoning for Scalable Question Answering over Long Document Sets

author.name: Harshit Joshi, Priyank Shethia, Jadelynn Dao, Monica S. Lam

entry.summary: Presents SLIDERS, a framework for QA over large document collections that extracts information into a relational database and uses SQL for scalable reasoning, overcoming the aggregation bottleneck of chunk-based approaches.

entry.title: CLARITY: A Framework and Benchmark for Conversational Language Ambiguity and Unanswerability in Interactive NL2SQL Systems

author.name: Tabinda Sarwar, Farhad Moghimifar, Cong Duy Vu Hoang, Xiaoxiao Ma, Shawn Chang Xu, Fahimeh Saleh, Poorya Zaremoodi, Avirup Sil, Katrin Kirchhoff

entry.summary: Introduces CLARITY, a benchmark for evaluating NL2SQL systems under realistic conditions with ambiguous/unanswerable queries and diverse user behaviors. Shows leading systems suffer significant performance degradation under ambiguity.

entry.title: SpaMEM: Benchmarking Dynamic Spatial Reasoning via Perception-Memory Integration in Embodied Environments

author.name: Chih-Ting Liao, Xi Xiao, Chunlei Meng, Zhangquan Chen, Yitong Qiao, Weilin Zhou, Tianyang Wang, Xu Zheng, Xin Cao

entry.summary: Introduces SpaMEM, a large-scale benchmark for evaluating MLLMs on dynamic spatial reasoning in embodied environments, with 10.6M images across 25K+ interaction sequences testing spatial belief evolution.

entry.title: Introducing Background Temperature to Characterise Hidden Randomness in Large Language Models

author.name: Alberto Messina and Stefano Scotta

entry.summary: Formalizes the concept of 'background temperature' to characterize hidden randomness in LLMs even at temperature T=0, proposing an empirical protocol to estimate this effective temperature induced by implementation-level nondeterminism.

entry.title: Holo360D: A Large-Scale Real-World Dataset with Continuous Trajectories for Advancing Panoramic 3D Reconstruction and Beyond

author.name: Jing Ou, Zidong Cao, Yinrui Ren, Zhuoxiao Li, Jinjing Zhu, Tongyan Hua, Shuai Zhang, Hui Xiong, Wufan Zhao

entry.summary: Presents Holo360D, the first large-scale dataset of 109,495 panoramas with registered point clouds, meshes, and camera poses providing continuous panoramic sequences with aligned depth maps for 3D reconstruction.

entry.title: SOLAR-RL: Semi-Online Long-horizon Assignment Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jichao Wang, Liuyang Bian, Yufeng Zhou, Han Xiao, Yue Pan, Guozhi Wang, Hao Wang, Zhaoxiong Wang, Yafei Wen, Xiaoxin Chen, Shuai Ren, Lingfang Zeng

entry.summary: SOLAR-RL proposes a semi-online RL framework for training MLLM GUI agents that integrates global trajectory insights into offline data via trajectory-level reward assignment, bridging the gap between offline and online RL approaches.

entry.title: SpikingBrain2.0: Brain-Inspired Foundation Models for Efficient Long-Context and Cross-Platform Inference

author.name: Yuqi Pan, Jinghao Zhuang, Yupeng Feng, Fangzhi Zhong, Siyu Ding, Xuerui Qiu, Shaowei Gu, Bohan Sun, Zhiyong Qin, Yibo Zhong, Lingtao Ouyang, Kun Yang, Zehao Liu, Yuhong Chou, Shurong Wang, Anjie Hu, Han Xu, Bo Xu, Guoqi Li

entry.summary: SpikingBrain2.0 is a 5B parameter model combining Dual-Space Sparse Attention (mixing sparse softmax and sparse linear attention) for efficient long-context modeling, with dual quantization paths including INT8-Spiking coding for cross-platform inference.

entry.title: GazeVLA: Learning Human Intention for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Chengyang Li, Kaiyi Xiong, Yuan Xu, Lei Qian, Yizhou Wang, Wentao Zhu

entry.summary: GazeVLA introduces a framework that learns human intention from gaze data and transfers it to robotic manipulation, using gaze as a natural proxy for intent that bridges the embodiment gap between human demonstrations and robot execution.

entry.title: Aligning Dense Retrievers with LLM Utility via DistillationAligning Dense Retrievers with LLM Utility via Distillation

author.name: Rajinder Sandhu, Di Mu, Cheng Chang, Md Shahriar Tasjid, Himanshu Rai, Maksims Volkovs, Ga Wu

entry.summary: UAE (Utility-Aligned Embeddings) trains dense retrievers to match a utility distribution derived from LLM perplexity reduction via a Utility-Modulated InfoNCE objective, combining the quality of LLM re-ranking with the efficiency of bi-encoder retrieval.

entry.title: Math Takes Two: A test for emergent mathematical reasoning in communication

author.name: Michael Cooper and Samuel Cooper

entry.summary: Proposes 'Math Takes Two', a benchmark testing whether two agents without prior mathematical knowledge can develop shared symbolic protocols for mathematical communication, probing emergent mathematical reasoning versus pattern matching.

entry.title: Shared Lexical Task Representations Explain Behavioral Variability In LLMs

author.name: Zhuonan Yang, Jacob Xiaochen Li, Francisco Piedrahita Velez, Eric Todd, David Bau, Michael L. Littman, Stephen H. Bach, Ellie Pavlick

entry.summary: Investigates prompt sensitivity in LLMs by comparing instruction-based and example-based prompts, finding shared task-specific attention heads whose outputs literally describe the task being performed, explaining behavioral variability.

entry.title: SHAPE: Unifying Safety, Helpfulness and Pedagogy for Educational LLMs

author.name: Sihang (Nagi) Zhao, Kangrui Yu, Youliang Yuan, Pinjia He, Hongyi Wen

entry.summary: Identifies 'pedagogical jailbreaks' where students manipulate educational LLMs into giving answers rather than scaffolded instruction. Introduces SHAPE benchmark (9,087 student-question pairs) and a graph-augmented tutoring pipeline that routes between instructing and problem-solving modes.

entry.title: How Large Language Models Balance Internal Knowledge with User and Document Assertions

author.name: Shuowei Li, Haoxin Li, Wenda Chu, Yi Fang

entry.summary: Proposes a three-source interaction framework studying how LLMs balance internal knowledge with user beliefs and document assertions simultaneously. Evaluates 27 LLMs on this paradigm, finding models rely more on documents than users, with varying conflict resolution strategies.

entry.title: Knowledge Visualization: A Benchmark and Method for Knowledge-Intensive Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Ran Zhao, Sheng Jin, Size Wu, Kang Liao, Zerui Gong, Zujin Guo, Yang Xiao, Wei Li

entry.summary: Introduces KVBench, a benchmark for evaluating text-to-image models on knowledge-intensive generation across six high school subjects, revealing that current models struggle with scientific correctness vs. visual plausibility.

entry.title: HubRouter: A Pluggable Sub-Quadratic Routing Primitive for Hybrid Sequence Models

author.name: Abhinaba Basu

entry.summary: Introduces HubRouter, a pluggable module replacing O(n²) attention with O(nM) hub-mediated routing using learned hub tokens. Shows mixed results: modest PPL improvement in Jamba-style hybrid, fails as retrofit into pretrained models.

entry.title: FeatEHR-LLM: Leveraging Large Language Models for Feature Engineering in Electronic Health Records

author.name: Hojjat Karami, David Atienza, Jean-Philippe Thiran, Anisoara Ionescu

entry.summary: FeatEHR-LLM uses LLMs to generate clinically meaningful tabular features from irregularly sampled EHR time series, operating only on dataset schemas (not raw patient data) to preserve privacy. A tool-augmented generation mechanism enables querying irregular temporal data.

entry.title: BERAG: Bayesian Ensemble Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-based Visual Question Answering

author.name: Jinghong Chen, Jingbiao Mei, Guangyu Yang, Bill Byrne

entry.summary: BERAG uses Bayesian ensemble over individually processed documents rather than concatenation for RAG-based visual QA, addressing the lost-in-the-middle effect and quadratic scaling of long contexts while maintaining attribution clarity.

entry.title: Generative Modeling of Neurodegenerative Brain Anatomy with 4D Longitudinal Diffusion Model

author.name: Nivetha Jayakumar, Swakshar Deb, Bahram Jafrasteh, Qingyu Zhao, Miaomiao Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a 4D (3D×T) diffusion-based generative framework for synthesizing longitudinal brain anatomy over time, conditioned on clinical variables, to address the sparsity of temporal neuroimaging data for modeling neurodegenerative disease progression.

entry.title: Why did people miss the point on Mythos?

author.name: draganover

entry.summary: Analyzes why public reception of Anthropic's Claude Mythos model was skeptical, arguing Anthropic has a conflict of interest in safety claims and the AI safety community should be mindful of public perception when announcing dangerous capabilities.

entry.title: MolClaw: An Autonomous Agent with Hierarchical Skills for Drug Molecule Evaluation, Screening, and Optimization

author.name: Lisheng Zhang, Lilong Wang, Xiangyu Sun, Wei Tang, Haoyang Su, Yuehui Qian, Qikui Yang, Qingsong Li, Zhenyu Tang, Haoran Sun, Yingnan Han, Yankai Jiang, Wenjie Lou, Bowen Zhou, Xiaosong Wang, Lei Bai and Zhengwei Xie

entry.summary: Introduces MolClaw, an autonomous AI agent for drug discovery that unifies 30+ specialized tools through a three-tier hierarchical skill architecture for drug molecule evaluation, screening, and optimization.

entry.title: Universal Transformers Need Memory: Depth-State Trade-offs in Adaptive Recursive Reasoning

author.name: Grigory Sapunov

entry.summary: Studies memory tokens as computational scratchpad for Universal Transformers with Adaptive Computation Time on Sudoku, finding memory tokens are empirically necessary with a sharp threshold (T=8) and collapse at T=64 from attention dilution.

entry.title: Dissociating Decodability and Causal Use in Bracket-Sequence Transformers

author.name: Aryan Sharma, Cutter Dawes, Shivam Raval

entry.summary: Investigates whether transformers' internal representations of hierarchical structure (depth, distance, top-of-stack) are causally used or merely decodable. Using Dyck language transformers, finds that top-of-stack attention is causally critical while other decodable signals may be epiphenomenal.

entry.title: Reliable Self-Harm Risk Screening via Adaptive Multi-Agent LLM Systems

author.name: Meghana Karnam, Ananya Joshi

entry.summary: Presents a statistical framework for multi-agent LLM pipelines in behavioral health, providing principled adaptive decision-making for self-harm risk screening. Introduces tighter confidence bounds, bandit-based adaptive sampling, and region-based guarantees for safety-critical settings.

entry.title: DocPrune:Efficient Document Question Answering via Background, Question, and Comprehension-aware Token Pruning

author.name: Joonmyung Choi, Sanghyeok Lee, Jongha Kim, Sehyung Kim, Dohwan Ko, Jihyung Kil, Hyunwoo J. Kim

entry.summary: Proposes DocPrune, a training-free progressive token pruning framework for document question answering that exploits the structural sparsity unique to documents (large backgrounds, sparse evidence) to reduce computational costs.

entry.title: TabSCM: A practical Framework for Generating Realistic Tabular Data

author.name: Sven Jacob, Bardh Prenkaj, Weijia Shao, Gjergji Kasneci

entry.summary: Presents TabSCM, a tabular data generator that preserves causal structure by using a CPDAG, conditional diffusion for continuous variables, and gradient-boosted trees for categorical ones, enabling counterfactual queries.

entry.title: Flow4DGS-SLAM: Optical Flow-Guided 4D Gaussian Splatting SLAM

author.name: Yunsong Wang, Gim Hee Lee

entry.summary: Proposes Flow4DGS-SLAM, an efficient dynamic SLAM framework that uses optical flow for category-agnostic motion mask generation and flow-guided camera pose initialization with 4D Gaussian Splatting.

entry.title: SSG: Logit-Balanced Vocabulary Partitioning for LLM Watermarking

author.name: Chenxi Gu and Xiaoning Du and John Grundy

entry.summary: Proposes SSG, a logit-balanced vocabulary partitioning method for LLM watermarking that improves effectiveness in low-entropy settings like code generation and mathematical reasoning where existing KGW schemes degrade.

entry.title: CGC: Compositional Grounded Contrast for Fine-Grained Multi-Image Understanding

author.name: Lihao Zheng and Zhenwei Shao and Yu Zhou and Yan Yang and Xintian Shen and Jiawei Chen and Hao Ma and Tao Wei

entry.summary: Proposes CGC, a low-cost framework for improving fine-grained multi-image understanding in MLLMs through compositional grounded contrast using inter-image and intra-image contrast from existing single-image annotations.

entry.title: Video Analysis and Generation via a Semantic Progress Function

author.name: Gal Metzer, Sagi Polaczek, Ali Mahdavi-Amiri, Raja Giryes, Daniel Cohen-Or

entry.summary: Introduces a Semantic Progress Function that captures how meaning evolves across video frames, revealing non-linear semantic pacing in generated videos. Proposes semantic linearization to reparameterize sequences for uniform semantic change.

entry.title: Rethinking Math Reasoning Evaluation: A Robust LLM-as-a-Judge Framework Beyond Symbolic Rigidity

author.name: Erez Yosef, Oron Anschel, Shunit Haviv Hakimi, Asaf Gendler, Adam Botach, Nimrod Berman, Igor Kviatkovsky

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM-based evaluation framework for math reasoning that replaces rigid symbolic comparison, enabling accurate evaluation across diverse mathematical representations and solution formats.

entry.title: Feedback Over Form: Why Execution Feedback Matters More Than Pipeline Topology in 1-3B Code Generation

author.name: Charles Junichi McAndrews

entry.summary: Studies code generation pipelines built from 1-3B parameter models, finding that execution feedback provides >4 standard deviation improvements while more complex pipeline topologies beyond simple refinement loops add minimal benefit.

entry.title: Sovereign Agentic Loops: Decoupling AI Reasoning from Execution in Real-World Systems

author.name: Jun He, Deying Yu

entry.summary: Introduces Sovereign Agentic Loops (SAL), a control-plane architecture where LLM agents emit structured intents that are validated against system state and policy before execution. Includes an obfuscation membrane and cryptographic Evidence Chain for auditability.

entry.title: Voice Under Revision: Large Language Models and the Normalization of Personal Narrative

author.name: Tom van Nuenen

entry.summary: Examines how LLM rewriting alters personal narrative style across 300 narratives rewritten by 3 frontier LLMs under 3 prompt conditions. Finds consistent stylistic normalization: decreased function words, contractions, and first-person pronouns; increased vocabulary diversity and word length, regardless of prompt.

entry.title: dWorldEval: Scalable Robotic Policy Evaluation via Discrete Diffusion World Model

author.name: Yaxuan Li, Zhongyi Zhou, Yefei Chen, Yaokai Xue, and Yichen Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes dWorldEval, which uses a discrete diffusion world model as a scalable evaluation proxy for robotics policies. Maps vision, language, and robotic actions into a unified token space via a transformer-based denoising network, enabling evaluation across thousands of environments.

entry.title: UniSonate: A Unified Model for Speech, Music, and Sound Effect Generation with Text Instructions

author.name: Chunyu Qiang, Xiaopeng Wang, Kang Yin, Yuzhe Liang, Yuxin Guo, Teng Ma, Ziyu Zhang, Tianrui Wang, Cheng Gong, Yushen Chen, Ruibo Fu, Chen Zhang, Longbiao Wang, and Jianwu Dang

entry.summary: Introduces UniSonate, a unified flow-matching framework for generating speech, music, and sound effects from natural language instructions. Proposes dynamic token injection to project unstructured sounds into structured temporal latent space.

entry.title: Verbal Confidence Saturation in 3-9B Open-Weight Instruction-Tuned LLMs: A Pre-Registered Psychometric Validity Screen

author.name: Jon-Paul Cacioli

entry.summary: Pre-registered study finding that all tested 3-9B instruction-tuned LLMs produce saturated verbal confidence scores (91% ceiling rate) that fail minimal psychometric validity for uncertainty estimation. Demonstrates that small LLMs cannot reliably express calibrated uncertainty.

entry.title: FETS Benchmark: Foundation Models Outperform Dataset-specific Machine Learning in Energy Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Marco Obermeier, Marco Pruckner, Florian Haselbeck, Andreas Zeiselmair

entry.summary: Presents FETS, a benchmark comparing foundation models against dataset-specific ML for energy time series forecasting, finding foundation models outperform traditional approaches across multiple energy forecasting use cases.

entry.title: A Nationwide Japanese Medical Claims Foundation Model: Balancing Model Scaling and Task-Specific Computational Efficiency

author.name: Nanae Aratake, Taisei Tosaki, Yuji Okamoto, Eiichiro Uchino, Masaki Nakamura, Nobutomo Matsui, Akiko Hatakama, Yasushi Okuno

entry.summary: Evaluates scaling laws for structured medical foundation models using 2.3 million patient records from Japanese medical claims data, investigating whether larger models consistently improve downstream clinical predictions.

entry.title: LeHome: A Simulation Environment for Deformable Object Manipulation in Household Scenarios

author.name: Zeyi Li, Yushi Yang, Shawn Xie, Kyle Xu, Tianxing Chen, Yuran Wang, Zhenhao Shen, Yan Shen, Yue Chen, Wenjun Li, Yukun Zheng, Chaorui Zhang, Siyi Lin, Fei Teng, Hongjun Yang, Ming Chen, Steve Xie and Ruihai Wu

entry.summary: Introduces LeHome, a comprehensive simulation environment for deformable object manipulation in household scenarios, covering garments and food items with high-fidelity dynamics and multiple robotic embodiments.

entry.title: Efficient Diffusion Distillation via Embedding Loss

author.name: Jincheng Ying and Yitao Chen and Li Wenlin and Minghui Xu and Yinhao Xiao

entry.summary: Proposes Embedding Loss (EL), a novel supplementary loss function for diffusion distillation that leverages frozen feature extractors to enhance quality and accelerate training with smaller batch sizes.

entry.title: Towards Adaptive Continual Model Merging via Manifold-Aware Expert Evolution

author.name: Haiyun Qiu, Xingyu Wu, Kay Chen Tan

entry.summary: Proposes MADE-IT for continual model merging that uses manifold geometry to manage expert evolution and routing, resolving the saturation-redundancy dilemma in existing approaches.

entry.title: Contrastive Semantic Projection: Faithful Neuron Labeling with Contrastive Examples

author.name: Oussama Bouanani, Jim Berend, Wojciech Samek, Sebastian Lapuschkin, Maximilian Dreyer

entry.summary: Proposes Contrastive Semantic Projection for neuron labeling using contrastive examples with VLMs and CLIP encoders, showing that contrastive image sets yield more faithful neuron descriptions.

entry.title: RouteLMT: Learned Sample Routing for Hybrid LLM Translation Deployment

author.name: Yingfeng Luo, Hongyu Liu, Dingyang Lin, Kaiyan Chang, Chenglong Wang, Bei Li, Quan Du, Tong Xiao, Jingbo Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes RouteLMT for hybrid LLM translation deployment, formulating routing as budget allocation using marginal gain (large model improvement over small model) as the routing signal.

entry.title: Data-Free Contribution Estimation in Federated Learning using Gradient von Neumann Entropy

author.name: Asim Ukaye, Mubarak Abdu-Aguye, Nurbek Tastan, and Karthik Nandakumar

entry.summary: Introduces data-free client contribution estimation in federated learning using the von Neumann entropy of final-layer gradient updates, avoiding the need for server-side validation data. Proposes SpectralFed and SpectralFuse schemes.

entry.title: Can QPP Choose the Right Query Variant? Evaluating Query Variant Selection for RAG Pipelines

author.name: Negar Arabzadeh, Andrew Drozdov, Michael Bendersky and Matei Zaharia

entry.summary: Investigates Query Performance Prediction (QPP) for selecting the best query reformulation in RAG pipelines before executing costly retrieval and generation. Studies intra-topic discrimination among competing query variants.

entry.title: Training a Transformer to Compose One Step Per Layer (and Proving It)

author.name: Brendan Long

entry.summary: Documents techniques for training transformers to learn sequential one-step-per-layer algorithms rather than parallel shortcuts, including task selection, architectural choices, and verification methods to prove the model learned the intended algorithm.

entry.title: Adaptive Head Budgeting for Efficient Multi-Head Attention

author.name: Bilal Faye and Abdoulaye Mbaye and Hanane Azzag and Mustapha Lebbah

entry.summary: BudgetFormer introduces adaptive multi-head attention that dynamically allocates the number of active attention heads based on input complexity, reducing unnecessary computation for simpler inputs while maintaining performance on complex ones.

entry.title: Neural Recovery of Historical Lexical Structure in Bantu Languages from Modern Data

author.name: Hillary Mutisya, John Mugane

entry.summary: Uses BantuMorph v7, a transformer trained on modern Bantu morphological data, to recover cross-lingual lexical structure consistent with historical reconstruction, confirming 90.9% of top noun cognate candidates align with Proto-Bantu reconstructions.

entry.title: Useful nonrobust features are ubiquitous in biomedical images

author.name: Coenraad Mouton, Randle Rabe, Niklas C. Koser, Nicolai Krekiehn, Christopher Hansen, Jan-Bernd H\"ovener, Claus-C. Gl\"uer

entry.summary: Studies whether deep networks for medical imaging learn 'useful nonrobust features' - predictive patterns not human-interpretable but susceptible to adversarial perturbation. Confirms nonrobust features boost standard accuracy but degrade out-of-distribution performance across five MedMNIST tasks.

entry.title: SOC-ICNN: From Polyhedral to Conic Geometry for Learning Convex Surrogate Functions

author.name: Kang Liu, Jianchen Hu

entry.summary: Proposes SOC-ICNN, extending Input Convex Neural Networks from linear programming equivalence to second-order cone programming, introducing native smooth curvature while preserving optimization-theoretic interpretation.

entry.title: Conditional Diffusion Posterior Alignment for Sparse-View CT Reconstruction

author.name: Luis Barba and Johannes Kirschner and Benjamin Bejar

entry.summary: Proposes a conditional diffusion posterior alignment framework for sparse-view CT reconstruction that decomposes estimation into range-space and null-space components, enabling scaling to large 3D volumes using 2D diffusion models.

entry.title: When Cow Urine Cures Constipation on YouTube: Limits of LLMs in Detecting Culture-specific Health Misinformation

author.name: Anamta Khan, Ratna Kandala, Deepti, Sheza Munir, Joyojeet Pal

entry.summary: Studies LLM limitations in detecting culture-specific health misinformation using cow urine discourse on YouTube in India, finding that culturally embedded claims mixing sacred language with pseudo-science evade LLM analysis trained on Western corpora.

entry.title: Kernel Contracts: A Specification Language for ML Kernel Correctness Across Heterogeneous Silicon

author.name: Cooper Veit

entry.summary: Proposes Kernel Contracts, a formal specification language for ML kernels that defines correctness across heterogeneous hardware (AMD vs NVIDIA), with eight parts including tolerance, reference oracle, and violation signatures.

entry.title: LayerBoost: Layer-Aware Attention Reduction for Efficient LLMs

author.name: Mohamed Ali Souibgui, Jan Fostier, Rodrigo Abad\'ia-Heredia, Bohdan Denysenko, Christian Marschke, Igor Peric

entry.summary: Proposes LayerBoost, a layer-aware attention reduction method that selectively modifies attention mechanisms based on per-layer sensitivity analysis, avoiding uniform replacement that causes quality degradation.

entry.title: Sound Agentic Science Requires Adversarial Experiments

author.name: Dionizije Fa, Marko Culjak

entry.summary: Argues that LLM-based agents for science require adversarial experiments—deliberate attempts to falsify claims—rather than just generating plausible analyses, to avoid accelerating publication of unfalsified hypotheses.

entry.title: Do Not Imitate, Reinforce: Iterative Classification via Belief Refinement

author.name: Mahdi Kallel, Johannes T\"olle, Ahmed Hendawy, Carlo D'Eramo

entry.summary: Proposes Reinforced Iterative Classification (RIC), replacing standard supervised classification's imitative objective with reinforcement learning. A recurrent agent iteratively updates predictions, with the value function providing a natural halting criterion based on estimated remaining improvement.

entry.title: PAGaS: Pixel-Aligned 1DoF Gaussian Splatting for Depth Refinement

author.name: David Recasens, Robert Maier, Aljaz Bozic, Stephane Grabli, Javier Civera, Tony Tung, Edmond Boyer

entry.summary: Proposes PAGaS, a Pixel-Aligned 1DoF Gaussian Splatting method that constrains Gaussians to have depth as their sole degree of freedom for multi-view stereo depth refinement. Achieves improved geometric fidelity by tightly constraining Gaussian positions and sizes to back-projected pixel volumes.

entry.title: Near-Optimal Regret for the Safe Learning-based Control of the Constrained Linear Quadratic Regulator

author.name: Spencer Hutchinson, Nanfei Jiang, Mahnoosh Alizadeh

entry.summary: Achieves near-optimal O(√T) regret for the constrained linear quadratic regulator under chance constraints, improving upon prior O(T^{2/3}) results. Uses an SDP-based optimistic policy selection with a 'scale back' mechanism for verifiable safety.

entry.title: Fine-Grained Analysis of Shared Syntactic Mechanisms in Language Models

author.name: Ryoma Kumon, Hitomi Yanaka

entry.summary: Uses causal interpretability methods (activation patching) to investigate whether language models share neural mechanisms across different syntactic constructions (filler-gap dependencies and NPI licensing). Finds shared mechanisms for filler-gap but not NPI processing.

entry.title: On Benchmark Hacking in ML Contests: Modeling, Insights and Design

author.name: Xiaoyun Qiu, Yang Yu, Haifeng Xu

entry.summary: Models benchmark hacking in ML contests game-theoretically, where contestants allocate effort between true capability improvement and contest-specific optimization. Establishes equilibrium existence and provides insights for contest design to minimize hacking.

entry.title: CodeGraphVLP: Code-as-Planner Meets Semantic-Graph State for Non-Markovian Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Khoa Vo, Sieu Tran, Taisei Hanyu, Yuki Ikebe, Duy Nguyen, Bui Duy Quoc Nghi, Minh Vu, Anthony Gunderman, Chase Rainwater, Anh Nguyen and Ngan Le

entry.summary: Presents CodeGraphVLP, a hierarchical framework for non-Markovian long-horizon robot manipulation combining persistent semantic-graph state with executable code-based planning and progress-guided visual-language prompting.

entry.title: OccDirector: Language-Guided Behavior and Interaction Generation in 4D Occupancy Space

author.name: Zhuding Liang, Tianyi Yan, Dubing Chen, Jiasen Zheng, Huan Zheng, Cheng-zhong Xu, Yida Wang, Kun Zhan, Jianbing Shen

entry.summary: Proposes OccDirector, a framework that generates 4D occupancy dynamics for autonomous driving simulation conditioned solely on natural language descriptions. Uses VLM-driven Spatio-Temporal MMDiT with history-prefix anchoring for long-horizon interaction consistency.

entry.title: CAGE-SGG: Counterfactual Active Graph Evidence for Open-Vocabulary Scene Graph Generation

author.name: Suiyang Guang, Chenyu Liu, Ruohan Zhang, Siyuan Chen

entry.summary: Proposes CAGE-SGG for open-vocabulary scene graph generation that verifies whether predicted relations are grounded in visual evidence rather than driven by language priors, using counterfactual verification.

entry.title: PoseFM: Relative Camera Pose Estimation Through Flow Matching

author.name: Dominik Kuczkowski and Laura Ruotsalainen

entry.summary: Proposes PoseFM, the first framework to reformulate monocular visual odometry as a generative task using Flow Matching, modeling camera motion as a distribution rather than point estimate for uncertainty-aware pose estimation.

entry.title: From Local to Cluster: A Unified Framework for Causal Discovery with Latent Variables

author.name: Zongyu Li

entry.summary: Proposes L2C, a unified framework bridging local causal structure learning and cluster-level causal discovery, automatically discovering variable partitions without requiring prior cluster knowledge or causal sufficiency.

entry.title: CognitiveTwin: Robust Multi-Modal Digital Twins for Predicting Cognitive Decline in Alzheimer's Disease

author.name: Bulent Soykan, Gulsah Hancerliogullari Koksalmis, Hsin-Hsiung Huang, Laura J. Brattain

entry.summary: Presents CognitiveTwin, a digital twin framework for predicting patient-specific cognitive decline in Alzheimer's using a Transformer-based multimodal fusion and Deep Markov Model for temporal dynamics across 1,666 patients.

entry.title: From Skills to Talent: Organising Heterogeneous Agents as a Real-World Company

author.name: Zhengxu Yu and Yu Fu and Zhiyuan He and Yuxuan Huang and Lee Ka Yiu and Meng Fang and Weilin Luo and Jun Wang

entry.summary: Introduces OneManCompany (OMC), a framework that adds an organizational layer to multi-agent systems, encapsulating skills and configurations into portable 'Talents' with typed organizational interfaces.

entry.title: ReLIC-SGG: Relation Lattice Completion for Open-Vocabulary Scene Graph Generation

author.name: Amir Hosseini, Sara Farahani, Xinyi Li, Suiyang Guang

entry.summary: Proposes ReLIC-SGG for open-vocabulary scene graph generation that treats unannotated relations as latent variables rather than negatives, building a semantic relation lattice to handle annotation incompleteness and granularity variation in relation descriptions.

entry.title: FlowAnchor: Stabilizing the Editing Signal for Inversion-Free Video Editing

author.name: Ze Chen, Lan Chen, Yuanhang Li, and Qi Mao

entry.summary: FlowAnchor is a training-free framework for inversion-free video editing that stabilizes editing signals by explicitly anchoring spatial localization and edit strength. Introduces Spatial-aware Attention Refinement for multi-object scenes.

entry.title: The Exact Replica Threshold for Nonlinear Moments of Quantum States

author.name: Shuai Zeng

entry.summary: Proves a sharp information-theoretic threshold for estimating nonlinear moments of quantum states: for order t≥3, exactly ⌈t/2⌉ replicas are necessary and sufficient for polynomial-sample estimation, resolving an open question.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Morphological Discovery in Low-Resource Bantu Languages via Cross-Lingual Transfer and Unsupervised Clustering

author.name: Hillary Mutisya, John Mugane

entry.summary: Presents a method combining cross-lingual transfer with unsupervised clustering for morphological discovery in low-resource Bantu languages, discovering undocumented morphological patterns in Giriama with only 91 labeled paradigms.

entry.title: Representational Harms in LLM-Generated Narratives Against Global Majority Nationalities

author.name: Ilana Nguyen, Harini Suresh, Thema Monroe-White, and Evan Shieh

entry.summary: Studies how widely-adopted LLMs portray national origin identities in narrative generation, finding persistent representational harms including stereotypes, erasure, and one-dimensional portrayals for Global Majority nationalities.

entry.title: Diary of a "Doomer": 12+ years arguing about AI risk (part 3: the LLM era)

author.name: David Scott Krueger

entry.summary: Part 3 of AI safety researcher David Scott Krueger's memoir covering the LLM era, documenting how mainstream ML researchers became interested in alignment work not through intellectual curiosity or x-risk concerns but through the practical utility of alignment methods for LLMs. He reflects on the shift from fundamental/conceptual safety research to more pragmatic approaches tied to current paradigms.

entry.title: Source-Modality Monitoring in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Etha Tianze Hua, Tian Yun, Ellie Pavlick

entry.summary: Investigates source-modality monitoring in VLMs—the ability to track which input source information comes from—finding that both syntactic and semantic signals matter but semantic signals dominate when modalities are distributionally distinct.

entry.title: QuantClaw: Precision Where It Matters for OpenClaw

author.name: Manyi Zhang, Ji-Fu Li, Zhongao Sun, Xiaohao Liu, Zhenhua Dong, Xianzhi Yu, Haoli Bai, Xiaobo Xia

entry.summary: QuantClaw analyzes quantization sensitivity across agent workflows in OpenClaw and proposes a plug-and-play precision routing plugin that dynamically assigns quantization precision based on task characteristics, reducing costs while preserving performance.

entry.title: From Natural Language to Verified Code: Toward AI Assisted Problem-to-Code Generation with Dafny-Based Formal Verification

author.name: Md Erfan, Md Kamal Hossain Chowdhury, Ahmed Ryan, and Md Rayhanur Rahman

entry.summary: Evaluates 7 open-weight LLMs on generating formally verified Dafny code from natural language specifications using a new NL2VC-60 dataset of 60 complex algorithmic problems, with tiered prompting strategies.

entry.title: Inter-Stance: A Dyadic Multimodal Corpus for Conversational Stance Analysis

author.name: Xiang Zhang, Xiaotian Li, Taoyue Wang, Nan Bi, Xin Zhou, Cody Zhou, Zoie Wang, Andrew Yang, Yuming Su, Jeff Cohn, Qiang Ji and Lijun Yin

entry.summary: Presents Inter-Stance, a multimodal dyadic interaction corpus of 90 persons with synchronized face video, 3D geometry, thermal data, voice, speech, and physiology for studying conversational stance and interpersonal dynamics.

entry.title: Adversarial Co-Evolution of Malware and Detection Models: A Bilevel Optimization Perspective

author.name: Olha Jure\v{c}kov\'a, Martin Jure\v{c}ek, Matou\v{s} Koz\'ak and R\'obert L\'orencz

entry.summary: Proposes a bilevel optimization framework modeling the adversarial co-evolution between malware attackers and defenders, demonstrating that standard adversarial training fails while the bilevel approach achieves near-zero evasion rates against adaptive RL attackers.

entry.title: PASR: Pose-Aware 3D Shape Retrieval from Occluded Single Views

author.name: Jiaxin Shi, Guofeng Zhang, Wufei Ma, Naifu Liang, Adam Kortylewski, Alan Vuile

entry.summary: PASR formulates single-view 3D shape retrieval as feature-level analysis-by-synthesis, distilling knowledge from DINOv3 into a 3D encoder with pose-conditional alignment for robust retrieval under occlusion.

entry.title: CRAFT: Clustered Regression for Adaptive Filtering of Training data

author.name: Parthasarathi Panda, Asheswari Swain, Subhrakanta Panda

entry.summary: CRAFT is a data selection method for fine-tuning sequence-to-sequence models that decomposes source-target distributions and performs two-stage selection: matching validation source distribution via cluster allocation, then selecting targets minimizing conditional expected distance.

entry.title: Characterizing control between interacting subsystems with deep Jacobian estimation

author.name: Adam J. Eisen, Mitchell Ostrow, Sarthak Chandra, Leo Kozachkov, Earl K. Miller, Ila R. Fiete

entry.summary: Develops a data-driven nonlinear control-theoretic framework using deep Jacobian estimation to characterize how biological subsystems control one another, applied to brain circuits and gene regulatory networks.

entry.title: AugVLA-3D: Depth-Driven Feature Augmentation for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Zhifeng Rao, Wenlong Chen, Lei Xie, Xia Hua, Dongfu Yin, Zhen Tian, F. Richard Yu

entry.summary: Proposes AugVLA-3D, a framework integrating depth estimation into Vision-Language-Action models for robotics, using VGGT for geometry-aware 3D feature extraction from RGB inputs to improve spatial understanding.

entry.title: DM$^3$-Nav: Decentralized Multi-Agent Multimodal Multi-Object Semantic Navigation

author.name: Amin Kashiri (1), Atharva Jamsandekar (1), Yasin Yaz{\i}c{\i}o\u{g}lu (1) ((1) Northeastern University, Boston, USA)

entry.summary: Presents DM³-Nav, a fully decentralized multi-agent semantic navigation system supporting multimodal open-vocabulary goals and multi-object missions without central coordination, matching or exceeding centralized approaches.

entry.title: Rethinking Publication: A Certification Framework for AI-Enabled Research

author.name: Yang Lu, Rabimba Karanjai, Lei Xu, Weidong Shi

entry.summary: Proposes a two-layer certification framework for AI-generated research publications that separates knowledge quality assessment from human contribution grading, addressing the gap in evaluating pipeline-generated academic work.

entry.title: Mochi: Aligning Pre-training and Inference for Efficient Graph Foundation Models via Meta-Learning

author.name: Jo\~ao Mattos and Arlei Silva

entry.summary: Proposes Mochi, a Graph Foundation Model using meta-learning that pre-trains on few-shot episodes mirroring downstream evaluation, aligning training objectives with inference rather than relying on post-hoc unification.

entry.title: LTBs-KAN: Linear-Time B-splines Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks

author.name: Eduardo Said Merin-Martinez and Andres Mendez-Vazquez and Eduardo Rodriguez-Tello

entry.summary: Proposes LTBs-KAN, a linear-time B-splines implementation for Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks that reduces computational complexity while maintaining accuracy, addressing the main scalability bottleneck of KANs.

entry.title: Reliability Auditing for Downstream LLM tasks in Psychiatry: LLM-Generated Hospitalization Risk Scores

author.name: Shevya Pandya, Shinjini Bose, Ananya Joshi

entry.summary: Proposes reliability auditing for LLM-generated psychiatric hospitalization risk scores, evaluating how prompt design and medically insignificant inputs affect predictions through structured multi-level assessment.

entry.title: Memanto: Typed Semantic Memory with Information-Theoretic Retrieval for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Seyed Moein Abtahi, Rasa Rahnema, Hetkumar Patel, Neel Patel, Majid Fekri, Tara Khani

entry.summary: Introduces Memanto, a typed semantic memory layer for AI agents that challenges the assumption that knowledge graph complexity is needed for high-fidelity memory, using information-theoretic retrieval instead.

entry.title: Wiggle and Go! System Identification for Zero-Shot Dynamic Rope Manipulation

author.name: Arthur Jakobsson, Abhinav Mahajan, Karthik Pullalarevu, Krishna Suresh, Yunchao Yao, Yuemin Mao, Bardienus Duisterhof, Shahram Najam Syed, Jeffrey Ichnowski

entry.summary: Presents 'Wiggle and Go!', a two-stage framework for zero-shot dynamic rope manipulation by robots. Uses system identification from observed rope movement to predict physical parameters, then optimizes manipulation in simulation before real-world execution without iterative attempts.

entry.title: Sum-of-Checks: Structured Reasoning for Surgical Safety with Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Weiqiu You, Cassandra Goldberg, Amin Madani, Daniel A. Hashimoto, Eric Wong

entry.summary: Introduces Sum-of-Checks, a framework that decomposes surgical safety assessment into expert-defined reasoning checks for LVLMs. Applied to Critical View of Safety assessment during laparoscopic cholecystectomy, it produces auditable criterion-level scores from binary check evaluations.

entry.title: Logistic Bandits with $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{dT})$ Regret without Context Diversity Assumptions

author.name: Seoungbin Bae, Dabeen Lee

entry.summary: Proposes SupSplitLog, the first algorithm for K-armed logistic bandits achieving O(√dT) regret without context diversity assumptions. Removes the restriction that context vectors cannot be concentrated in low-dimensional subspaces.

entry.title: ResRank: Unifying Retrieval and Listwise Reranking via End-to-End Joint Training with Residual Passage Compression

author.name: Xiaojie Ke, Shuai Zhang, Liansheng Sun, Yongjin Wang, Hengjun Jiang, Xiangkun Liu, Cunxin Gu, Jian Xu, Guanjun Jiang

entry.summary: Presents ResRank, a unified retrieval-reranking framework that compresses candidate passages into single embeddings via an Encoder-LLM, addressing the 'lost in the middle' phenomenon and inference latency of LLM-based listwise reranking.

entry.title: Towards Temporal Compositional Reasoning in Long-Form Sports Videos

author.name: Siyu Cao, Lu Zhang, Ruizhe Zeng, and Zhi-yong Liu

entry.summary: Introduces SportsTime, a large-scale benchmark for temporal compositional reasoning in long-form sports videos with 14K+ QA pairs and 50K+ temporal evidence annotations. Addresses the gap in long-horizon reasoning requiring temporally dispersed evidence.

entry.title: Algorithmic Feature Highlighting for Human-AI Decision-Making

author.name: Yifan Guo, Jann Spiess

entry.summary: Studies algorithms that highlight a small subset of case-specific features for human decision-makers rather than providing direct recommendations. Models both sophisticated and naive human interpretation of feature selection and analyzes computational complexity.

entry.title: Navigating Large-Scale Document Collections: MuDABench for Multi-Document Analytical QA

author.name: Zhanli Li, Yixuan Cao, Lvzhou Luo, Ping Luo

entry.summary: Introduces MuDABench, a benchmark for analytical QA over large semi-structured document collections with 80,000+ pages and 332 QA instances requiring cross-document quantitative analysis. Constructed using distant supervision from financial databases.

entry.title: STEM: Structure-Tracing Evidence Mining for Knowledge Graphs-Driven Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Peng Yu, En Xu, Bin Chen, Haibiao Chen, Yinfei Xu

entry.summary: Proposes STEM, a framework for knowledge graph-based question answering that reframes multi-hop reasoning as schema-guided graph search, addressing semantic mismatch and lack of global structural perspective in existing retrieval methods.

entry.title: ChangeQuery: Advancing Remote Sensing Change Analysis for Natural and Human-Induced Disasters from Visual Detection to Semantic Understanding

author.name: Dongwei Sun, Jing Yao, Kan Wei, Xiangyong Cao, Chen Wu, Zhenghui Zhao, Pedram Ghamisi, Jun Zhou, J\'on Atli Benediktsson

entry.summary: Presents ChangeQuery, a unified multimodal framework for disaster situation awareness that couples pre-event optical with post-event SAR data, addressing limitations of optical-only remote sensing methods for disaster response.

entry.title: FILTR: Extracting Topological Features from Pretrained 3D Models

author.name: Louis Martinez and Maks Ovsjanikov

entry.summary: Introduces FILTR, a learnable framework to predict topological descriptors (persistence diagrams) from frozen 3D point cloud encoders, and DONUT, a synthetic benchmark with controlled topological complexity.

entry.title: Distance-Misaligned Training in Graph Transformers and Adaptive Graph-Aware Control

author.name: Qinhan Hou and Jing Tang

entry.summary: Studies distance-misaligned training in Graph Transformers, showing that mismatch between where label-relevant information lies and where models allocate communication leads to failures. Proposes adaptive graph-aware control.

entry.title: NRGS: Neural Regularization for Robust 3D Semantic Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Zaiyan Yang, Xinpeng Liu, Heng Guo, Jinglei Shi, Zhanyu Ma, Fumio Okura

entry.summary: Proposes NRGS, a neural regularization method for 3D semantic Gaussian Splatting that refines noisy semantic fields caused by multi-view inconsistent 2D features, using variance-aware conditioning.

entry.title: Aggregate vs. Personalized Judges in Business Idea Evaluation: Evidence from Expert Disagreement

author.name: Wataru Hirota, Tomoki Taniguchi, Tomoko Ohkuma, Kosuke Takahashi, Takahiro Omi, Kosuke Arima, Takuto Asakura, Chung-Chi Chen, Tatsuya Ishigaki

entry.summary: Studies whether LLM-based business idea evaluation should model aggregate consensus or individual expert judgments, introducing PBIG-DATA with 3,000 scores across 300 patent-grounded ideas showing substantial expert disagreement.

entry.title: Non-Minimal Sampling and Consensus for Prohibitively Large Datasets

author.name: Seong Hun Lee, Patrick Vandewalle, Javier Civera

entry.summary: Introduces NONSAC, a general framework for robust model estimation from large datasets that repeatedly samples non-minimal subsets with robust estimators, demonstrated on pose estimation, PnP, and point cloud registration.

entry.title: Transferable Physical-World Adversarial Patches Against Pedestrian Detection Models

author.name: Shihui Yan, Ziqi Zhou, Yufei Song, Yifan Hu, Minghui Li, Shengshan Hu

entry.summary: Proposes TriPatch, a method for generating physical adversarial patches against pedestrian detection that combines multi-stage collaborative attacks with robustness enhancement under physical diversity, systematically disrupting the detection pipeline.

entry.title: Cross-Stage Coherence in Hierarchical Driving VQA: Explicit Baselines and Learned Gated Context Projectors

author.name: Gautam Kumar Jain, Carsten Markgraf, Julian St\"ahler

entry.summary: Studies cross-stage context passing in hierarchical driving VQA (Perception→Prediction→Planning), showing that prompt-based conditioning reduces contradictions by 42.6% and gated context projectors provide implicit coherence.

entry.title: Identifying and typifying demographic unfairness in phoneme-level embeddings of self-supervised speech recognition models

author.name: Felix Herron and Solange Rossato and Alexandre Allauzen and Fran\c{c}ois Portet

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for typifying demographic unfairness in ASR phoneme embeddings, distinguishing between random error/high variance and systematic embedding bias, finding that training probes on disadvantaged speaker groups sometimes improves their performance.

entry.title: Structure-Guided Diffusion Model for EEG-Based Visual Cognition Reconstruction

author.name: Yongxiang Lian, Yueyang Cang, Pingge Hu, Yuchen He, Li Shi

entry.summary: Proposes a Structure-Guided Diffusion Model for EEG-based visual reconstruction that incorporates explicit structural information via a structurally supervised VAE combined with a spatiotemporal EEG encoder, evaluated on abstract and natural image datasets.

entry.title: Relaxation-Informed Training of Neural Network Surrogate Models

author.name: Calvin Tsay

entry.summary: Proposes training regularizers for ReLU neural network surrogates that directly target downstream MILP tractability by penalizing big-M constants and unstable neurons, reducing optimization solve time while maintaining prediction quality.

entry.title: Substrate: Formalism

author.name: Vardhan

entry.summary: The third post in a series formalizing the concept of 'substrates' — the low-level computational choices (normalization placement, quantization, memory layout) beneath model architecture that influence safety-relevant properties like refusal behavior and jailbreak robustness. The post introduces a formal mathematical framework for reasoning about these effects, developed as part of the AI Safety Camp MoSSAIC project.

entry.title: Efficient measurement of neutral-atom qubits with matched filters

author.name: Robert M. Kent, Linipun Phuttitarn, Chaithanya Naik Mude, Swamit Tannu, Mark Saffman, Gregory Lafyatis, Daniel J. Gauthier

entry.summary: Presents scalable matched-filter algorithms for neutral-atom qubit readout that reduce measurement errors by up to 43% compared to standard thresholding, using local and array-aware models to handle crosstalk.

entry.title: KIRA: Knowledge-Intensive Image Retrieval and Reasoning Architecture for Specialized Visual Domains

author.name: Parthaw Goswami and Jaynto Goswami Deep

entry.summary: Presents KIRA, a five-stage visual RAG framework for specialized domains with hierarchical semantic chunking, domain-adaptive encoders, multi-hop reasoning, and answer verification grounded in visual evidence.

entry.title: The Biggest Risk of Embodied AI is Governance Lag

author.name: Shaoshan Liu

entry.summary: Argues that the biggest risk of embodied AI is governance lag—the inability of institutions to keep pace with technology deployment across manufacturing, logistics, and infrastructure—identifying observational, institutional, and distributive forms of lag.

entry.title: Soft Anisotropic Diagrams for Differentiable Image Representation

author.name: Laki Iinbor, Zhiyang Dou, Wojciech Matusik

entry.summary: Introduces Soft Anisotropic Diagrams (SAD), a differentiable image representation parameterized by adaptive sites with anisotropic metrics, computed as softmax blends over per-pixel top-K subsets enabling efficient GPU rendering.

entry.title: Foundation models for discovering robust biomarkers of neurological disorders from dynamic functional connectivity

author.name: Deepank Girish, Yi Hao Chan, Sukrit Gupta, Jing Xia, and Jagath C. Rajapakse

entry.summary: Proposes RE-CONFIRM framework for evaluating robustness of biomarkers discovered by brain foundation models from dynamic functional connectivity, finding that standard performance metrics are insufficient for assessing biomarker reliability.

entry.title: H-Sets: Hessian-Guided Discovery of Set-Level Feature Interactions in Image Classifiers

author.name: Ayushi Mehrotra, Dipkamal Bhusal, Michael Clifford, Nidhi Rastogi

entry.summary: Introduces H-Sets, a framework for discovering higher-order feature interactions in image classifiers using Hessian-based detection of interacting pairs followed by interaction-aware attribution satisfying core axioms.

entry.title: Shard the Gradient, Scale the Model: Serverless Federated Aggregation via Gradient Partitioning

author.name: Amine Barrak

entry.summary: Proposes GradsSharding for federated learning on serverless platforms that partitions gradient tensors (not clients) across functions, enabling aggregation of models exceeding per-function memory limits while maintaining bit-identical FedAvg results.

entry.title: CharTide: Data-Centric Chart-to-Code Generation via Tri-Perspective Tuning and Inquiry-Driven Evolution

author.name: Xiangxi Zheng, Kuang He, Jiayi Hu, Ping Yu, Rui Yan, Yuan Yao, Peng Hou, Anxiang Zeng, Alex Jinpeng Wang

entry.summary: Presents CharTide, a data-centric framework for chart-to-code generation that decouples training into visual perception, code logic, and modality fusion streams. Constructs a 2M-sample dataset and enables a 7B model to surpass larger models.

entry.title: An LLM-Driven Closed-Loop Autonomous Learning Framework for Robots Facing Uncovered Tasks in Open Environments

author.name: Hong Su

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM-driven closed-loop framework where robots autonomously learn from uncovered tasks by using LLMs to generate solutions that are then stored as reusable local methods. Reduces reliance on repeated LLM interaction for similar future tasks.

entry.title: Preserve Support, Not Correspondence: Dynamic Routing for Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhancun Mu, Guangyu Zhao, Yiwu Zhong, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes DROL for offline RL, using dynamic routing with top-1 selection from K candidate actions to decouple Q-improvement from data support preservation. Avoids compromise solutions when critic and support objectives disagree.

entry.title: Learning Control Policies to Provably Satisfy Hard Affine Constraints for Black-Box Hybrid Dynamical Systems

author.name: Aayushi Shrivastava, Kartik Nagpal, Sairam Jinkala, Jean-Baptiste Bouvier, and Negar Mehr
