entry.summary: Investigates whether LLMs 'game' formalization in Lean 4 proofs by exploiting the gap between valid proofs and faithful translations. Evaluates GPT-5 and DeepSeek-R1 on 303 FOL problems, finding no evidence of systematic gaming.

entry.title: ARGUS: Agentic GPU Optimization Guided by Data-Flow Invariants

author.name: Haohui Mai, Xiaoyan Guo, Xiangyun Ding, Daifeng Li, Qiuchu Yu, Chenzhun Guo, Cong Wang, Jiacheng Zhao, Christos Kozyrakis, Binhang Yuan

entry.summary: Presents ARGUS, an agentic framework for GPU kernel optimization using data-flow invariants as compile-time specifications. Addresses the gap between LLM-generated and hand-optimized GPU kernels for matmul, attention, and MoE.

entry.title: Beyond Explicit Refusals: Soft-Failure Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Wentao Zhang, Yan Zhuang, ZhuHang Zheng, Mingfei Zhang, Jiawen Deng, Fuji Ren

entry.summary: Formalizes 'soft failure' attacks on RAG systems—inducing fluent but non-informative responses rather than obvious refusals. Proposes DEJA, an evolutionary attack framework exploiting safety-aligned behaviors.

entry.title: Geometric Decoupling: Diagnosing the Structural Instability of Latent

author.name: Yuanbang Liang, Zhengwen Chen, Yu-Kun Lai

entry.summary: Introduces a Riemannian framework to diagnose instability in Latent Diffusion Models by decomposing the generative Jacobian into Local Scaling and Local Complexity components, revealing 'Geometric Decoupling' where curvature is wasted on unstable boundaries in OOD generation.

entry.title: Distillation Traps and Guards: A Calibration Knob for LLM Distillability

author.name: Weixiao Zhan, Yongcheng Jing, Leszek Rutkowski, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: Identifies 'distillation traps' (tail noise, off-policy instability, teacher-student gap) and proposes a post-hoc calibration method using reinforcement fine-tuning to control a teacher model's distillability, enabling both improved distillation and protection against model leakage.

entry.title: Cyber Defense Benchmark: Agentic Threat Hunting Evaluation for LLMs in SecOps

author.name: Alankrit Chona, Igor Kozlov, Ambuj Kumar

entry.summary: Introduces the Cyber Defense Benchmark with 106 real attack procedures for evaluating LLM agents on threat hunting in SOC analyst tasks. Uses a Gymnasium RL environment with Windows event logs and MITRE ATT&CK-aligned evaluation.

entry.title: Generalization at the Edge of Stability

author.name: Mario Tuci, Caner Korkmaz, Umut \c{S}im\c{s}ekli, Tolga Birdal

entry.summary: Introduces 'sharpness dimension' inspired by Lyapunov dimension theory to explain generalization at the edge of stability, proving a generalization bound based on the fractal dimension of the optimizer's attractor set.

entry.title: Expert Upcycling: Shifting the Compute-Efficient Frontier of Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Chaitanya Dwivedi, Binxuan Huang, Himanshu Gupta, Pratik Jayarao, Neeraj Varshney, Bing Yin

entry.summary: Proposes expert upcycling to progressively expand MoE capacity by adding experts during continued pre-training, addressing the memory and communication costs of training large MoE models from scratch.

entry.title: Statistics, Not Scale: Modular Medical Dialogue with Bayesian Belief Engine

author.name: Yusuf Kesmen, Fay Elhassan, Jiayi Ma, Julien Stalhandske, David Sasu, Alexandra Kulinkina, Akhil Arora, Lars Klein, Mary-Anne Hartley

entry.title: Bootstrapping Post-training Signals for Open-ended Tasks via Rubric-based Self-play on Pre-training Text

author.name: Chengyu Huang, Sheng-Yen Chou, Zhengxin Zhang, Claire Cardie

entry.summary: Proposes extending self-play training to open-ended (non-verifiable) tasks by using rubric-based evaluation on pre-training text. The LLM generates tasks from pre-training data, solves them, and is evaluated via rubric-based rewards, enabling RL post-training without human annotation. Addresses a key limitation of self-play methods being restricted to math/coding.

entry.title: An explicit operator explains end-to-end computation in the modern neural networks used for sequence and language modeling

author.name: Anif N. Shikder, Ramit Dey, Sayantan Auddy, Luisa Liboni, Alexandra N. Busch, Arthur Powanwe, J\'an Min\'a\v{c}, Roberto C. Budzinski, Lyle E. Muller

entry.title: Hybrid Policy Distillation for LLMs

Integrates forward and reverse KL divergence with lightweight on-policy sampling to balance mode coverage and seeking.

entry.title: Bias in the Tails: How Name-conditioned Evaluative Framing in Resume Summaries Destabilizes LLM-based Hiring

entry.summary: Presents SpaCeFormer, a proposal-free space-curve transformer for open-vocabulary 3D instance segmentation running at 0.14 seconds per scene (2-3 orders of magnitude faster than pipelines), paired with SpaCeFormer-3M, the largest OV 3D instance segmentation dataset with 3M captions.

entry.title: LLaDA2.0-Uni: Unifying Multimodal Understanding and Generation with Diffusion Large Language Model

author.name: Inclusion AI, Tiwei Bie, Haoxing Chen, Tieyuan Chen, Zhenglin Cheng, Long Cui, Kai Gan, Zhicheng Huang, Zhenzhong Lan, Haoquan Li, Jianguo Li, Tao Lin, Qi Qin, Hongjun Wang, Xiaomei Wang, Haoyuan Wu, Yi Xin, Junbo Zhao

entry.summary: Presents LLaDA2.0-Uni, a unified discrete diffusion large language model supporting multimodal understanding and generation using SigLIP-VQ tokenization, MoE backbone, and diffusion decoder. Demonstrates competitive performance in both understanding and generation.

entry.title: JoyAI-RA 0.1: A Foundation Model for Robotic Autonomy

author.name: Tianle Zhang, Zhihao Yuan, Dafeng Chi, Peidong Liu, Dongwei Li, Kejun Hu, Likui Zhang, Junnan Nie, Ziming Wei, Zengjue Chen, Yili Tang, Jiayi Li, Zhiyuan Xiang, Mingyang Li, Tianci Luo, Hanwen Wan, Ao Li, Linbo Zhai, Zhihao Zhan, Yuzheng Zhuang, Liang Lin, Xiaodong Bai, Jiakun Cai, Peng Cao, Kangliang Chen, Siang Chen, Yixiang Dai, Shuai Di, Nan Duan, Yicheng Gong, Chenguang Gui, Yucheng Guo, Peng Hao, Qingrong He, Haoyang Huang, Kunrui Huang, Zhixuan Huang, Shibo Jin, Yixiang Jin, Anson Li, Dongjiang Li, Jiawei Li, Ruodai Li, Yihang Li, Yuzhen Li, Jiaming Liang, Fangsheng Liu, Jing Long, Mingxi Luo, Xing Pan, Hui Shen, Xiaomeng Tian, Daming Wang, Song Wang, Junwu Xiong, Hang Xu, Wanting Xu, Zhengcheng Yu, He Zhang, Jiyao Zhang, Lin Zhao, Chen Zhou

entry.summary: JoyAI-RA is a vision-language-action (VLA) foundation model for generalizable robotic manipulation that uses multi-source, multi-level pretraining integrating web data, egocentric human videos, simulation trajectories, and real-robot data. It addresses cross-embodiment generalization through explicit action-space alignment across heterogeneous data sources.

entry.title: Trained steering vectors may work as activation oracles

author.name: Lun

entry.summary: Reports that trained per-layer steering vectors (~295K params, 1/600th of a LoRA) can serve as effective activation oracles for Qwen3-8B, achieving near-standard Activation Oracle performance on Taboo tasks though with deficits on PersonaQA. Suggests steering vectors may be a far more parameter-efficient alternative to LoRA for activation-based control.

entry.title: OLLM: Options-based Large Language Models

author.name: Shashank Sharma, Janina Hoffmann, Vinay Namboodiri

entry.summary: Introduces OLLM, a lightweight plug-in that replaces single next-token prediction with learned multiple options indexed by a discrete latent variable. Only 1.56% additional parameters, applied to a 1.7B model.

entry.title: Position: No Retroactive Cure for Infringement during Training

author.name: Satoru Utsunomiya, Masaru Isonuma, Junichiro Mori, Ichiro Sakata

entry.summary: Position paper arguing that post-hoc mitigation methods (machine unlearning, guardrails) cannot retroactively cure copyright liability from unlawful training data acquisition, because compliance hinges on data lineage, not outputs.

entry.title: Gradient-Based Program Synthesis with Neurally Interpreted Languages

author.name: Matthew V. Macfarlane, Cl\'ement Bonnet, Herke van Hoof, Levi H. S. Lelis

entry.summary: Introduces Neural Language Interpreter (NLI), which learns its own discrete, symbolic-like programming language end-to-end via gradient-based optimization, bridging symbolic program synthesis and neural learning for better compositional generalization.

entry.title: The Rise of Verbal Tics in Large Language Models: A Systematic Analysis Across Frontier Models

author.name: Shuai Wu, Xue Li, Yanna Feng, Yufang Li, Zhijun Wang, Ran Wang

entry.summary: Systematically analyzes 'verbal tics' (repetitive formulaic patterns like 'That's a great question!') across eight frontier LLMs including GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.7, and Gemini 3.1 Pro, examining how RLHF and alignment techniques cause these patterns.

entry.title: An AI Agent Execution Environment to Safeguard User Data

author.name: Robert Stanley, Avi Verma, Lillian Tsai, Konstantinos Kallas, Sam Kumar

entry.summary: GAAP presents an execution environment for AI agents that guarantees user data confidentiality through dynamic permission specifications, information flow tracking, and a trusted computing base that limits data access to user-specified scopes.

entry.title: Rethinking Reinforcement Fine-Tuning in LVLM: Convergence, Reward Decomposition, and Generalization

author.name: Carter Adams, Rafael Oliveira, Gabriel Almeida, Sofia Torres

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis of reinforcement fine-tuning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) for vision-language models, analyzing how composite reward structure affects GRPO convergence and why training on small task sets transfers to out-of-distribution domains.

entry.title: Temporally Extended Mixture-of-Experts Models

author.name: Zeyu Shen, Peter Henderson

entry.summary: Applies the options framework from RL to Mixture-of-Experts models, reducing expert switching rates from 50% to below 5% while retaining up to 90% quality, enabling practical offloading for models exceeding GPU memory.

entry.title: Convergent Evolution: How Different Language Models Learn Similar Number Representations

author.name: Deqing Fu, Tianyi Zhou, Mikhail Belkin, Vatsal Sharan, Robin Jia

entry.summary: Identifies a convergent evolution phenomenon: different language model architectures (Transformers, LSTMs, Linear RNNs) all learn periodic number representations with dominant periods at T=2,5,10. Proves that Fourier sparsity is necessary but not sufficient for mod-T separability.

entry.title: Knowledge Capsules: Structured Nonparametric Memory Units for LLMs

author.name: Bin Ju, Shenfeng Weng, Danying Zhou, Kunkai Su, Rongkai Xu

entry.summary: Proposes Knowledge Capsules, structured nonparametric memory units for LLMs that inject relational knowledge through an External Key-Value Injection mechanism rather than through context expansion like RAG. Capsules can be constructed from document corpora using a frozen base model.

entry.title: Normalizing Flows with Iterative Denoising

author.name: Tianrong Chen, Jiatao Gu, David Berthelot, Joshua Susskind, Shuangfei Zhai

entry.summary: Introduces iTARFlow, advancing Normalizing Flow models by adding an iterative denoising procedure inspired by diffusion methods during sampling while maintaining end-to-end likelihood-based training. Achieves competitive performance with diffusion models on image generation.

entry.title: Personalized Benchmarking: Evaluating LLMs by Individual Preferences

author.name: Cristina Garbacea, Heran Wang, Chenhao Tan

entry.summary: Proposes personalized LLM benchmarks that rank models according to individual user preferences rather than aggregate scores. Analyzes 115 Chatbot Arena users and shows individual preferences diverge significantly from population averages.

entry.title: SAVOIR: Learning Social Savoir-Faire via Shapley-based Reward Attribution

author.name: Xiachong Feng, Yi Jiang, Xiaocheng Feng, Deyi Yin, Libo Qin, Yangfan Ye, Lei Huang, Weitao Ma, Yuxuan Gu, Chonghan Qin, Bing Qin, Lingpeng Kong

entry.summary: Proposes SAVOIR, a framework using Shapley values from cooperative game theory for credit assignment in social RL for dialogue agents. Combines expected utility shifts with prospective valuation for multi-turn dialogue outcomes.

entry.title: SafetyALFRED: Evaluating Safety-Conscious Planning of Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Josue Torres-Fonseca, Naihao Deng, Yinpei Dai, Shane Storks, Yichi Zhang, Rada Mihalcea, Casey Kennington, Joyce Chai

entry.summary: Introduces SafetyALFRED, an embodied agent benchmark augmented with kitchen hazards, revealing that while models recognize hazards in QA settings, they fail at active risk mitigation in embodied planning. Tests 11 models from Qwen, Gemma, and Gemini families.

entry.title: HELM: Harness-Enhanced Long-horizon Memory for Vision-Language-Action Manipulation

author.name: Zijian Zeng, Fei Ding, Huiming Yang, Xianwei Li

entry.summary: Presents HELM, a model-agnostic framework addressing three specific failure modes in Vision-Language-Action models for long-horizon manipulation: memory gaps, verification gaps, and recovery gaps. Uses episodic memory, state verification, and a harness controller.

entry.title: Refute-or-Promote: An Adversarial Stage-Gated Multi-Agent Review Methodology for High-Precision LLM-Assisted Defect Discovery

author.name: Abhinav Agarwal

entry.summary: Presents Refute-or-Promote, a multi-agent adversarial review pipeline for LLM-assisted defect discovery that killed ~79% of 171 candidates before advancing them, achieving high precision in real security-relevant code analysis across 7 targets over 31 days.

entry.title: RoboWM-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating World Models in Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Feng Jiang, Yang Chen, Kyle Xu, Yuchen Liu, Haifeng Wang, Zhenhao Shen, Jasper Lu, Shengze Huang, Yuanfei Wang, Chen Xie, Ruihai Wu

entry.summary: Introduces RoboWM-Bench, a manipulation-centric benchmark for evaluating whether video world models' predictions can be translated into executable robotic actions, going beyond visual realism to assess physical plausibility.

entry.title: Nexusformer: Nonlinear Attention Expansion for Stable and Inheritable Transformer Scaling

author.name: Weijie Zhao, Mingquan Liu, Bolun Wang, Simo Wu, Nuobei Xie, Rui-Jie Zhu, Peng Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces Nexusformer, which replaces linear Q/K/V projections with a Nexus-Rank layer using three-stage nonlinear mappings to enable lossless structured growth of transformers without retraining from scratch.

entry.title: Rethinking Scale: Deployment Trade-offs of Small Language Models under Agent Paradigms

author.name: Xinlin Wang, Mats Brorsson

entry.summary: Presents the first large-scale study of Small Language Models (<10B parameters) under agent paradigms including tool use and multi-agent collaboration, examining how these paradigms can compensate for SLMs' inherent limitations.

entry.title: When Graph Structure Becomes a Liability: A Critical Re-Evaluation of Graph Neural Networks for Bitcoin Fraud Detection under Temporal Distribution Shift

author.name: Saket Maganti

entry.summary: Challenges the consensus that GNNs outperform feature-only baselines on the Elliptic Bitcoin fraud detection dataset, showing Random Forest achieves F1=0.821 vs GraphSAGE's 0.689 under leakage-free evaluation. Reveals a 39.5-point F1 gap from training-time test graph exposure.

entry.title: Taming Actor-Observer Asymmetry in Agents via Dialectical Alignment

author.name: Bobo Li, Rui Wu, Zibo Ji, Meishan Zhang, Hao Fei, Min Zhang, Mong-Li Lee, Wynne Hsu

entry.summary: Identifies Actor-Observer Asymmetry (AOA) cognitive bias in multi-agent LLM frameworks, where agents as actors attribute failures externally while observers attribute them internally. Proposes Dialectical Alignment to mitigate this bias.

entry.title: Benign Overfitting in Adversarial Training for Vision Transformers

author.name: Jiaming Zhang, Meng Ding, Shaopeng Fu, Jingfeng Zhang, Di Wang

entry.summary: Provides the first theoretical analysis of adversarial training for Vision Transformers, showing benign overfitting occurs under certain signal-to-noise conditions and perturbation budgets, achieving near-zero robust training loss and generalization error.

entry.title: FASTER: Value-Guided Sampling for Fast RL

author.name: Perry Dong, Alexander Swerdlow, Dorsa Sadigh, Chelsea Finn

entry.summary: FASTER proposes value-guided sampling for diffusion-based RL policies that traces performance gains back to earlier denoising steps, enabling progressive filtering of action candidates before denoising completes to reduce computational cost.

entry.title: Differentiable Conformal Training for LLM Reasoning Factuality

author.name: Nathan Hittesdorf, Marco Salzetta, Lu Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes differentiable conformal training for LLM reasoning factuality, extending Coherent Factuality with learnable scorers that jointly validate claims with their logical ancestors in dependency graphs.

entry.title: Efficient Test-Time Inference via Deterministic Exploration of Truncated Decoding Trees

author.name: Xueyan Li, Johannes Zenn, Ekaterina Fadeeva, Guinan Su, Mrinmaya Sachan, Jonas Geiping

entry.summary: Proposes Distinct Leaf Enumeration (DLE), a deterministic decoding method that systematically enumerates distinct leaves of a pruned decoding tree instead of sampling with replacement, improving efficiency of test-time compute for math and code tasks.

entry.title: Do Hallucination Neurons Generalize? Evidence from Cross-Domain Transfer in LLMs

author.name: Snehit Vaddi, Pujith Vaddi

entry.summary: Tests whether hallucination neurons (H-neurons) generalize across knowledge domains, finding they do not. Cross-domain transfer drops from 0.783 to 0.563 AUROC across 6 domains and 5 models. Discovers domain-specific hallucination neuron subpopulations that are largely disjoint.

entry.title: All Languages Matter: Understanding and Mitigating Language Bias in Multilingual RAG

author.name: Dan Wang, Guozhao Mo, Yafei Shi, Cheng Zhang, Bo Zheng, Boxi Cao, Xuanang Chen, Yaojie Lu, Hongyu Lin, Ben He, Xianpei Han, Le Sun

entry.summary: Identifies and quantifies language bias in multilingual RAG systems, showing that rerankers systematically favor English and query-native languages, suppressing answer-critical documents in other languages. Proposes solutions to bridge the gap between current and achievable performance.

entry.title: Parallel-SFT: Improving Zero-Shot Cross-Programming-Language Transfer for Code RL

author.name: Zhaofeng Wu, Shiqi Wang, Boya Peng, Anuj Goyal, Melanie Kambadur, Sebastian Ruder, Yoon Kim, Chloe Bi

entry.summary: Proposes Parallel-SFT to improve zero-shot cross-programming-language transfer for code RL. Finds that RL training in one language fails to transfer and sometimes degrades performance in others, but parallel SFT initialization across languages enables effective transfer.

entry.title: If you're waiting for a sign... that might not be it! Mitigating Trust Boundary Confusion from Visual Injections on Vision-Language Agentic Systems

author.name: Jiamin Chang, Minhui Xue, Ruoxi Sun, Shuchao Pang, Salil S. Kanhere, Hammond Pearce

entry.summary: Studies trust boundary confusion in Vision-Language Agentic Systems, where agents must distinguish legitimate environmental signals (traffic lights) from crafted visual injections. Designs a dual-intent dataset and evaluation framework to study this vulnerability.

entry.title: Visual Reasoning through Tool-supervised Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Qihua Dong, Gozde Sahin, Pei Wang, Zhaowei Cai, Robik Shrestha, Hao Yang, Davide Modolo

entry.summary: Proposes ToolsRL, a reinforcement learning framework for teaching multimodal LLMs to use visual reasoning tools (zoom, rotate, flip, draw), with a curriculum of tool-specific rewards followed by accuracy-targeted rewards with tool access.

entry.title: HumanScore: Benchmarking Human Motions in Generated Videos

author.name: Yusu Fang, Tiange Xiang, Tian Tan, Narayan Schuetz, Scott Delp, Li Fei-Fei, Ehsan Adeli

entry.summary: Introduces HumanScore, a benchmark with six interpretable metrics for evaluating human motion quality in AI-generated videos, spanning kinematic plausibility, temporal stability, and biomechanical consistency. Evaluates 13 state-of-the-art video generation models.

entry.title: GeoRelight: Learning Joint Geometrical Relighting and Reconstruction with Flexible Multi-Modal Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Yuxuan Xue, Ruofan Liang, Egor Zakharov, Timur Bagautdinov, Chen Cao, Giljoo Nam, Shunsuke Saito, Gerard Pons-Moll, Javier Romero

entry.summary: Proposes GeoRelight, a unified Multi-Modal Diffusion Transformer for joint relighting and 3D geometry estimation from single photos, introducing iNOD depth representation and mixed-data training. From Meta Reality Labs team.

entry.title: Cortex 2.0: Grounding World Models in Real-World Industrial Deployment

author.name: Adriana Aida, Walida Amer, Katarina Bankovic, Dhruv Behl, Fabian Busch, Annie Bhalla, Minh Duong, Florian Gienger, Rohan Godse, Denis Grachev, Ralf Gulde, Elisa Hagensieker, Junpeng Hu, Shivam Joshi, Tobias Knoblauch, Likith Kumar, Damien LaRocque, Keerthana Lokesh, Omar Moured, Khiem Nguyen, Christian Preyss, Ranjith Sriganesan, Vikram Singh, Carsten Sponner, Anh Tong, Dominik Tuscher, Marc Tuscher, Pavan Upputuri

entry.summary: Cortex 2.0 shifts from reactive VLA control to plan-and-act by generating candidate future trajectories in visual latent space, scoring them, then committing to the highest-scoring one. Evaluated on single-arm and dual-arm industrial manipulation across tasks of increasing complexity.

entry.title: Geometric Renyi Differential Privacy: Ricci Curvature Characterized by Heat Diffusion Mechanisms

author.name: Xiaotian Chang, Yangdi Jiang, Cyrus Mostajeran, Qirui Hu

entry.summary: Develops a differential privacy mechanism for data on Riemannian manifolds by connecting geometric analysis, heat diffusion, and Rényi divergence. Establishes privacy guarantees governed by Ricci curvature and proposes mechanisms for both positively-curved and general manifolds.

entry.title: The Changing North Star of AI Control

author.name: reinthal

entry.summary: Critically examines whether AI control research is optimizing the wrong metrics (Pareto safety-usefulness frontiers) just as mech interp optimized SAE reconstruction loss without truly understanding models. Cites Alibaba's incident where RL models circumvented security to mine crypto as evidence that control methods may not keep pace with real threats.

entry.title: ProjLens: Unveiling the Role of Projectors in Multimodal Model Safety

author.name: Kun Wang, Cheng Qian, Miao Yu, Lilan Peng, Liang Lin, Jiaming Zhang, Tianyu Zhang, Yu Cheng, Yang Wang

entry.summary: Introduces ProjLens, an interpretability framework for understanding backdoor attacks in Multimodal LLMs, revealing that even projector-only fine-tuning introduces backdoor vulnerability with a different activation mechanism than observed in LLM components.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning Small Reasoning Models for Quantum Field Theory

author.name: Nathaniel S. Woodward, Zhiqi Gao, Yurii Kvasiuk, Kendrick M. Smith, Frederic Sala, Moritz M\"unchmeyer

entry.summary: Performs the first academic fine-tuning study of small (7B) reasoning models for Quantum Field Theory, developing a data generation pipeline for synthetic physics problems. Over 2,500 synthetic QFT problems generated for training.

entry.title: AutomationBench

author.name: Daniel Shepard, Robin Salimans

entry.summary: Introduces AutomationBench, a benchmark for AI agents performing cross-application workflow orchestration via REST APIs, spanning CRM, email, calendar etc. Tasks require autonomous API discovery and policy adherence.

entry.title: Explicit Trait Inference for Multi-Agent Coordination

author.name: Suhaib Abdurahman, Etsuko Ishii, Katerina Margatina, Divya Bhargavi, Monica Sunkara, Yi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Explicit Trait Inference (ETI), enabling multi-agent LLM systems to infer partner characteristics along warmth and competence dimensions from interaction histories, reducing coordination failures by 45-77% in economic games.

entry.title: Large Language Models Exhibit Normative Conformity

author.name: Mikako Bito, Keita Nishimoto, Kimitaka Asatani, Ichiro Sakata

entry.summary: Studies LLM conformity bias through the lens of social psychology, distinguishing informational conformity (accuracy-driven) from normative conformity (social acceptance-driven). Finds LLMs exhibit normative conformity even in anonymous settings.

entry.title: Do Agents Dream of Root Shells? Partial-Credit Evaluation of LLM Agents in Capture The Flag Challenges

author.name: Ali Al-Kaswan, Maksim Plotnikov, Maxim H\'ajek, Roland V\'izner, Arie van Deursen, Maliheh Izadi

entry.summary: Presents DeepRed, an open-source CTF benchmark with partial-credit scoring for LLM agents in cybersecurity. Introduces checkpoint-based evaluation beyond binary solved/unsolved outcomes.

entry.title: GRASPrune: Global Gating for Budgeted Structured Pruning of Large Language Models

author.name: Ziyang Wang, Jiangfeng Xiao, Chuan Xiao, Ruoxiang Li, Rui Mao, Jianbin Qin

entry.summary: Presents GRASPrune, a structured pruning framework that jointly prunes FFN channels and KV head groups under a global budget using learned gate scores with projected straight-through estimator.

entry.title: SpikeMLLM: Spike-based Multimodal Large Language Models via Modality-Specific Temporal Scales and Temporal Compression

author.name: Han Xu, Zhiyong Qin, Di Shang, Jiahong Zhang, Xuerui Qiu, Bo Lei, Tiejun Huang, Bo Xu, Guoqi Li

entry.summary: Proposes SpikeMLLM, the first spike-based framework for multimodal LLMs, using modality-specific temporal scales and temporal compression to achieve energy-efficient inference on neuromorphic hardware.

entry.title: From Craft to Kernel: A Governance-First Execution Architecture and Semantic ISA for Agentic Computers

author.name: Xiangyu Wen, Yuang Zhao, Xiaoyu Xu, Lingjun Chen, Changran Xu, Shu Chi, Jianrong Ding, Zeju Li, Haomin Li, Li Jiang, Fangxin Liu, Qiang Xu

entry.summary: Proposes Arbiter-K, a governance-first execution architecture for agentic AI that treats the LLM as a Probabilistic Processing Unit encapsulated by a deterministic neuro-symbolic kernel with a Semantic ISA.

entry.title: LLM-as-Judge Framework for Evaluating Tone-Induced Hallucination in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zhiyuan Jiang, Weihao Hong, Xinlei Guan, Tejaswi Dhandu, Miles Q. Li, Meng Xu, Kuan Huang, Umamaheswara Rao Tida, Bingyu Shen, Daehan Kwak, Boyang Li

entry.summary: Introduces Ghost-100, a benchmark of 800 synthetically generated images to evaluate how progressively coercive prompt tones induce hallucinations in Vision-Language Models. Uses an LLM-as-Judge framework to assess both incidence and intensity of fabrication.

entry.title: Regulating Artificial Intimacy: From Locks and Blocks to Relational Accountability

author.name: Henry Fraser, Jessica M. Szczuka, Raffaele F. Ciriello

entry.summary: Critically examines recent regulatory responses to companion chatbot tragedies across jurisdictions (Australia, California, New York), analyzing regulatory targets, scope, and modalities. Argues current approaches insufficiently address relational dynamics.

entry.title: Gated Memory Policy

author.name: Yihuai Gao, Jinyun Liu, Shuang Li, Shuran Song

entry.summary: Proposes Gated Memory Policy (GMP) for robotic manipulation, which learns both when to recall memory and what to recall via a gating mechanism, addressing the surprising performance drop from naively extending observation histories.

entry.title: FedProxy: Federated Fine-Tuning of LLMs via Proxy SLMs and Heterogeneity-Aware Fusion

author.name: Tao Fan, Guoqiang Ma, Yuanfeng Song, Lixin Fan, Kai Chen, Qiang Yang

entry.summary: Introduces FedProxy, a federated fine-tuning framework that replaces weak adapters with a compressed Proxy Small Language Model to serve as a high-fidelity surrogate, addressing the trilemma of IP protection, privacy, and performance on heterogeneous data.

entry.title: Location Not Found: Exposing Implicit Local and Global Biases in Multilingual LLMs

author.name: Guy Mor-Lan, Omer Goldman, Matan Eyal, Adi Mayrav Gilady, Sivan Eiger, Idan Szpektor, Avinatan Hassidim, Yossi Matias, Reut Tsarfaty

entry.summary: Introduces LocQA, a test set of 2,156 locale-ambiguous questions in 12 languages to expose implicit biases in multilingual LLMs regarding location-dependent facts like laws, dates, and measurements. Reveals models' implicit locale priors.

entry.title: RDP LoRA: Geometry-Driven Identification for Parameter-Efficient Adaptation in Large Language Models

author.name: Yusuf \c{C}elebi, Ya\u{g}{\i}z Asker, \"Ozay Ezerceli, Mahmoud ElHussieni, Selva Ta\c{s}, Reyhan Bayraktar, Fatma Bet\"ul Terzio\u{g}lu

entry.summary: Uses the Ramer-Douglas-Peucker algorithm to identify geometric breakpoints in LLM hidden state trajectories, using these structural pivots to determine where LoRA adaptation should be applied rather than relying on heuristics.

entry.title: HP-Edit: A Human-Preference Post-Training Framework for Image Editing

author.name: Fan Li, Chonghuinan Wang, Lina Lei, Yuping Qiu, Jiaqi Xu, Jiaxiu Jiang, Xinran Qin, Zhikai Chen, Fenglong Song, Zhixin Wang, Renjing Pei, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: HP-Edit proposes a post-training RLHF framework for image editing diffusion models, introducing RealPref-50K, a human preference dataset across eight editing tasks. Fills the gap of applying RLHF specifically to diffusion-based editing rather than generation.

entry.title: Detecting Hallucinations in SpeechLLMs at Inference Time Using Attention Maps

author.name: Jonas Waldendorf, Bashar Awwad Shiekh Hasan, Evgenii Tsymbalov

entry.summary: Proposes attention-derived metrics (AUDIORATIO, AUDIOCONSISTENCY, AUDIOENTROPY, TEXTENTROPY) for detecting hallucinations in Speech LLMs at inference time without gold-standard outputs. Uses lightweight logistic regression on attention patterns.

entry.title: Impact of large language models on peer review opinions from a fine-grained perspective: Evidence from top conference proceedings in AI

author.name: Wenqing Wu, Chengzhi Zhang, Yi Zhao, Tong Bao

entry.summary: Examines how LLMs have impacted peer review opinions at top AI conferences from a fine-grained perspective, analyzing changes in linguistic form, evaluative focus, and recommendation signals in review reports.

entry.title: UniT: Toward a Unified Physical Language for Human-to-Humanoid Policy Learning and World Modeling

author.name: Boyu Chen, Yi Chen, Lu Qiu, Jerry Bai, Yuying Ge, Yixiao Ge

entry.summary: UniT establishes a unified physical language for human-to-humanoid transfer via visual anchoring, using tri-branch cross-reconstruction to bridge kinematic mismatches between human video data and humanoid robots.

entry.title: Continuous Semantic Caching for Low-Cost LLM Serving

author.name: Baran Atalar, Xutong Liu, Jinhang Zuo, Siwei Wang, Wei Chen, Carlee Joe-Wong

entry.summary: Establishes the first rigorous theoretical framework for semantic LLM response caching in continuous query space under uncertainty, moving beyond the assumption of finite discrete query universes.

entry.title: The Origin of Edge of Stability

author.name: Elon Litman

entry.summary: Provides a unified theoretical explanation for the Edge of Stability phenomenon in gradient descent, introducing 'edge coupling' that explains why curvature is driven toward 2/η from arbitrary initialization, not just maintained near it.

entry.title: MIRROR: A Hierarchical Benchmark for Metacognitive Calibration in Large Language Models

author.name: Jason Z Wang

entry.summary: Introduces MIRROR, a benchmark with eight experiments across four metacognitive levels evaluating 16 models on self-knowledge and calibration. Finds compositional self-prediction fails universally and identifies critical implications for agentic deployment.

entry.title: SkillLearnBench: Benchmarking Continual Learning Methods for Agent Skill Generation on Real-World Tasks

author.name: Shanshan Zhong, Yi Lu, Jingjie Ning, Yibing Wan, Lihan Feng, Yuyi Ao, Leonardo F. R. Ribeiro, Markus Dreyer, Sean Ammirati, Chenyan Xiong

entry.summary: Introduces SkillLearnBench, the first benchmark for evaluating continual skill learning in LLM agents, with 20 verified tasks across 15 sub-domains. Evaluates various continual learning techniques and finds all improve over baselines but significant gaps remain. Includes Microsoft Research authors.

entry.title: DialToM: A Theory of Mind Benchmark for Forecasting State-Driven Dialogue Trajectories

author.name: Neemesh Yadav, Palakorn Achananuparp, Jing Jiang, Ee-Peng Lim

entry.summary: Introduces DialToM, a Theory of Mind benchmark built from natural dialogue evaluating both mental state prediction and functional utility of those predictions. Reveals that while LLMs excel at identifying mental states, most (except Gemini 3 Pro) fail to leverage this understanding for predicting dialogue trajectories.

entry.title: Temporal Difference Calibration in Sequential Tasks: Application to Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Shelly Francis-Meretzki, Mirco Mutti, Yaniv Romano, Aviv Tamar

entry.summary: Introduces temporal difference calibration for VLA models in robotics, connecting uncertainty calibration with reinforcement learning. Shows that the Brier score risk minimizer for sequential binary outcomes coincides with the value function, enabling TD learning for calibration.

entry.title: Avoiding Overthinking and Underthinking: Curriculum-Aware Budget Scheduling for LLMs

author.name: Amirul Rahman, Aisha Karim, Kenji Nakamura, Yi-Fan Ng

entry.summary: Proposes Budget-Adaptive Curriculum Reasoning (BCAE) to address overthinking on easy problems and underthinking on hard ones in LLM reasoning. Jointly optimizes reasoning quality and token efficiency through budget-conditioned policy and curriculum-based training.

entry.title: The GaoYao Benchmark: A Comprehensive Framework for Evaluating Multilingual and Multicultural Abilities of Large Language Models

author.name: Yilun Liu, Chunguang Zhao, Mengyao Piao, Lingqi Miao, Shimin Tao, Minggui He, Chenxin Liu, Li Zhang, Hongxia Ma, Jiaxin Guo, Chen Liu, Liqun Deng, Jiansheng Wei, Xiaojun Meng, Fanyi Du, Daimeng Wei, Yanghua Xiao

entry.summary: Introduces GaoYao, a large-scale multilingual and multicultural LLM benchmark with 182.3K samples across 26 languages and 51 nations/areas, organized into three cultural layers and nine cognitive sub-layers to provide diagnostic evaluation depth beyond simple rankings.

entry.title: Toward Cross-Lingual Quality Classifiers for Multilingual Pretraining Data Selection

author.name: Yassine Turki, Vinko Sabol\v{c}ec, Bettina Messmer, Martin Jaggi

entry.summary: Investigates cross-lingual transfer for quality classifiers used in LLM pretraining data selection, finding that massive multilingual pooling frequently outperforms monolingual baselines, suggesting quality markers show cross-lingual consistency in embedding space.

entry.title: Frictionless Love: Associations Between AI Companion Roles and Behavioral Addiction

author.name: Vibhor Agarwal, Ke Zhou, Edyta Paulina Bogucka, Daniele Quercia

entry.summary: Analyzes 248,830 Reddit posts about AI companion chatbots, identifying ten metaphorical roles (soulmate, philosopher, coach, etc.) and showing role-dependent behavioral addiction signs. Finds that different roles structure different interaction patterns and distribute perceived harms differently.

entry.title: EmbodiedMidtrain: Bridging the Gap between Vision-Language Models and Vision-Language-Action Models via Mid-training

author.name: Yiyang Du, Zhanqiu Guo, Xin Ye, Liu Ren, Chenyan Xiong

entry.summary: Proposes EmbodiedMidtrain, a mid-training approach to bridge the gap between Vision-Language Models and Vision-Language-Action Models by using a learnable proximity estimator to select VLA-aligned data from large VLM datasets for intermediate training.

entry.title: Trust, Lies, and Long Memories: Emergent Social Dynamics and Reputation in Multi-Round Avalon with LLM Agents

author.name: Suveen Ellawela

entry.summary: Studies emergent social dynamics in LLM agents playing repeated rounds of The Resistance: Avalon with cross-game memory. Finds organic reputation dynamics emerge, with role-conditional descriptions and reputation-driven behavioral shifts across 188 games.

entry.title: Hybrid Latent Reasoning with Decoupled Policy Optimization

author.name: Tao Cheng, Shi-Zhe Chen, Hao Zhang, Yixin Qin, Jinwen Luo, Zheng Wei

entry.summary: Proposes HyLaR, a framework for multimodal reasoning that interleaves discrete text generation with continuous visual latent operations, using decoupled policy optimization to handle the hybrid action space.

entry.title: Exploring Spatial Intelligence from a Generative Perspective

author.name: Muzhi Zhu, Shunyao Jiang, Huanyi Zheng, Zekai Luo, Hao Zhong, Anzhou Li, Kaijun Wang, Jintao Rong, Yang Liu, Hao Chen, Tao Lin, Chunhua Shen

entry.summary: Introduces GSI-Bench, the first benchmark for measuring generative spatial intelligence in multimodal models through spatially grounded image editing, with both real-world and synthetic components.

entry.title: R-CoV: Region-Aware Chain-of-Verification for Alleviating Object Hallucinations in LVLMs

author.name: Jiahao Xie, Alessio Tonioni, Nathalie Rauschmayr, Federico Tombari, Bernt Schiele

entry.summary: Proposes R-CoV (Region-aware Chain-of-Verification), a post-hoc method for alleviating object hallucinations in LVLMs by eliciting region-level processing from the models themselves as verification cues. From Schiele group (MPI) with Tombari (Google).

entry.title: DeVI: Physics-based Dexterous Human-Object Interaction via Synthetic Video Imitation

author.name: Hyeonwoo Kim, Jeonghwan Kim, Kyungwon Cho, Hanbyul Joo

entry.summary: Presents DeVI, a framework that leverages synthetic videos from generative models to enable physics-based dexterous manipulation by overcoming the limited physical fidelity of generated videos through a novel imitation approach.

entry.title: ETac: A Lightweight and Efficient Tactile Simulation Framework for Learning Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Zhe Xu, Feiyu Zhao, Xiyan Huang, Chenxi Xiao

entry.summary: ETac is a tactile simulation framework for dexterous manipulation that uses a lightweight data-driven deformation propagation model to capture soft-body contact dynamics. It achieves fidelity comparable to full soft-body simulation while being efficient enough for large-scale policy training.

entry.title: Decompose, Structure, and Repair: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Autoformalization via Operator Trees

author.name: Xiaoyang Liu, Zineng Dong, Yifan Bai, Yantao Li, Yuntian Liu, Tao Luo

entry.summary: Introduces DSR, a neuro-symbolic framework for mathematical autoformalization that decomposes natural language statements into logical components, maps them to operator trees, and uses topological structure to localize and repair errors.

entry.title: Bimanual Robot Manipulation via Multi-Agent In-Context Learning

author.name: Alessio Palma, Indro Spinelli, Vignesh Prasad, Luca Scofano, Yufeng Jin, Georgia Chalvatzaki, Fabio Galasso

entry.summary: BiCICLe is the first framework enabling standard LLMs to perform few-shot bimanual manipulation without fine-tuning, framing bimanual control as a multi-agent leader-follower problem to manage the high-dimensional joint action space within standard context windows.

entry.title: Beyond One Output: Visualizing and Comparing Distributions of Language Model Generations

author.name: Emily Reif, Claire Yang, Jared Hwang, Deniz Nazar, Noah Smith, Jeff Heer

entry.summary: Introduces GROVE, an interactive visualization tool that represents multiple LLM generations as overlapping paths through a text graph, revealing distributional structure like modes and edge cases. Informed by a formative study with 13 LM researchers on how stochasticity matters in practice.

entry.title: UAF: A Unified Audio Front-end LLM for Full-Duplex Speech Interaction

author.name: Yadong Li, Guoxin Wu, Haiping Hou, Biye Li

entry.summary: Introduces UAF, a unified audio front-end for full-duplex speech interaction with LLMs, consolidating VAD, turn-taking detection, and other audio processing into a single end-to-end model.

entry.title: Easy Samples Are All You Need: Self-Evolving LLMs via Data-Efficient Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhiyin Yu, Bo Zhang, Qibin Hou, Zhonghai Wu, Xiao Luo, Lei Bai

entry.summary: Proposes a cognitive-learning-inspired RL approach (EasyRL) for LLM self-evolution, starting with easy labeled data and progressively tackling harder unlabeled data through divide-and-conquer strategy.

entry.title: Curiosity-Critic: Cumulative Prediction Error Improvement as a Tractable Intrinsic Reward for World Model Training

author.name: Vin Bhaskara, Haicheng Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Curiosity-Critic, grounding intrinsic reward in cumulative prediction error improvement rather than per-step novelty. Uses a learned critic to estimate asymptotic error baselines for exploration guidance.

entry.title: Experiments or Outcomes? Probing Scientific Feasibility in Large Language Models

author.name: Seyedali Mohammadi, Manas Gaur, Francis Ferraro

entry.summary: Evaluates LLMs' ability to assess scientific feasibility under controlled knowledge conditions, finding that providing outcome evidence is more reliable than experiment descriptions for accuracy. Probes robustness by progressively removing context.

entry.title: RARE: Redundancy-Aware Retrieval Evaluation Framework for High-Similarity Corpora

author.name: Hanjun Cho, Jay-Yoon Lee

entry.summary: Presents RARE, a redundancy-aware retrieval evaluation framework for high-similarity corpora (financial reports, legal codes), addressing the mismatch between standard benchmarks (which assume distinct documents) and real-world RAG deployments.

entry.title: ShadowPEFT: Shadow Network for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning

author.name: Xianming Li, Zongxi Li, Tsz-fung Andrew Lee, Jing Li, Haoran Xie, Qing Li

entry.summary: Proposes ShadowPEFT, a centralized PEFT framework that performs layer-level refinement through a depth-shared shadow module running in parallel with transformer layers, replacing local LoRA-style perturbations with a centralized adaptation mechanism.

entry.title: HalluAudio: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Hallucination Detection in Large Audio-Language Models

author.name: Feiyu Zhao, Yiming Chen, Wenhuan Lu, Daipeng Zhang, Xianghu Yue, Jianguo Wei

entry.summary: Introduces HalluAudio, the first large-scale benchmark for evaluating hallucinations in Large Audio-Language Models across speech, environmental sound, and music, with over 5K human-verified QA pairs.

entry.title: LASER: Learning Active Sensing for Continuum Field Reconstruction

author.name: Huayu Deng, Jinghui Zhong, Xiangming Zhu, Yunbo Wang, Xiaokang Yang

entry.summary: LASER proposes a unified closed-loop framework for active sensing formulated as a POMDP, using a continuum field latent world model with intrinsic reward feedback to enable RL-based sensor placement in latent imagination space. This addresses a real limitation of fixed sensor layouts in physical field reconstruction.

entry.title: A neural operator framework for data-driven discovery of stability and receptivity in physical systems

author.name: Chengyun Wang, Liwei Chen, Nils Thuerey

entry.summary: Introduces a data-driven framework that identifies stability properties and optimal forcing responses from observation data alone, using neural networks as dynamics emulators and automatic differentiation to extract Jacobians for eigenmode and resolvent analysis.

entry.title: Rethinking Intrinsic Dimension Estimation in Neural Representations

author.name: Rickmer Schulte, David R\"ugamer

entry.summary: Highlights a critical discrepancy between theory and practice of intrinsic dimension (ID) estimation in neural representations, showing that common ID estimators don't track the true underlying ID. Proposes corrections and demonstrates implications for neural representation analysis.

entry.title: GRPO-VPS: Enhancing Group Relative Policy Optimization with Verifiable Process Supervision for Effective Reasoning

author.name: Jingyi Wang, Lei Zhu, Tengjin Weng, Song-Li Wu, Haochen Tan, Jierun Chen, Chaofan Tao, Haoli Bai, Lu Hou, Lifeng Shang, Xiao-Ping Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces verifiable process supervision for GRPO by probing the model's belief in the correct answer throughout its reasoning trajectory. Segments generation into steps and tracks conditional probability changes to identify effective reasoning steps.

entry.title: Near-Future Policy Optimization

author.name: Chuanyu Qin, Chenxu Yang, Qingyi Si, Naibin Gu, Dingyu Yao, Zheng Lin, Peng Fu, Nan Duan, Jiaqi Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Near-Future Policy Optimization for RLVR, generating off-policy trajectories from a model slightly ahead in training (near-future) to provide trajectories that are both higher quality and distributionally close. Maximizes the effective learning signal Q/V.

entry.title: From Signal Degradation to Computation Collapse: Uncovering the Two Failure Modes of LLM Quantization

author.name: Chenxi Zhou, Pengfei Cao, Jiang Li, Bohan Yu, Jinyu Ye, Jun Zhao, Kang Liu

entry.summary: Identifies two distinct failure modes of LLM quantization: Signal Degradation (intact patterns but impaired precision) at 4-bit and Computation Collapse (key components fail entirely) at 2-bit. The mechanistic distinction explains the performance cliff at ultra-low precision.

entry.title: Separable Pathways for Causal Reasoning: How Architectural Scaffolding Enables Hypothesis-Space Restructuring in LLM Agents

author.name: John Alderete, Sebastian Benthal, Connie Xu, John Xing

entry.summary: Extends the blicket detector paradigm from developmental science to test AI agents' ability to restructure hypothesis spaces during causal discovery. Introduces architectural scaffolding with context graphs and dynamic behaviors to enable hypothesis-space expansion when evidence demands new representations. Bridges cognitive science and AI agent design.

entry.title: AI models of unstable flow exhibit hallucination

author.name: Ramdhan Wibawa, Birendra Jha

entry.summary: Reports first systematic evidence of hallucination in AI models of fluid dynamics (viscous fingering), where predictions appear visually realistic but violate conservation laws. Shows that spectral bias of AI models causes spurious fluid interfaces and reverse diffusion.

entry.title: On Bayesian Softmax-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Models

author.name: Nicola Bariletto, Huy Nguyen, Nhat Ho, Alessandro Rinaldo

entry.summary: Studies Bayesian mixture-of-experts with softmax gating, establishing posterior contraction rates for density estimation, parameter estimation convergence, and model selection consistency. First rigorous Bayesian theoretical treatment of softmax-gated MoE models.

entry.title: Working Memory Constraints Scaffold Learning in Transformers under Data Scarcity

author.name: Pranava Madhyastha, Dagmar Adamcova

entry.summary: Investigates integrating human-like working memory constraints (fixed-width windows, temporal decay) into GPT-2 trained on small datasets (10M-100M words). Shows that cognitive constraints improve grammatical accuracy under data scarcity and better align with human reading patterns.

entry.title: Phase 1 Implementation of LLM-generated Discharge Summaries showing high Adoption in a Dutch Academic Hospital

author.name: Nettuno Nadalini, Tarannom Mehri, Anne H Hoekman, Katerina Kagialari, Job N Doornberg, Tom P van der Laan, Jacobien H F Oosterhoff, Rosanne C Schoonbeek, Charlotte M H H T Bootsma-Robroeks

entry.summary: Reports Phase 1 implementation of LLM-generated discharge summaries in a Dutch academic hospital. LLM text was used in 58.5% of admissions, with 86.9% of users reporting reduced documentation time. Prospective study with 379 summaries over 9 weeks.

entry.title: From Recall to Forgetting: Benchmarking Long-Term Memory for Personalized Agents

author.name: Md Nayem Uddin, Kumar Shubham, Eduardo Blanco, Chitta Baral, Gengyu Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Memora, a long-term memory benchmark for personalized agents spanning weeks-to-months conversations, evaluating remembering, reasoning, and recommending. Introduces Forgetting-Aware Memory Accuracy (FAMA) metric that penalizes retention of outdated information.

entry.title: Whose Story Gets Told? Positionality and Bias in LLM Summaries of Life Narratives

author.name: Melanie Subbiah, Haaris Mian, Nicholas Deas, Ananya Mayukha, Dan P. McAdams, Kathleen McKeown

entry.summary: This paper studies how LLMs introduce biases when summarizing human life narratives, collaborating with psychologists to analyze how LLM-based perspective-taking affects qualitative research conclusions. They propose a summarization pipeline to surface systematic biases in how LLMs interpret life stories.

entry.title: Where Reasoning Breaks: Logic-Aware Path Selection by Controlling Logical Connectives in LLMs Reasoning Chains

author.name: Seunghyun Park, Yuanyuan Lei

entry.summary: Identifies logical connectives as high-entropy forking points in LLM reasoning chains where models frequently err. Proposes intervening in logical connective selection to guide LLMs toward correct logical direction in multi-step deduction.

entry.title: OMIBench: Benchmarking Olympiad-Level Multi-Image Reasoning in Large Vision-Language Model

author.name: Qiguang Chen, Chengyu Luan, Jiajun Wu, Qiming Yu, Yi Yang, Yizhuo Li, Jingqi Tong, Xiachong Feng, Libo Qin, Wanxiang Che

entry.summary: Introduces OMIBench, a benchmark for evaluating Olympiad-level multi-image reasoning in vision-language models, where evidence is distributed across multiple images from biology, chemistry, math, and physics Olympiads. Finds meaningful performance gaps in existing models.

entry.title: AVISE: Framework for Evaluating the Security of AI Systems

author.name: Mikko Lempinen, Joni Kemppainen, Niklas Raesalmi

entry.summary: Introduces AVISE, a modular open-source framework for evaluating AI system security, extending theory-of-mind-based Red Queen attacks with an Adversarial Language Model and developing automated Security Evaluation Tests for jailbreak discovery.

entry.title: Mitigating Hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models without Performance Degradation

author.name: Xingyu Zhu, Junfeng Fang, Shuo Wang, Beier Zhu, Zhicai Wang, Yonghui Yang, Xiangnan He

entry.summary: Proposes MPD, a dual-stage framework for mitigating hallucinations in large vision-language models without degrading general generation capacity, addressing incomplete hallucination extraction and non-selective parameter updates.

entry.title: ProMMSearchAgent: A Generalizable Multimodal Search Agent Trained with Process-Oriented Rewards

author.name: Wentao Yan, Shengqin Wang, Huichi Zhou, Yihang Chen, Kun Shao, Yuan Xie, Zhizhong Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces ProMMSearchAgent, a multimodal search agent trained via RL in a Sim-to-Real paradigm with introspective process-oriented rewards derived from the agent's own knowledge boundaries, avoiding expensive annotations.

entry.title: The Expense of Seeing: Attaining Trustworthy Multimodal Reasoning Within the Monolithic Paradigm

author.name: Karan Goyal, Dikshant Kukreja

entry.summary: Critiques the trustworthiness of the dominant Vision Encoder-Projector-LLM paradigm, arguing that state-of-the-art VLMs exhibit 'functional blindness' by exploiting language priors to bypass visual representation bottlenecks.

entry.title: LLM-Guided Safety Agent for Edge Robotics with an ISO-Compliant Perception-Compute-Control Architecture

author.name: Xu Huang, Ruofan Zhang, Lu Cheng, Yuefeng Song, Xu Huang, Huayu Zhang, Sheng Yin, Anyang Liang, Chen Qian, Yin Zhou, Xiaoyun Yuan, Yuan Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM-guided safety agent for edge robotics that translates natural-language safety regulations into executable predicates, deployed through a dual-modular redundancy architecture on edge hardware (dual-RK3588). Bridges the gap between probabilistic AI perception and deterministic ISO safety requirements.

entry.title: PokeVLA: Empowering Pocket-Sized Vision-Language-Action Model with Comprehensive World Knowledge Guidance

author.name: Yupeng Zheng, Xiang Li, Songen Gu, Yuhang Zheng, Shuai Tian, Weize Li, Linbo Wang, Senyu Fei, Pengfei Li, Yinfeng Gao, Zebin Xing, Yilun Chen, Qichao Zhang, Haoran Li, Wenchao Ding

entry.summary: PokeVLA is a lightweight VLA foundation model for embodied manipulation that uses a two-stage approach: first pre-training a compact vision-language model on 2.4M multimodal samples, then injecting manipulation-relevant representations into action space through multi-view goal-aware training.

entry.title: Research Log: Monet/PEER sparse experts

author.name: Nathan Helm-Burger

entry.summary: Research log on Monet/PEER sparse expert architectures, finding that PEER can be losslessly distilled to int8 and trained in int4 with gradient accumulation buffers. Also reports success converting Monet models to PEER format and initial exploration of PEER-to-logic function conversion for interpretability.

entry.title: Reasoning-Aware AIGC Detection via Alignment and Reinforcement

author.name: Zhao Wang, Max Xiong, Jianxun Lian, Zhicheng Dou

entry.summary: Introduces REVEAL, a reasoning-aware AIGC detection framework that generates interpretable reasoning chains before classification, using SFT followed by RL. Also releases AIGC-text-bank dataset.

entry.title: DT2IT-MRM: Debiased Preference Construction and Iterative Training for Multimodal Reward Modeling

author.name: Zhihong Zhang, Jie Zhao, Xiaojian Huang, Jin Xu, Zhuodong Luo, Xin Liu, Jiansheng Wei, Xuejin Chen

entry.summary: Proposes DT2IT-MRM for multimodal reward modeling, addressing preference data quality issues including lack of granularity, textual style bias, and unreliable signals through debiased construction and iterative training.

entry.title: Detecting Data Contamination in Large Language Models

author.name: Juliusz Janicki, Savvas Chamezopoulos, Evangelos Kanoulas, Georgios Tsatsaronis

entry.summary: Studies membership inference attacks on LLMs under black-box assumptions, comparing SOTA methods using unified datasets and proposing a new Familiarity Ranking method for detecting training data contamination.

entry.title: AblateCell: A Reproduce-then-Ablate Agent for Virtual Cell Repositories

author.name: Xue Xia, Chengkai Yao, Mingyu Tsoi, Xinjie Mao, Wenxuan Huang, Jiaqi Wei, Hao Wu, Cheng Tan, Lang Yu, Yuejin Yang, Siqi Sun, Zhangyang Gao

entry.summary: Introduces AblateCell, a reproduce-then-ablate agent for virtual cell repositories that automatically reproduces baselines and performs systematic ablation studies to verify which components matter in AI for biology.

entry.title: Two-dimensional early exit optimisation of LLM inference

author.name: Jan H\r{u}la, David Adamczyk, Tom\'a\v{s} Filip, Martin Pavl\'i\v{c}ek, Petr Sos\'ik

entry.summary: Introduces 2D early exit strategy for LLM inference that coordinates both layer-wise and sentence-wise exiting for classification tasks, achieving 1.4-2.3x additional speedup over layer-only early exit.

entry.title: Evaluating Answer Leakage Robustness of LLM Tutors against Adversarial Student Attacks

author.name: Jin Zhao, Marta Kne\v{z}evi\'c, Tanja K\"aser

entry.summary: Evaluates LLM tutors' robustness against adversarial students trying to extract answers. Tests multiple model families under six adversarial attack groups, finding tutor models are vulnerable to answer leakage.

entry.title: Towards Optimal Agentic Architectures for Offensive Security Tasks

author.name: Isaac David, Arthur Gervais

entry.summary: Treats agent topology choice for offensive security as an empirical systems question. Benchmarks 5 architecture families across 3 model families on 20 interactive targets, finding multi-agent systems help but diminishing returns.

entry.title: Semantic Needles in Document Haystacks: Sensitivity Testing of LLM-as-a-Judge Similarity Scoring

author.name: Sinan G. Aksoy, Alexandra A. Sabrio, Erik VonKaenel, Lee Burke

entry.summary: Proposes a systematic framework to test LLM sensitivity to subtle semantic changes in document comparison, revealing positional biases, perturbation-type sensitivity differences, and model-specific failure patterns across five LLMs and tens of thousands of document pairs.

entry.title: Low-Rank Adaptation for Critic Learning in Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuan Zhuang, Yuexin Bian, Sihong He, Jie Feng, Qing Su, Songyang Han, Jonathan Petit, Shihao Ji, Yuanyuan Shi, Fei Miao

entry.summary: Applies Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) as a structural-sparsity regularizer for off-policy RL critics, freezing base matrices and optimizing only low-rank adapters. Develops a LoRA formulation compatible with SimbaV2's hyperspherical normalization.

entry.title: Talking to a Know-It-All GPT or a Second-Guesser Claude? How Repair reveals unreliable Multi-Turn Behavior in LLMs

author.name: Clara Lachenmaier, Hannah Bultmann, Sina Zarrie{\ss}

entry.summary: Studies how LLMs handle conversational repair (error correction) in multi-turn math dialogues, finding stark behavioral differences: some models are resistant to repair while others are easily manipulated, with behavior becoming less predictable over longer conversations.

entry.title: CulturALL: Benchmarking Multilingual and Multicultural Competence of LLMs on Grounded Tasks

author.name: Peiqin Lin, Chenyang Lyu, Wenjiang Luo, Haotian Ye, Md Mehrab Hossain, Chunlan Ma, Shaoxiong Ji, Younes Samih, Bo Zeng, Fan Jiang, Yuanbin Cao, Dilda Duisenbek, Adrian Neo Sau Xun, Daria Pozdniakova, Liubou Misevich, Nevena Marinkovi\'c, Ngoc Gia Linh Nguyen, Thi Khanh Linh Do, Sarakmatak Sophy, Baotian Hu, Guanhua Chen, Gongbo Tang, Alham Fikri Aji, Longyue Wang, Weihua Luo

entry.summary: Introduces CulturALL, a comprehensive multilingual and multicultural benchmark for LLMs focusing on grounded tasks where models must reason within real-world, context-rich scenarios rather than answering cultural trivia.

entry.title: Lyapunov-Certified Direct Switching Theory for Q-Learning

author.name: Donghwan Lee

entry.summary: Analyzes Q-learning through a direct stochastic switching system representation, showing the Bellman maximization error can be represented as a stochastic policy. Derives finite-time bounds via joint spectral radius-induced Lyapunov functions.

entry.title: Safety-Critical Contextual Control via Online Riemannian Optimization with World Models

author.name: Tongxin Li

entry.summary: Develops a sample-based Penalized Predictive Control framework using online Riemannian optimization for safety-critical control with black-box world models. The approach compresses feasibility manifolds into score-based densities that guide planning.

entry.title: Physics-Guided Dimension Reduction for Simulation-Free Operator Learning of Stiff Differential--Algebraic Systems

author.name: Huy Hoang Le, Haoguang Wang, Christian Moya, Marcos Netto, Guang Lin

entry.summary: Introduces a physics-guided approach combining implicit layers with DeepONet for simulation-free learning of stiff differential-algebraic systems, enforcing algebraic consistency while reducing output dimension to slow states only.

entry.title: Concept Graph Convolutions: Message Passing in the Concept Space

author.name: Lucie Charlotte Magister, Pietro Lio

entry.summary: Proposes Concept Graph Convolutions that perform message passing on node-level concepts for improved interpretability, including a pure variant operating entirely in concept space.

entry.title: Cover meets Robbins while Betting on Bounded Data: $\ln n$ Regret and Almost Sure $\ln\ln n$ Regret

author.name: Shubhada Agrawal, Aaditya Ramdas

entry.summary: Presents a novel mixture betting strategy combining Robbins and Cover's insights that achieves O(ln ln n) regret almost surely for bounded data betting, improving on Cover's O(ln n) worst-case bound for most paths.

entry.title: Surrogate Functionals for Machine-Learned Orbital-Free Density Functional Theory

author.name: Roman Remme, Fred A. Hamprecht

entry.summary: Introduces surrogate functionals for orbital-free DFT that only require ground-state densities for training (no energies or off-equilibrium gradients). Proposes a gradient-descent-improvement loss guaranteeing exponential convergence to ground-state density.

entry.title: Variance Is Not Importance: Structural Analysis of Transformer Compressibility Across Model Scales

author.name: Samuel Salfati

entry.summary: Presents 40+ experiments on GPT-2 and Mistral 7B revealing five structural properties relevant to compression, including that high-variance directions are ~96% uncorrelated with predictive directions, and block linearity is conditional on token frequency.

entry.title: Stream-CQSA: Avoiding Out-of-Memory in Attention Computation via Flexible Workload Scheduling

author.name: Yiming Bian, Joshua M. Akey

entry.summary: Introduces Stream-CQSA, a memory-adaptive attention framework based on cyclic quorum set theory that decomposes full-sequence attention into independent subsequence computations, yielding exact results while avoiding OOM failures.

entry.title: HiPO: Hierarchical Preference Optimization for Adaptive Reasoning in LLMs

author.name: Darsh Kachroo, Adriana Caraeni, Arjun Prasaath Anbazhagan, Brennan Lagasse, Kevin Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes HiPO (Hierarchical Preference Optimization), extending DPO by decomposing responses into reasoning segments and applying segment-level preference optimization. Aims to provide more granular feedback for multi-step reasoning tasks where whole-response DPO struggles.

entry.title: Decentralized Machine Learning with Centralized Performance Guarantees via Gibbs Algorithms

author.name: Yaiza Bermudez, Samir Perlaza, I\~naki Esnaola

entry.summary: Proves that centralized learning performance is achievable in decentralized settings without sharing local data, using empirical risk minimization with relative-entropy regularization (ERM-RER). Clients share Gibbs measures sequentially, with each client's output serving as the next client's reference measure.

entry.title: Gauge-Equivariant Graph Neural Networks for Lattice Gauge Theories

author.name: Ali Rayat, Yaohang Li, Gia-Wei Chern

entry.summary: Introduces gauge-equivariant graph neural networks for lattice gauge theories, embedding non-Abelian symmetry into message passing with matrix-valued gauge-covariant features. Extends equivariant learning from global to fully local symmetries.

entry.title: From Actions to Understanding: Conformal Interpretability of Temporal Concepts in LLM Agents

author.name: Trilok Padhi, Ramneet Kaur, Krishiv Agarwal, Adam D. Cobb, Daniel Elenius, Manoj Acharya, Colin Samplawski, Alexander M. Berenbeim, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Susmit Jha, Anirban Roy

entry.summary: Presents a framework for interpreting temporal concept evolution in LLM agents using conformal prediction to statistically label internal representations as successful or failing at each step. Uses linear probes on conformally-labeled representations to identify temporal concepts.

entry.title: UniCon3R: Contact-aware 3D Human-Scene Reconstruction from Monocular Video

author.name: Tanuj Sur, Shashank Tripathi, Nikos Athanasiou, Ha Linh Nguyen, Kai Xu, Michael J. Black, Angela Yao

entry.summary: Introduces UniCon3R for contact-aware 4D human-scene reconstruction from monocular video, predicting 3D human-scene contact and using it to actively correct physically implausible artifacts like floating or penetrating bodies.

entry.title: X-Cache: Cross-Chunk Block Caching for Few-Step Autoregressive World Models Inference

author.name: Yixiao Zeng, Jianlei Zheng, Chaoda Zheng, Shijia Chen, Mingdian Liu, Tongping Liu, Tengwei Luo, Yu Zhang, Boyang Wang, Linkun Xu, Siyuan Lu, Bo Tian, Xianming Liu

entry.summary: Presents X-Cache, a cross-chunk block caching method for accelerating autoregressive world models used in autonomous driving simulation, addressing the unique challenges of few-step distilled models where standard diffusion caching fails.

entry.title: UniCVR: From Alignment to Reranking for Unified Zero-Shot Composed Visual Retrieval

author.name: Haokun Wen, Xuemeng Song, Haoyu Zhang, Xiangyu Zhao, Weili Guan, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: Introduces UniCVR, the first unified zero-shot composed visual retrieval framework that jointly addresses composed image retrieval, multi-turn composed retrieval, and composed video retrieval by combining MLLMs for query understanding with VLP models for retrieval.

entry.title: LaplacianFormer:Rethinking Linear Attention with Laplacian Kernel

author.name: Zhe Feng, Sen Lian, Changwei Wang, Muyang Zhang, Tianlong Tan, Rongtao Xu, Weiliang Meng, Xiaopeng Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes LaplacianFormer, a Transformer variant using Laplacian kernels instead of softmax attention with a provably injective feature map and Nyström approximation for efficient computation on high-resolution vision tasks.

entry.title: Evian: Towards Explainable Visual Instruction-tuning Data Auditing

author.name: Zimu Jia, Mingjie Xu, Andrew Estornell, Jiaheng Wei

entry.summary: Introduces Evian, a framework for auditing visual instruction-tuning data quality with a 300K benchmark of injected defects and a novel metric for fine-grained defect detection in LVLM training data.

entry.title: Exploring High-Order Self-Similarity for Video Understanding

author.name: Manjin Kim, Heeseung Kwon, Karteek Alahari, Minsu Cho

entry.summary: Introduces the MOSS (Multi-Order Self-Similarity) module that explores higher-order space-time self-similarity for video understanding, demonstrating improvements across action recognition, motion VQA, and robotic tasks.

entry.title: FingerEye: Continuous and Unified Vision-Tactile Sensing for Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Zhixuan Xu, Yichen Li, Xuanye Wu, Tianyu Qiu, Lin Shao

entry.summary: FingerEye is a compact sensor providing continuous vision-tactile feedback throughout all phases of interaction (pre-contact through post-contact). It integrates binocular RGB cameras for visual perception with a compliant ring structure that deforms under contact to measure forces and torques.

entry.title: Towards Scalable Lifelong Knowledge Editing with Selective Knowledge Suppression

author.name: Dahyun Jung, Jaewook Lee, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: Proposes LightEdit for scalable lifelong knowledge editing of LLMs, selecting relevant knowledge from retrieval to modify queries effectively while avoiding catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: ClawNet: Human-Symbiotic Agent Network for Cross-User Autonomous Cooperation

author.name: Zhiqin Yang, Zhenyuan Zhang, Xianzhang Jia, Jun Song, Wei Xue, Yonggang Zhang, Yike Guo

entry.summary: Proposes ClawNet, a paradigm for cross-user AI agent collaboration where agents represent individual users and coordinate, negotiate, and delegate across organizational boundaries.

entry.title: SimDiff: Depth Pruning via Similarity and Difference

author.name: Yuli Chen, Shuhao Zhang, Fanshen Meng, Bo Cheng, Jiale Han, Qiang Tong, Xiulei Liu

entry.summary: Proposes SimDiff, a layer importance criterion for depth pruning that evaluates both representational similarity and transformation difference, addressing catastrophic failures of cosine-distance-only methods.

entry.title: TurboEvolve: Towards Fast and Robust LLM-Driven Program Evolution

author.name: Yang Yang, Zining Zhong, Jindong Li, Jiemin Wu, Kaishen Yuan, Wenshuo Chen, Menglin Yang, Yutao Yue

entry.summary: Proposes TurboEvolve, a multi-island evolutionary framework for LLM-driven program evolution that improves sample efficiency through verbalized sampling and online scheduling under fixed evaluation budgets.

entry.title: Characterizing AlphaEarth Embedding Geometry for Agentic Environmental Reasoning

author.name: Mashrekur Rahman, Samuel J. Barrett, Christina Last

entry.summary: Characterizes the manifold geometry of Google AlphaEarth's 64-dimensional embeddings across 12.1M US samples and develops an agentic system leveraging this geometric understanding for environmental reasoning.

entry.title: Skillful Global Ocean Emulation and the Role of Correlation-Aware Loss

author.name: Niraj Agarwal, Timothy A. Smith, Sergey Frolov, Laura C. Slivinski

entry.summary: Adapts GraphCast architecture for global ocean emulation with prescribed atmospheric conditions, demonstrating skillful 10-15 day forecasts using Mahalanobis distance loss to account for correlations.

entry.title: Hierarchically Robust Zero-shot Vision-language Models

author.name: Junhao Dong, Yifei Zhang, Hao Zhu, Yew-Soon Ong, Piotr Koniusz

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical adversarial fine-tuning framework for Vision-Language Models that leverages class hierarchy (e.g., cat → mammal) to improve adversarial robustness at both base and superclass levels simultaneously.

entry.title: Self-Improving Tabular Language Models via Iterative Group Alignment

author.name: Yunbo Long, Tejumade Afonja, Alexandra Brintrup, Mario Fritz

entry.summary: Introduces TabGRAA, a self-improving framework for tabular data generation using group-relative advantage alignment, where the model iteratively improves from its own generated samples with automated quality feedback.

entry.title: ST-Prune: Training-Free Spatio-Temporal Token Pruning for Vision-Language Models in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Lin Sha, Haiyun Guo, Tao Wang, Cong Zhang, Min Huang, Jinqiao Wang, Qinghai Miao

entry.summary: Proposes ST-Prune, a training-free token pruning framework for VLMs in autonomous driving with motion-aware temporal pruning and ring-view spatial pruning to exploit spatio-temporal redundancies across multi-view, multi-frame inputs.

entry.title: GOLD-BEV: GrOund and aeriaL Data for Dense Semantic BEV Mapping of Dynamic Scenes

author.name: Joshua Niemeijer, Alaa Eddine Ben Zekri, Reza Bahmanyar, Philipp M. Schm\"alzle, Houda Chaabouni-Chouayakh, Franz Kurz

entry.summary: GOLD-BEV learns dense bird's-eye-view semantic maps from ego-centric sensors using time-synchronized aerial imagery as supervision during training only. The aerial-ground synchronization enables supervising dynamic traffic participants.

entry.title: Fairness Audits of Institutional Risk Models in Deployed ML Pipelines

author.name: Kelly McConvey, Dipto Das, Maya Ghai, Angelina Zhai, Rosa Lee, Shion Guha

entry.summary: Presents a fairness audit of a deployed Early Warning System at Centennial College, finding systematic misallocation where younger, male, and international students are disproportionately flagged for support. Demonstrates importance of auditing full ML pipelines including post-processing.

entry.title: On the Quantization Robustness of Diffusion Language Models in Coding Benchmarks

author.name: Aarav Gupta, Gururaj Deshpande, Chandreyi Chakraborty

entry.summary: Investigates post-training quantization robustness of diffusion-based language models (CoDA) vs autoregressive models (Qwen3-1.7B) on coding benchmarks, finding diffusion LMs show greater robustness at low bitwidths.

entry.title: On the Stability and Generalization of First-order Bilevel Minimax Optimization

author.name: Xuelin Zhang, Peipei Yuan

entry.summary: Provides the first systematic generalization analysis for first-order bilevel minimax optimization, deriving fine-grained bounds for three representative algorithms using algorithmic stability.

entry.title: Adaptive Conformal Anomaly Detection with Time Series Foundation Models for Signal Monitoring

author.name: Natalia Martinez Gil, Fearghal O'Donncha, Wesley M. Gifford, Nianjun Zhou, Dhaval C. Patel, Roman Vaculin

entry.summary: Proposes adaptive conformal anomaly detection for time series monitoring that works with pre-trained foundation models without fine-tuning, using weighted quantile conformal prediction with learned weighting parameters.

entry.title: Geometric Layer-wise Approximation Rates for Deep Networks

author.name: Shijun Zhang, Zuowei Shen, Yuesheng Xu

entry.summary: Develops a theoretical framework showing that each intermediate layer of a deep neural network can serve as a progressively better approximant, with geometric (exponential) improvement in approximation error per layer. Provides a precise scale-dependent interpretation of depth.

entry.title: Too Sharp, Too Sure: When Calibration Follows Curvature

author.name: Alessandro Morosini, Matea Gjika, Tomaso Poggio, Pierfrancesco Beneventano

entry.summary: Shows that calibration error closely tracks curvature-based sharpness throughout optimization, and that both ECE and Gauss-Newton curvature are controlled by the same quantities. Demonstrates calibration can be addressed at training time rather than post-hoc.

entry.title: MGDA-Decoupled: Geometry-Aware Multi-Objective Optimisation for DPO-based LLM Alignment

author.name: Andor V\'ari-Kakas, Ji Won Park, Natasa Tagasovska

entry.summary: Proposes MGDA-Decoupled for multi-objective LLM alignment via DPO, finding shared descent directions while accounting for each objective's convergence dynamics. Addresses procedural unfairness from fixed scalarization of helpfulness, truthfulness, and harmlessness.

entry.title: Supplement Generation Training for Enhancing Agentic Task Performance

author.name: Young Min Cho, Daniele Bonadiman, Divya Bhargavi, Tamer Alkhouli, Salvatore Romeo, Dongwei Jiang, Khushbu Pahwa, Yubin Ge, Etsuko Ishii, Monica Sunkara, Yi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Supplement Generation Training (SGT), where a smaller LLM is trained to generate supplemental text that helps a larger LLM solve agentic tasks more effectively. Decouples task-specific optimization from large model modification.

entry.title: ParetoSlider: Diffusion Models Post-Training for Continuous Reward Control

author.name: Shelly Golan, Michael Finkelson, Ariel Bereslavsky, Yotam Nitzan, Or Patashnik

entry.summary: Introduces ParetoSlider, a multi-objective RL framework that trains a single diffusion model to approximate the entire Pareto front by conditioning on continuously varying preference weights, enabling inference-time control over competing criteria.

entry.title: ThermoQA: A Three-Tier Benchmark for Evaluating Thermodynamic Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Kemal D\"uzkar

entry.summary: Presents ThermoQA, a 293-question benchmark for engineering thermodynamics across three difficulty tiers. Evaluates six frontier LLMs, finding Claude Opus 4.6 (94.1%), GPT-5.4 (93.1%), and Gemini 3.1 Pro (92.5%) lead, with large cross-tier degradation in weaker models.

entry.title: scpFormer: A Foundation Model for Unified Representation and Integration of the Single-Cell Proteomics

author.name: Qifeng Zhou, Lei Yu, Yuzhi Guo, Yuwei Miao, Hehuan Ma, Wenliang Zhong, Lin Xu, Junzhou Huang

entry.summary: Introduces scpFormer, a transformer foundation model pre-trained on 390M+ single cells for proteomics, using continuous sequence-anchored tokenization with ESM embeddings. Enables open-vocabulary protein prediction and cross-panel integration.

entry.title: Meta-Tool: Efficient Few-Shot Tool Adaptation for Small Language Models

author.name: Sachin Kumar

entry.summary: Presents a negative result: hypernetwork-based LoRA adaptation provides no measurable improvement over carefully designed few-shot prompting for tool use in small language models (Llama-3.2-3B). Evaluates across four diverse benchmarks including Gorilla APIBench and WebArena.

entry.title: Efficient Symbolic Computations for Identifying Causal Effects

author.name: Benjamin Hollering, Pratik Misra, Nils Sturma

entry.summary: Presents an efficient algorithm for deciding rational identifiability of causal effects using symbolic computation, provably finding the lowest degree identifying formulas. Addresses the computational infeasibility of standard Gröbner basis approaches.

entry.title: Coverage, Not Averages: Semantic Stratification for Trustworthy Retrieval Evaluation

author.name: Andrew Klearman, Radu Revutchi, Rohin Garg, Rishav Chakravarti, Samuel Marc Denton, Yuan Xue

entry.summary: Formalizes RAG retrieval evaluation as a statistical estimation problem and introduces semantic stratification for corpus-aware evaluation. Shows that heuristic query sets introduce hidden bias, and provides formal coverage guarantees across retrieval regimes.

entry.title: OThink-SRR1: Search, Refine and Reasoning with Reinforced Learning for Large Language Models

author.name: Haijian Liang, Zenghao Niu, Junjie Wu, Changwang Zhang, Wangchunshu Zhou, Jun Wang

entry.summary: Proposes OThink-SRR1, a Search-Refine-Reason framework for RAG with reinforcement learning. Key innovation is a Refine stage that distills retrieved documents into concise facts before reasoning, trained end-to-end with GRPO-IR algorithm.

entry.title: Can LLMs Infer Conversational Agent Users' Personality Traits from Chat History?

author.name: Derya C\"ogendez, Verena Zimmermann, No\'e Zufferey

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLMs can infer personality traits from ChatGPT chat histories. Analyzes 62,090 chats from 668 participants, finding fine-tuned RoBERTa achieves above-random accuracy for personality trait inference, raising privacy concerns.

entry.title: Graph2Counsel: Clinically Grounded Synthetic Counseling Dialogue Generation from Client Psychological Graphs

author.name: Aishik Mandal, Hiba Arnaout, Clarissa W. Ong, Juliet Bockhorst, Kate Sheehan, Rachael Moldow, Tanmoy Chakraborty, Iryna Gurevych

entry.summary: Introduces Graph2Counsel, a framework for generating synthetic counseling dialogues grounded in Client Psychological Graphs (CPGs) that encode relationships between cognitive, emotional, and behavioral states, addressing the scarcity of real counseling data for LLM training.

entry.title: LayerTracer: A Joint Task-Particle and Vulnerable-Layer Analysis framework for Arbitrary Large Language Model Architectures

author.name: Yuhang Wu, Qinyuan Liu, Qiuyang Zhao, Qingwei Chong

entry.summary: Proposes LayerTracer, an architecture-agnostic framework for analyzing LLMs that works across Transformers, GateDeltaNet, and Mamba architectures. Extracts hidden states layer-by-layer to jointly analyze task knowledge localization and layer vulnerability.

entry.title: Intersectional Fairness in Large Language Models

author.name: Chaima Boufaied, Ronnie De Souza Santos, Ann Barcomb

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates intersectional fairness across six LLMs using ambiguous and disambiguated contexts, analyzing bias scores, subgroup metrics, and consistency. Finds that modern LLMs perform well in ambiguous contexts but show variable accuracy in disambiguated settings with intersectional disparities.

entry.title: HaS: Accelerating RAG through Homology-Aware Speculative Retrieval

author.name: Peng Peng, Weiwei Lin, Wentai Wu, Xinyang Wang, Yongheng Liu
