entry.summary: Proposes a test-time scaling framework for coding agents that converts rollout trajectories into structured summaries preserving hypotheses, errors, and partial progress, enabling effective selection and reuse across attempts. Features authors from CMU, Meta, and Princeton.

entry.title: OmniMouse: Scaling properties of multi-modal, multi-task Brain Models on 150B Neural Tokens

author.name: Konstantin F. Willeke, Polina Turishcheva, Alex Gilbert, Goirik Chakrabarty, Hasan A. Bedel, Paul G. Fahey, Yongrong Qiu, Marissa A. Weis, Michaela Vystr\v{c}ilov\'a, Taliah Muhammad, Lydia Ntanavara, Rachel E. Froebe, Kayla Ponder, Zheng Huan Tan, Emin Orhan, Erick Cobos, Sophia Sanborn, Katrin Franke, Fabian H. Sinz, Alexander S. Ecker, Andreas S. Tolias

entry.summary: Presents OmniMouse, a multi-modal multi-task brain model trained on 3.1 million neurons from 73 mice (150B neural tokens). Demonstrates scaling laws for neural data modeling, achieving state-of-the-art across neural prediction, behavioral decoding, and neural forecasting tasks.

entry.title: LLMs Know They're Wrong and Agree Anyway: The Shared Sycophancy-Lying Circuit

author.name: Manav Pandey

entry.summary: Shows that across 12 open-weight LLMs, the same small set of attention heads carries a 'this is wrong' signal during both sycophancy and factual lying, revealing a shared circuit. Silencing these heads flips sycophantic behavior while preserving factual accuracy.

entry.title: How Adversarial Environments Mislead Agentic AI?

author.name: Zhonghao Zhan, Huichi Zhou, Zhenhao Li, Peiyuan Jing, Krinos Li, Hamed Haddadi

entry.summary: Identifies the 'Trust Gap' in tool-using AI agents - they're evaluated for capability but not skepticism. Introduces Adversarial Environmental Injection (AEI) and POTEMKIN benchmark where tool outputs are poisoned to deceive agents.

entry.title: Reasoning Structure Matters for Safety Alignment of Reasoning Models

author.name: Yeonjun In, Wonjoong Kim, Sangwu Park, Chanyoung Park

entry.summary: Shows that safety failures in large reasoning models stem from the reasoning structure itself, and proposes AltTrain, a simple SFT method using only 1K examples to alter reasoning structure for safety alignment without complex RL.

entry.title: Towards Understanding the Robustness of Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Ahson Saiyed, Sabrina Sadiekh, Chirag Agarwal

entry.summary: Studies using pretrained Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) inserted into transformer residual streams at inference time as a defense against jailbreak attacks, achieving up to 5x reduction in attack success rate. Tests across four model families (Gemma, LLaMA, Mistral, Qwen) and multiple attack types without modifying model weights. Reveals a monotonic relationship between SAE width and robustness.

entry.title: EVPO: Explained Variance Policy Optimization for Adaptive Critic Utilization in LLM Post-Training

author.name: Chengjun Pan, Shichun Liu, Jiahang Lin, Dingwei Zhu, Jiazheng Zhang, Shihan Dou, Songyang Gao, Zhenhua Han, Binghai Wang, Rui Zheng, Xuanjing Huang, Tao Gui, Yansong Feng

entry.summary: EVPO introduces explained variance as a criterion for adaptively choosing between critic-based (PPO) and critic-free (GRPO) baselines in RL for LLM post-training. Unifies PPO and GRPO as extremes of a Kalman gain and shows a learned critic can increase variance in sparse-reward settings.

entry.title: Separating Geometry from Probability in the Analysis of Generalization

author.name: Maxim Raginsky, Benjamin Recht

entry.summary: Presents an alternative view of generalization that separates geometric from probabilistic assumptions, using sensitivity analysis rather than i.i.d. assumptions. Authors include Benjamin Recht, a prominent ML theorist.

entry.title: NeuroAI and Beyond: Bridging Between Advances in Neuroscience and ArtificialIntelligence

author.name: Anthony Zador, Jean-Marc Fellous, Terrence Sejnowski, Gina Adam, James B Aimone, Akwasi Akwaboah, Yiannis Aloimonos, Carmen Amo Alonso, Chiara Bartolozzi, Michael J. Bennington, Michael Berry, Bing W. Brunton, Gert Cauwenberghs, Hillel J. Chiel, Tobi Delbruck, John Doyle, Jason Eshraghian, Ralph Etienne-Cummings, Cornelia Fermuller, Matthew Jacobsen, Ali A. Minai, Barbara Oakley, Alexander G. Ororbia II, Joe Paton, Blake Richards, Yulia Sandamirskaya, Abhronil Sengupta, Shihab Shamma, Michael P. Stryker, Seong Jong Yoo, Steven W. Zucker

entry.summary: NSF workshop report identifying three AI capability gaps (physical world interaction, brittle learning, energy inefficiency) and mapping neuroscience principles that could address each. Features prominent authors (Zador, Sejnowski, etc.).

entry.title: Harmful Intent as a Geometrically Recoverable Feature of LLM Residual Streams

author.name: Isaac Llorente-Saguer

entry.summary: Demonstrates that harmful intent is geometrically recoverable from LLM residual streams as a linear direction in most layers (AUROC 0.98) across 12 models spanning four architectural families and three alignment variants. Angular deviation succeeds where linear projection fails.

entry.title: Evaluation-driven Scaling for Scientific Discovery

author.name: Haotian Ye, Haowei Lin, Jingyi Tang, Yizhen Luo, Caiyin Yang, Chang Su, Rahul Thapa, Rui Yang, Ruihua Liu, Zeyu Li, Chong Gao, Dachao Ding, Guangrong He, Miaolei Zhang, Lina Sun, Wenyang Wang, Yuchen Zhong, Zhuohao Shen, Di He, Jianzhu Ma, Stefano Ermon, Tongyang Li, Xiaowen Chu, James Zou, Yuzhi Xu

entry.summary: Introduces SimpleTES, a general framework for scaling evaluation-driven scientific discovery loops by strategically combining test-time compute with evaluation feedback. Addresses how to principally scale trial-and-error discovery with LLMs.

entry.title: Beyond Indistinguishability: Measuring Extraction Risk in LLM APIs

author.name: Ruixuan Liu, David Evans, Li Xiong

entry.summary: Formalizes a separation between extraction and indistinguishability-based privacy in LLM APIs, showing they are incomparable. Introduces (l,b)-inextractability as a new privacy definition requiring exponential queries for extraction.

entry.title: ARES: Adaptive Red-Teaming and End-to-End Repair of Policy-Reward System

author.name: Jiacheng Liang, Yao Ma, Tharindu Kumarage, Satyapriya Krishna, Rahul Gupta, Kai-Wei Chang, Aram Galstyan, Charith Peris

entry.summary: Proposes ARES, a framework that discovers and mitigates dual vulnerabilities where both the LLM policy and reward model fail simultaneously in RLHF. Uses a 'Safety Mentor' to compose adversarial prompts and generate matching safe responses.

entry.title: Temporal UI State Inconsistency in Desktop GUI Agents: Formalizing and Defending Against TOCTOU Attacks on Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Wenpeng Xu

entry.summary: Formalizes TOCTOU (Time-Of-Check, Time-Of-Use) vulnerabilities in GUI agents that control desktops via screenshot-and-click loops. Identifies a 6.51s observation-to-action gap enabling UI manipulation attacks, with one primitive achieving 100% redirection success. Proposes Pre-execution UI State Verification defense.

entry.title: TEMPO: Scaling Test-time Training for Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Qingyang Zhang, Xinke Kong, Haitao Wu, Qinghua Hu, Minghao Wu, Baosong Yang, Yu Cheng, Yun Luo, Ganqu Cui, Changqing Zhang

entry.summary: TEMPO scales test-time training for large reasoning models by interleaving policy refinement on unlabeled questions with periodic critic recalibration, formalized through EM. Addresses reward drift and diversity collapse in TTT.

entry.title: An Efficient Black-Box Reduction from Online Learning to Multicalibration, and a New Route to $\Phi$-Regret Minimization

author.name: Gabriele Farina, Juan Carlos Perdomo

entry.summary: Provides a black-box reduction from online learning to online multicalibration, resolving the main open question from SODA '24. Shows that oracle-efficient online multicalibration with sqrt(T) guarantees is achievable and connects to Phi-regret minimization.

entry.title: AI 2027 Tracker: One Year of Predictions vs. Reality

author.name: hauspost

entry.summary: A systematic tracking of 53 predictions from the 'AI 2027' scenario against reality over one year, finding that capability predictions are running behind schedule but safety/security risks are arriving ahead of predicted timelines. Notably, Claude Mythos Preview autonomously finding thousands of zero-days happened ~1 year early vs predictions.

entry.title: Local Linearity of LLMs Enables Activation Steering via Model-Based Linear Optimal Control

author.name: Julian Skifstad, Xinyue Annie Yang, Glen Chou

entry.summary: Shows that transformer layer-wise dynamics are well-approximated by locally-linear models and leverages this to apply linear quadratic regulator (LQR) control theory for activation steering. Provides feedback-based, anticipative control that accounts for perturbation propagation through layers.

entry.title: Owner-Harm: A Missing Threat Model for AI Agent Safety

author.name: Dongcheng Zhang, Yiqing Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes Owner-Harm threat model for AI agents - behaviors that damage the deployer rather than third parties. Shows existing safety systems achieve 100% on generic harm but only 14.8% on owner-harm scenarios.

entry.title: Where Fake Citations Are Made: Tracing Field-Level Hallucination to Specific Neurons in LLMs

author.name: Yuefei Chen, Yihao Quan, Xiaodong Lin, Ruixiang Tang

entry.summary: Traces field-level hallucination in LLM-generated citations to specific neurons, studying 9 models and 108K references. Finds author names fail far more than other fields, probes don't transfer across fields, and identifies sparse field-specific hallucination neurons via elastic-net regularization in Qwen2.5-32B.

entry.title: Discrete Tilt Matching

author.name: Yuyuan Chen, Shiyi Wang, Peter Potaptchik, Jaeyeon Kim, Michael S. Albergo

entry.summary: Derives Discrete Tilt Matching (DTM), a likelihood-free RL fine-tuning method for masked diffusion language models that reformulates fine-tuning as state-level matching of local unmasking posteriors under reward tilting.

entry.title: When Safety Fails Before the Answer: Benchmarking Harmful Behavior Detection in Reasoning Chains

author.name: Ishita Kakkar, Enze Zhang, Rheeya Uppaal, Junjie Hu

entry.summary: Introduces HarmThoughts, a benchmark for step-wise safety evaluation of reasoning traces in LLMs, capturing how harm unfolds through distinct behavioral steps rather than just evaluating final outputs.

entry.title: Micro Language Models Enable Instant Responses

author.name: Wen Cheng, Tuochao Chen, Karim Helwani, Sriram Srinivasan, Luke Zettlemoyer, Shyamnath Gollakota

entry.summary: Introduces micro language models (μLMs, 8-30M parameters) designed for edge devices like smartwatches that generate the first 4-8 words on-device while a cloud model completes the response, masking cloud latency. Shows useful generation survives at extreme model scales.

entry.title: $R^2$-dLLM: Accelerating Diffusion Large Language Models via Spatio-Temporal Redundancy Reduction

author.name: Zhenbang Du, Kejing Xia, Xinrui Zhong, Yonggan Fu, Nicolai Oswald, Binfei Ji, Brucek Khailany, Pavlo Molchanov, Yingyan Lin

entry.summary: Proposes R²-dLLM for accelerating Diffusion Large Language Models by reducing spatial redundancy (confidence clusters, positional ambiguity) and temporal redundancy (repeated remasking of stabilized predictions) during decoding.

entry.title: Human-Guided Harm Recovery for Computer Use Agents

author.name: Christy Li, Sky CH-Wang, Andi Peng, Andreea Bobu

entry.summary: Formalizes 'harm recovery' for computer-use agents - steering agents from harmful states back to safe ones after prevention fails. Includes a user study producing recovery rubrics and a dataset of 1,150 pairwise judgments.

entry.title: Do LLMs Game Formalization? Evaluating Faithfulness in Logical Reasoning

author.name: Kyuhee Kim, Auguste Poiroux, Antoine Bosselut

entry.summary: Investigates whether frontier models (GPT-5, DeepSeek-R1) exploit the gap between valid Lean 4 proofs and faithful formalizations of natural language logic problems. Finds no evidence of systematic 'formalization gaming'.

entry.title: Compile to Compress: Boosting Formal Theorem Provers by Compiler Outputs

author.name: Guchan Li, Rui Tian, Hongning Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a learning-to-refine framework for formal theorem proving that exploits the compression from compiler outputs (diverse proof attempts map to compact failure modes), achieving tree search guided by verifier feedback.

entry.title: Distillation Traps and Guards: A Calibration Knob for LLM Distillability

author.name: Weixiao Zhan, Yongcheng Jing, Leszek Rutkowski, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: Identifies 'distillation traps' (tail noise, off-policy instability, teacher-student gap) that cause knowledge distillation to fail, and proposes a post-hoc calibration method using reinforcement fine-tuning to control a teacher LLM's distillability—enabling both better distillation and protection against model leakage.

entry.title: The Rise of Verbal Tics in Large Language Models: A Systematic Analysis Across Frontier Models

author.name: Shuai Wu, Xue Li, Yanna Feng, Yufang Li, Zhijun Wang, Ran Wang

entry.summary: Systematically analyzes verbal tics (repetitive formulaic patterns like 'That's a great question!' and overused words like 'delve') across eight frontier LLMs including GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.7, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and Grok 4.2. Studies how RLHF and alignment produce these patterns.

entry.title: VLA Foundry: A Unified Framework for Training Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Jean Mercat, Sedrick Keh, Kushal Arora, Isabella Huang, Paarth Shah, Haruki Nishimura, Shun Iwase, Katherine Liu

entry.summary: VLA Foundry is an open-source framework unifying LLM, VLM, and VLA training in a single codebase, supporting end-to-end pipelines from language pretraining to action-expert fine-tuning, with models trained on Qwen3-VL backbone.

entry.title: Unsupervised Confidence Calibration for Reasoning LLMs from a Single Generation

author.name: Thomas Zollo, Jimmy Wang, Richard Zemel

entry.summary: Proposes unsupervised confidence calibration for reasoning LLMs from a single generation by distilling self-consistency signals from offline sampling into a lightweight deployment-time predictor. Substantially outperforms baselines across 9 reasoning models.

entry.title: Structure-guided molecular design with contrastive 3D protein-ligand learning

author.name: Carles Navarro, Philipp Tholke, Gianni de Fabritiis

entry.summary: Presents a unified framework for structure-based drug discovery combining SE(3)-equivariant contrastive learning of 3D protein-ligand interactions with autoregressive molecular generation conditioned on commercial compound spaces. Achieves competitive zero-shot virtual screening.

entry.title: Cell-Based Representation of Relational Binding in Language Models

author.name: Qin Dai, Benjamin Heinzerling, Kentaro Inui

entry.summary: Discovers that LLMs encode relational binding via Cell-based Binding Representations (CBR) - low-dimensional linear subspaces where entity-relation pairs map to cells from which attributes are retrieved during inference.

entry.title: Pause or Fabricate? Training Language Models for Grounded Reasoning

author.name: Yiwen Qiu, Linjuan Wu, Yizhou Liu, Yuchen Yan, Jin Ma, Xu Tan, Yao Hu, Daoxin Zhang, Wenqi Zhang, Weiming Lu, Jun Xiao, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: Proposes GRIL, a multi-turn reinforcement learning framework that trains LLMs to pause and ask clarifying questions when premises for valid inference are missing, rather than fabricating information. Addresses 'ungrounded reasoning' through inferential boundary awareness.

entry.title: Pando: A Controlled Benchmark for Interpretability Methods

author.name: Ziqian Zhong

entry.summary: Introduces Pando, an interpretability benchmark with 720+ fine-tuned LLMs carrying known decision rules and varying rationale faithfulness. Finds gradient-based methods outperform blackbox baselines while non-gradient methods struggle.

entry.title: Automated Deanonymization is Here

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: Jeff Kaufman demonstrates that modern LLMs (specifically Claude Opus 4.7) can now trivially deanonymize authors from short text snippets through stylometry, a task that previously required custom code and technical expertise. This represents a significant practical privacy degradation.

entry.title: Position: No Retroactive Cure for Infringement during Training

author.name: Satoru Utsunomiya, Masaru Isonuma, Junichiro Mori, Ichiro Sakata

entry.summary: Position paper arguing that post-hoc mitigation methods (unlearning, guardrails) cannot retroactively cure copyright liability from unlawful training data acquisition, because compliance hinges on data lineage not outputs.

entry.title: Beyond Explicit Refusals: Soft-Failure Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Wentao Zhang, Yan Zhuang, ZhuHang Zheng, Mingfei Zhang, Jiawen Deng, Fuji Ren

entry.summary: Formalizes 'soft failure' attacks on RAG systems - generating fluent but non-informative responses rather than overt refusals. Proposes DEJA, an evolutionary attack framework exploiting safety-aligned behaviors.

entry.title: One Step Forward and K Steps Back: Better Reasoning with Denoising Recursion Models

author.name: Chris Cameron, Wangzheng Wang, Nikita Ivanov, Ashmita Bhattacharyya, Didier Ch\'etelat, Yingxue Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes denoising recursion models that combine looped transformers with diffusion-inspired training for iterative refinement on reasoning tasks requiring search-like computation. Addresses the challenge of learning refinement trajectories without intermediate supervision.

entry.title: Intentional Updates for Streaming Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Arsalan Sharifnassab, Mohamed Elsayed, Kris De Asis, A. Rupam Mahmood, Richard S. Sutton

entry.summary: Proposes 'intentional updates' for streaming reinforcement learning that specify the intended outcome of an update and solve for the step size, extending Normalized LMS to deep RL. Addresses instability in streaming (batch size=1) settings. Authored by Richard Sutton's group.

entry.title: When Graph Structure Becomes a Liability: A Critical Re-Evaluation of Graph Neural Networks for Bitcoin Fraud Detection under Temporal Distribution Shift

author.name: Saket Maganti

entry.summary: Shows that the consensus that GNNs outperform feature-only baselines on the Elliptic Bitcoin Dataset does not hold under leakage-free evaluation. Random Forest achieves F1=0.821 vs GraphSAGE's 0.689, with a 39.5-point gap attributable to test-time adjacency leakage.

entry.title: Generalization at the Edge of Stability

author.name: Mario Tuci, Caner Korkmaz, Umut \c{S}im\c{s}ekli, Tolga Birdal

entry.summary: Introduces 'sharpness dimension' based on Lyapunov dimension theory for neural networks training at the edge of stability, proving a generalization bound that connects chaotic training dynamics to improved generalization.

entry.title: DASH-KV: Accelerating Long-Context LLM Inference via Asymmetric KV Cache Hashing

author.name: Jinyu Guo, Zhihan Zhang, Yutong Li, Jiehui Xie, Md. Tamim Iqbal, Dongshen Han, Lik-Hang Lee, Sung-Ho Bae, Jie Zou, Yang Yang, Chaoning Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces DASH-KV, an acceleration framework for long-context LLM inference that reformulates attention as approximate nearest-neighbor search via asymmetric deep hashing, with different encodings for queries and keys.

entry.title: Personalized Benchmarking: Evaluating LLMs by Individual Preferences

author.name: Cristina Garbacea, Heran Wang, Chenhao Tan

entry.summary: Proposes personalized LLM benchmarking using individual ELO ratings and Bradley-Terry coefficients for 115 Chatbot Arena users, showing that user preferences diverge significantly from aggregate rankings.

entry.title: OLLM: Options-based Large Language Models

author.name: Shashank Sharma, Janina Hoffmann, Vinay Namboodiri

entry.summary: Introduces Options LLM (OLLM), replacing single next-token prediction with a set of learned options indexed by a discrete latent variable. Lightweight plug-in adding only 1.56% parameters to a 1.7B backbone.

entry.title: SafetyALFRED: Evaluating Safety-Conscious Planning of Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Josue Torres-Fonseca, Naihao Deng, Yinpei Dai, Shane Storks, Yichi Zhang, Rada Mihalcea, Casey Kennington, Joyce Chai

entry.summary: Introduces SafetyALFRED, augmenting the ALFRED embodied agent benchmark with kitchen hazards, revealing that models can recognize hazards in QA settings but fail at active risk mitigation in embodied planning.

entry.title: ARGUS: Agentic GPU Optimization Guided by Data-Flow Invariants

author.name: Haohui Mai, Xiaoyan Guo, Xiangyun Ding, Daifeng Li, Qiuchu Yu, Chenzhun Guo, Cong Wang, Jiacheng Zhao, Christos Kozyrakis, Binhang Yuan

entry.summary: Introduces ARGUS, an agentic framework for GPU kernel optimization using data-flow invariants as compile-time specifications, bridging the gap between LLM-generated and hand-optimized kernels.

entry.title: Geometric Decoupling: Diagnosing the Structural Instability of Latent

author.name: Yuanbang Liang, Zhengwen Chen, Yu-Kun Lai

entry.summary: Introduces a Riemannian framework to diagnose instability in Latent Diffusion Models by analyzing the generative Jacobian, decomposing geometry into Local Scaling and Local Complexity. Discovers 'Geometric Decoupling' where out-of-distribution generation wastes curvature on unstable semantic boundaries rather than perceptible details.

entry.title: Gradient-Based Program Synthesis with Neurally Interpreted Languages

author.name: Matthew V. Macfarlane, Cl\'ement Bonnet, Herke van Hoof, Levi H. S. Lelis

entry.summary: Proposes Neural Language Interpreter (NLI), a Latent Adaptation Network that learns its own discrete programming language end-to-end, bridging symbolic and neural program synthesis. Discovers primitive operations and composes them to solve tasks without predefined domain-specific languages.

entry.title: Nexusformer: Nonlinear Attention Expansion for Stable and Inheritable Transformer Scaling

author.name: Weijie Zhao, Mingquan Liu, Bolun Wang, Simo Wu, Nuobei Xie, Rui-Jie Zhu, Peng Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces Nexusformer, which replaces linear Q/K/V projections in transformers with nonlinear Nexus-Rank layers using dual activations in progressively higher dimensions, enabling lossless structured growth and model inheritance without retraining from scratch.

entry.title: How Do Answer Tokens Read Reasoning Traces? Self-Reading Patterns in Thinking LLMs for Quantitative Reasoning

author.name: Haoyang Chen, Yi Liu, Jianzhi Shao, Tao Zhang, Chengfu Huo, Wei Hu

entry.summary: Analyzes how answer tokens in thinking LLMs read reasoning traces, identifying a 'self-reading pattern' where correct solutions show forward-drifting attention focus and concentration on semantic anchors, while incorrect solutions show diffuse attention.

entry.title: Taming Actor-Observer Asymmetry in Agents via Dialectical Alignment

author.name: Bobo Li, Rui Wu, Zibo Ji, Meishan Zhang, Hao Fei, Min Zhang, Mong-Li Lee, Wynne Hsu

entry.summary: Identifies Actor-Observer Asymmetry (AOA) cognitive bias in multi-agent LLM frameworks, where actors attribute failures externally while observers blame internal faults. Proposes Dialectical Alignment to mitigate this bias.

entry.title: An AI Agent Execution Environment to Safeguard User Data

author.name: Robert Stanley, Avi Verma, Lillian Tsai, Konstantinos Kallas, Sam Kumar

entry.summary: GAAP presents an execution environment for AI agents that guarantees confidentiality of private user data through dynamic permission specifications and secure execution, protecting against prompt injection and unscrupulous providers.

entry.title: SAW-INT4: System-Aware 4-Bit KV-Cache Quantization for Real-World LLM Serving

author.name: Jinda Jia, Jisen Li, Zhongzhu Zhou, Jung Hwan Heo, Jue Wang, Tri Dao, Shuaiwen Leon Song, Ben Athiwaratkun, Chenfeng Xu, Tianyi Zhang, Xiaoxia Wu

entry.summary: SAW-INT4 identifies that simple token-wise INT4 quantization with block-diagonal Hadamard rotation consistently achieves the best accuracy-efficiency tradeoff for KV-cache compression under real serving constraints.

entry.title: Calibrating Scientific Foundation Models with Inference-Time Stochastic Attention

author.name: Akash Yadav, Taiwo A. Adebiyi, Ruda Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces Stochastic Attention, a lightweight inference-time modification that adds calibrated uncertainty to transformer-based scientific foundation models without retraining. Uses randomized attention weights controlled by a single concentration parameter to produce predictive ensembles.

entry.title: An Empirical Study of Multi-Generation Sampling for Jailbreak Detection in Large Language Models

author.name: Hanrui Luo, Shreyank N Gowda

entry.summary: Shows that single-output evaluation systematically underestimates LLM jailbreak vulnerability; sampling multiple generations reveals significantly more harmful behavior. Evaluates lexical and inconsistency-based detectors across sampling budgets.

entry.title: Remask, Don't Replace: Token-to-Mask Refinement in Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Lin Yao

entry.summary: Proposes Token-to-Mask (T2M) remasking for masked diffusion language models like LLaDA, identifying three failure modes of the standard Token-to-Token editing approach and showing that resetting suspect tokens to mask state enables better correction.

entry.title: Prioritizing the Best: Incentivizing Reliable Multimodal Reasoning by Rewarding Beyond Answer Correctness

author.name: Mengzhao Jia, Zhihan Zhang, Meng Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes Groupwise Ranking Reward for multimodal RL that addresses reasoning-answer inconsistency by ranking trajectories beyond just answer correctness. Compares reward models vs generative rewards for trajectory supervision.

entry.title: STAR-Teaming: A Strategy-Response Multiplex Network Approach to Automated LLM Red Teaming

author.name: MinJae Jung, YongTaek Lim, Chaeyun Kim, Junghwan Kim, Kihyun Kim, Minwoo Kim

entry.summary: Introduces STAR-Teaming, a black-box automated red teaming framework using a multi-agent system with a strategy-response multiplex network, recasting the attack strategy search into a tractable network structure.

entry.title: I used this repo to partially replicate Anthropic's Emotion Concepts paper in a day

author.name: ewern

entry.summary: Introduces 'traitinterp', an open-source tool for running linear probe experiments on LLMs, and uses it to partially replicate Anthropic's Emotion Concepts paper on Llama 3.3 70B. Finds mostly similar results to Sonnet 4.5, except Llama's assistant-position tracks user emotion (r=0.63) while Sonnet keeps them independent (r=0.11).

entry.title: RoboWM-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating World Models in Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Feng Jiang, Yang Chen, Kyle Xu, Yuchen Liu, Haifeng Wang, Zhenhao Shen, Jasper Lu, Shengze Huang, Yuanfei Wang, Chen Xie, Ruihai Wu

entry.summary: Introduces RoboWM-Bench, a manipulation-centric benchmark for evaluating whether video world models produce physically plausible and executable predictions for robot manipulation, going beyond visual realism to embodiment-grounded evaluation.

entry.title: AutomationBench

author.name: Daniel Shepard, Robin Salimans

entry.summary: Introduces AutomationBench, evaluating AI agents on cross-application workflow orchestration via REST APIs, spanning Sales, Marketing, Operations, Support, Finance, and HR domains with tasks requiring autonomous API discovery and policy compliance.

entry.title: SAVOIR: Learning Social Savoir-Faire via Shapley-based Reward Attribution

author.name: Xiachong Feng, Yi Jiang, Xiaocheng Feng, Deyi Yin, Libo Qin, Yangfan Ye, Lei Huang, Weitao Ma, Yuxuan Gu, Chonghan Qin, Bing Qin, Lingpeng Kong

entry.summary: Proposes SAVOIR, a Shapley value-based credit assignment framework for training socially intelligent language agents via RL, grounded in cooperative game theory for multi-turn dialogue.

entry.title: Large Language Models Exhibit Normative Conformity

author.name: Mikako Bito, Keita Nishimoto, Kimitaka Asatani, Ichiro Sakata

entry.summary: Shows that LLMs exhibit normative conformity (changing responses to avoid social conflict) distinct from informational conformity, with implications for LLM-based multi-agent decision-making.

entry.title: Do Agents Dream of Root Shells? Partial-Credit Evaluation of LLM Agents in Capture The Flag Challenges

author.name: Ali Al-Kaswan, Maksim Plotnikov, Maxim H\'ajek, Roland V\'izner, Arie van Deursen, Maliheh Izadi

entry.summary: Presents DeepRed, an open-source CTF benchmark with partial-credit scoring for evaluating LLM agents on realistic cybersecurity challenges, moving beyond binary solved/unsolved outcomes.

entry.title: HELM: Harness-Enhanced Long-horizon Memory for Vision-Language-Action Manipulation

author.name: Zijian Zeng, Fei Ding, Huiming Yang, Xianwei Li

entry.summary: Presents HELM, a model-agnostic framework for improving Vision-Language-Action models on long-horizon manipulation tasks. Identifies three execution-loop deficiencies (memory, verification, recovery gaps) and addresses them with episodic memory, state verification, and harness control components.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning Small Reasoning Models for Quantum Field Theory

author.name: Nathaniel S. Woodward, Zhiqi Gao, Yurii Kvasiuk, Kendrick M. Smith, Frederic Sala, Moritz M\"unchmeyer

entry.summary: Performs the first fine-tuning study of small (7B) reasoning models for theoretical physics, specifically Quantum Field Theory. Develops a data generation pipeline for synthetic QFT problems and curated collections for training verifiable reasoning capabilities.

entry.title: Refute-or-Promote: An Adversarial Stage-Gated Multi-Agent Review Methodology for High-Precision LLM-Assisted Defect Discovery

author.name: Abhinav Agarwal

entry.summary: Presents Refute-or-Promote, a multi-agent adversarial pipeline for LLM-assisted software defect discovery that uses adversarial kill mandates and cross-model critics to reduce false positives. Over 31 days across 7 targets, killed ~79% of candidates before advancing high-precision findings.

entry.title: ProjLens: Unveiling the Role of Projectors in Multimodal Model Safety

author.name: Kun Wang, Cheng Qian, Miao Yu, Lilan Peng, Liang Lin, Jiaming Zhang, Tianyu Zhang, Yu Cheng, Yang Wang

entry.summary: Introduces ProjLens, an interpretability framework for understanding backdoor attacks in Multimodal LLMs through the lens of projector modules. Shows that even projector-only fine-tuning introduces backdoor vulnerability with a mechanism different from full-model poisoning.

entry.title: Rethinking Scale: Deployment Trade-offs of Small Language Models under Agent Paradigms

author.name: Xinlin Wang, Mats Brorsson

entry.summary: Presents the first large-scale study of Small Language Models (<10B parameters) under agent paradigms (tool use, multi-agent collaboration), examining deployment trade-offs and how agent frameworks compensate for SLM limitations.

entry.title: HP-Edit: A Human-Preference Post-Training Framework for Image Editing

author.name: Fan Li, Chonghuinan Wang, Lina Lei, Yuping Qiu, Jiaqi Xu, Jiaxiu Jiang, Xinran Qin, Zhikai Chen, Fenglong Song, Zhixin Wang, Renjing Pei, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: HP-Edit proposes a post-training framework for aligning image editing diffusion models with human preferences using RLHF, introducing RealPref-50K, a dataset of 50K real-world human preference annotations across eight editing tasks.

entry.title: Cyber Defense Benchmark: Agentic Threat Hunting Evaluation for LLMs in SecOps

author.name: Alankrit Chona, Igor Kozlov, Ambuj Kumar

entry.summary: Introduces the Cyber Defense Benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on threat hunting in SOC analyst tasks, wrapping 106 real attack procedures into a Gymnasium RL environment with 75K-135K log records per episode.

entry.title: Benign Overfitting in Adversarial Training for Vision Transformers

author.name: Jiaming Zhang, Meng Ding, Shaopeng Fu, Jingfeng Zhang, Di Wang

entry.summary: Provides the first theoretical analysis of adversarial training for Vision Transformers, showing benign overfitting occurs under certain signal-to-noise ratios and perturbation budgets.

entry.title: FASTER: Value-Guided Sampling for Fast RL

author.name: Perry Dong, Alexander Swerdlow, Dorsa Sadigh, Chelsea Finn

entry.summary: FASTER proposes value-guided sampling for diffusion-based RL policies that traces performance gains back to earlier denoising steps, formulating multi-sample selection as an MDP to progressively filter candidates before full denoising.

entry.title: Rethinking Dataset Distillation: Hard Truths about Soft Labels

author.name: Priyam Dey, Aditya Sahdev, Sunny Bhati, Konda Reddy Mopuri, R. Venkatesh Babu

entry.summary: Shows that in large-scale dataset distillation with soft labels, random image baselines perform on par with SOTA methods, and analyzes the role of data quality across different label regimes.

entry.title: Mechanistic Anomaly Detection via Functional Attribution

author.name: Hugo Lyons Keenan, Christopher Leckie, Sarah Erfani

entry.summary: Reframes mechanistic anomaly detection as functional attribution, using influence functions to measure coupling between test samples and a reference set. Architecture-agnostic and resistant to obfuscation.

entry.title: Policy Gradient Primal-Dual Method for Safe Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback

author.name: Qiang Liu, Adrienne Kline, Ermin Wei

entry.summary: Formulates Safe RLHF as an infinite-horizon discounted CMDP and proposes two algorithms that don't require reward model fitting, with theoretical analysis for continuing interaction settings.

entry.title: Accelerating Optimization and Machine Learning through Decentralization

author.name: Ziqin Chen, Zuang Wang, Yongqiang Wang

entry.summary: Demonstrates that decentralized optimization can paradoxically accelerate convergence over centralized methods, reframing decentralization from a necessary compromise to a potential advantage. This challenges conventional wisdom about distributed training.

entry.title: Planning in entropy-regularized Markov decision processes and games

author.name: Jean-Bastien Grill, Omar Darwiche Domingues, Pierre M\'enard, R\'emi Munos, Michal Valko

entry.summary: Proposes SmoothCruiser, a planning algorithm for entropy-regularized MDPs and two-player games achieving O(1/epsilon^4) sample complexity, which is problem-independent. This contrasts with non-regularized settings where no polynomial worst-case guarantees exist.

entry.title: Dual Triangle Attention: Effective Bidirectional Attention Without Positional Embeddings

author.name: Logan Halle, Jason P. Gleghorn

entry.summary: Introduces Dual Triangle Attention, a bidirectional attention mechanism that splits each head into two complementary triangular masks (past-and-self, future-and-self), providing positional information without explicit positional embeddings.

entry.title: Benchmarking Quantum Kernel Support Vector Machines Against Classical Baselines on Tabular Data: A Rigorous Empirical Study with Hardware Validation

author.name: Siavash Kakavand, Christoph Strohmeyer, Michael Schlotter

entry.summary: Presents a rigorous empirical benchmark of quantum kernel SVMs against classical baselines across 970 experiments, finding no statistically significant quantum advantage at alpha=0.05, though quantum methods show steeper learning curves.

entry.title: Probing for Reading Times

author.name: Eleftheria Tsipidi, Samuel Kiegeland, Francesco Ignazio Re, Tianyang Xu, Mario Giulianelli, Karolina Stanczak, Ryan Cotterell

entry.summary: Probes language model representations for human reading times across five languages, finding that early layers outperform surprisal in predicting early-pass eye-tracking measures, suggesting early processing of syntactic cues.

entry.title: Disparities In Negation Understanding Across Languages In Vision-Language Models

author.name: Charikleia Moraitaki, Sarah Pan, Skyler Pulling, Gwendolyn Flusche, Kumail Alhamoud, Marzyeh Ghassemi

entry.summary: Introduces the first human-verified multilingual negation benchmark for VLMs spanning 7 languages, finding systematic affirmation bias that varies by language. Standard CLIP fails most on Arabic and Tagalog.

entry.title: Detoxification for LLM: From Dataset Itself

author.name: Wei Shao, Yihang Wang, Gaoyu Zhu, Ziqiang Cheng, Lei Yu, Jiafeng Guo, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes HSPD pipeline with SoCD for detoxifying pretraining data directly, rather than post-training or inference-time detoxification. LLM guides localization and rewriting of toxic spans while preserving semantics.

entry.title: Voice of India: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Real-World Speech Recognition in India

author.name: Kaushal Bhogale, Manas Dhir, Amritansh Walecha, Manmeet Kaur, Vanshika Chhabra, Aaditya Pareek, Hanuman Sidh, Sagar Jain, Bhaskar Singh, Utkarsh Singh, Tahir Javed, Shobhit Banga, Mitesh M. Khapra

entry.summary: Introduces Voice of India, a large-scale ASR benchmark from real telephonic conversations covering 15 Indian languages across 139 regional clusters, with 536 hours from 36,691 speakers and spelling variation-aware evaluation.

entry.title: Mind the Unseen Mass: Unmasking LLM Hallucinations via Soft-Hybrid Alphabet Estimation

author.name: Hongxing Pan, Yingying Guo, Wenqing Kuang, Jiashi Lu

entry.summary: Proposes SHADE, an estimator combining Good-Turing coverage with heat-kernel spectral analysis for uncertainty quantification in black-box LLMs, addressing underestimation of semantic diversity in small sample settings.

entry.title: HarDBench: A Benchmark for Draft-Based Co-Authoring Jailbreak Attacks for Safe Human-LLM Collaborative Writing

author.name: Euntae Kim, Soomin Han, Buru Chang

entry.summary: Introduces HarDBench, a benchmark for evaluating LLM robustness against draft-based co-authoring jailbreak attacks, where users provide harmful drafts and ask LLMs to complete/revise them.

entry.title: Lost in Translation: Do LVLM Judges Generalize Across Languages?

author.name: Md Tahmid Rahman Laskar, Mohammed Saidul Islam, Mir Tafseer Nayeem, Amran Bhuiyan, Mizanur Rahman, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque, Jimmy Huang

entry.summary: Introduces MM-JudgeBench, the first large-scale multilingual multimodal benchmark for evaluating judge models, with 60K+ pairwise instances across 25 languages. Reveals that reward models used for LVLM alignment degrade significantly in non-English settings.

entry.title: A Self-Evolving Framework for Efficient Terminal Agents via Observational Context Compression

author.name: Jincheng Ren, Siwei Wu, Yizhi Li, Kang Zhu, Shu Xu, Boyu Feng, Ruibin Yuan, Wei Zhang, Riza Batista-Navarro, Jian Yang, Chenghua Lin

entry.summary: Proposes TACO, a self-evolving framework that automatically discovers compression rules for terminal agent observations, reducing quadratic token cost growth in multi-turn agentic tasks. The framework is plug-and-play and generalizes across terminal environments.

entry.title: URoPE: Universal Relative Position Embedding across Geometric Spaces

author.name: Yichen Xie, Depu Meng, Chensheng Peng, Yihan Hu, Quentin Herau, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Wei Zhan

entry.summary: Proposes URoPE, extending Rotary Position Embedding to cross-view and cross-dimensional geometric spaces by projecting 3D points along camera rays. Enables positional encoding across camera views in a unified framework.

entry.title: Denoising, Fast and Slow: Difficulty-Aware Adaptive Sampling for Image Generation

author.name: Johannes Schusterbauer, Ming Gui, Yusong Li, Pingchuan Ma, Felix Krause, Bj\"orn Ommer

entry.summary: Proposes patch-level adaptive noise scheduling for diffusion/flow models where different image regions get different timesteps and compute. Introduces a timestep sampler controlling maximum patch-level information during training.

entry.title: CityRAG: Stepping Into a City via Spatially-Grounded Video Generation

author.name: Gene Chou, Charles Herrmann, Kyle Genova, Boyang Deng, Songyou Peng, Bharath Hariharan, Jason Y. Zhang, Noah Snavely, Philipp Henzler

entry.summary: Presents CityRAG, a video generative model that uses geo-registered data as context to ground generation to real physical locations while maintaining learned priors for complex motion and appearance changes. Targets autonomous driving simulation.

entry.title: Mask World Model: Predicting What Matters for Robust Robot Policy Learning

author.name: Yunfan Lou, Xiaowei Chi, Xiaojie Zhang, Zezhong Qian, Chengxuan Li, Rongyu Zhang, Yaoxu Lyu, Guoyu Song, Chuyao Fu, Haoxuan Xu, Pengwei Wang, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces Mask World Model (MWM), which predicts semantic mask evolution instead of RGB pixels in world models for robot policy learning. Creates a geometric information bottleneck forcing focus on essential physical dynamics.

entry.title: Beyond One Output: Visualizing and Comparing Distributions of Language Model Generations

author.name: Emily Reif, Claire Yang, Jared Hwang, Deniz Nazar, Noah Smith, Jeff Heer

entry.summary: Introduces GROVE, an interactive visualization tool that represents multiple LLM generations as overlapping paths through a text graph, revealing distributional structure like modes and edge cases. Based on a formative study with 13 LM researchers.

entry.title: Explicit Trait Inference for Multi-Agent Coordination

author.name: Suhaib Abdurahman, Etsuko Ishii, Katerina Margatina, Divya Bhargavi, Monica Sunkara, Yi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Explicit Trait Inference (ETI), enabling LLM agents to infer partner warmth and competence from interaction histories to improve coordination. Reduces payoff loss by 45-77% in economic games.

entry.title: GRASPrune: Global Gating for Budgeted Structured Pruning of Large Language Models

author.name: Ziyang Wang, Jiangfeng Xiao, Chuan Xiao, Ruoxiang Li, Rui Mao, Jianbin Qin

entry.summary: Introduces GRASPrune, a structured pruning framework that jointly prunes FFN channels and KV head groups under a global budget using learned gate scores with projected straight-through estimators.

entry.title: SpikeMLLM: Spike-based Multimodal Large Language Models via Modality-Specific Temporal Scales and Temporal Compression

author.name: Han Xu, Zhiyong Qin, Di Shang, Jiahong Zhang, Xuerui Qiu, Bo Lei, Tiejun Huang, Bo Xu, Guoqi Li

entry.summary: Proposes SpikeMLLM, the first spike-based framework for multimodal LLMs, unifying ANN quantization in spiking representation space with modality-specific temporal scales and temporal compression.

entry.title: Easy Samples Are All You Need: Self-Evolving LLMs via Data-Efficient Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhiyin Yu, Bo Zhang, Qibin Hou, Zhonghai Wu, Xiao Luo, Lei Bai

entry.summary: Proposes EasyRL, an RL approach for LLMs inspired by cognitive learning theory that starts with easy labeled samples and progressively tackles harder unlabeled data, avoiding annotation costs and model collapse.

entry.title: From Craft to Kernel: A Governance-First Execution Architecture and Semantic ISA for Agentic Computers

author.name: Xiangyu Wen, Yuang Zhao, Xiaoyu Xu, Lingjun Chen, Changran Xu, Shu Chi, Jianrong Ding, Zeju Li, Haomin Li, Li Jiang, Fangxin Liu, Qiang Xu

entry.summary: Proposes Arbiter-K, a governance-first execution architecture for agentic AI that treats the LLM as a 'Probabilistic Processing Unit' encapsulated by a deterministic neuro-symbolic kernel with a Semantic ISA.

entry.title: Curiosity-Critic: Cumulative Prediction Error Improvement as a Tractable Intrinsic Reward for World Model Training

author.name: Vin Bhaskara, Haicheng Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Curiosity-Critic, an intrinsic reward mechanism that grounds exploration in cumulative prediction error improvement rather than single-step novelty, using a learned critic for the asymptotic error baseline.

entry.title: LLM-as-Judge Framework for Evaluating Tone-Induced Hallucination in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zhiyuan Jiang, Weihao Hong, Xinlei Guan, Tejaswi Dhandu, Miles Q. Li, Meng Xu, Kuan Huang, Umamaheswara Rao Tida, Bingyu Shen, Daehan Kwak, Boyang Li

entry.summary: Introduces Ghost-100, a benchmark of 800 synthetically generated images to evaluate how progressively coercive prompt phrasing increases hallucination in Vision-Language Models. Tests tone-induced hallucination across task types using LLM-as-Judge evaluation with negative-ground-truth design.

entry.title: Gated Memory Policy

author.name: Yihuai Gao, Jinyun Liu, Shuang Li, Shuran Song

entry.summary: Proposes Gated Memory Policy (GMP) for robotic manipulation that learns when and what to recall from history via a learned memory gate mechanism. Addresses the problem that naively extending observation histories often degrades visuomotor policy performance.

entry.title: Talking to a Know-It-All GPT or a Second-Guesser Claude? How Repair reveals unreliable Multi-Turn Behavior in LLMs

author.name: Clara Lachenmaier, Hannah Bultmann, Sina Zarrie{\ss}

entry.summary: Studies how LLMs handle conversational repair in multi-turn dialogues around math questions, finding stark differences across models—from being resistant to repair attempts to being easily manipulated. Shows behavior becomes less predictable as conversations extend.

entry.title: Location Not Found: Exposing Implicit Local and Global Biases in Multilingual LLMs

author.name: Guy Mor-Lan, Omer Goldman, Matan Eyal, Adi Mayrav Gilady, Sivan Eiger, Idan Szpektor, Avinatan Hassidim, Yossi Matias, Reut Tsarfaty

entry.summary: Presents LocQA, a test set of 2,156 locale-ambiguous questions in 12 languages to expose implicit geographic biases in multilingual LLMs. Questions have no locale indicators beyond the querying language, revealing models' implicit priors about locations.

entry.title: RDP LoRA: Geometry-Driven Identification for Parameter-Efficient Adaptation in Large Language Models

author.name: Yusuf \c{C}elebi, Ya\u{g}{\i}z Asker, \"Ozay Ezerceli, Mahmoud ElHussieni, Selva Ta\c{s}, Reyhan Bayraktar, Fatma Bet\"ul Terzio\u{g}lu

entry.summary: Models LLM hidden state evolution as a geometric trajectory and uses the Ramer-Douglas-Peucker algorithm to identify critical breakpoints for deciding where to apply LoRA, replacing heuristic layer selection with training-free geometric analysis.

entry.title: LASER: Learning Active Sensing for Continuum Field Reconstruction

author.name: Huayu Deng, Jinghui Zhong, Xiangming Zhu, Yunbo Wang, Xiaokang Yang

entry.summary: LASER proposes a unified framework for active sensing that formulates sensor placement as a POMDP, using a continuum field latent world model with RL to simulate 'what-if' scenarios in latent space. This enables adaptive sensor movement rather than fixed layouts for physical field reconstruction.

entry.title: Impact of large language models on peer review opinions from a fine-grained perspective: Evidence from top conference proceedings in AI

author.name: Wenqing Wu, Chengzhi Zhang, Yi Zhao, Tong Bao

entry.summary: Studies how LLMs have impacted peer review at top AI conferences from a fine-grained perspective, examining changes in linguistic form, evaluative focus, and recommendation signals in review reports.

entry.title: UniT: Toward a Unified Physical Language for Human-to-Humanoid Policy Learning and World Modeling

author.name: Boyu Chen, Yi Chen, Lu Qiu, Jerry Bai, Yuying Ge, Yixiao Ge

entry.summary: UniT introduces a unified latent action tokenizer for human-to-humanoid transfer, using visual anchoring and tri-branch cross-reconstruction to bridge kinematic mismatches between human and robot embodiments.

entry.title: Efficient Mixture-of-Experts LLM Inference with Apple Silicon NPUs

author.name: Afsara Benazir, Felix Xiaozhu Lin

entry.summary: Demonstrates efficient MoE LLM inference on Apple Neural Engine (NPU), solving challenges of dynamic tensor shapes, irregular operators, and dispatch overhead for neural processing units.

entry.title: HardNet++: Nonlinear Constraint Enforcement in Neural Networks

author.name: Andrea Goertzen, Kaveh Alim, Navid Azizan

entry.summary: Introduces HardNet++, a method for enforcing general nonlinear constraints on neural network outputs by simulating implicit differentiation at inference time. Critical for safety-critical applications where soft constraints are insufficient.

entry.title: Less Is More: Cognitive Load and the Single-Prompt Ceiling in LLM Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Manuel Israel Cazares

entry.summary: Systematic empirical study of prompt engineering for formal mathematical reasoning showing a 'single-prompt ceiling' around 60-79% accuracy despite extensive optimization. Tests 40+ prompt variants across three LLMs.

entry.title: TRN-R1-Zero: Text-rich Network Reasoning via LLMs with Reinforcement Learning Only

author.name: Yilun Liu, Ruihong Qiu, Zi Huang

entry.summary: Proposes TRN-R1-Zero, a post-training framework for text-rich network reasoning trained solely via reinforcement learning, using a neighbour-aware group relative policy optimization that adjusts rewards based on informativeness of graph context.

entry.title: Mango: Multi-Agent Web Navigation via Global-View Optimization

author.name: Weixi Tong, Yifeng Di, Tianyi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Mango, a multi-agent web navigation method that formulates URL selection as a multi-armed bandit problem, using Thompson Sampling to allocate navigation budget across candidate starting points rather than always starting from the root URL.

entry.title: Debating the Unspoken: Role-Anchored Multi-Agent Reasoning for Half-Truth Detection

author.name: Yixuan Tang, Yirui Zhang, Hang Feng, Anthony K. H. Tung

entry.summary: Proposes RADAR, a multi-agent debate framework for detecting half-truths (factually correct but misleading claims) using adversarial roles (Politician vs Scientist) moderated by a Judge, with early termination.

entry.title: Do Emotions Influence Moral Judgment in Large Language Models?

author.name: Mohammad Saim, Tianyu Jiang

entry.summary: Studies how emotions influence moral judgment in LLMs, showing positive emotions increase moral acceptability and negative emotions decrease it, with effects strong enough to reverse binary judgments in up to 20% of cases.

entry.title: ReflectMT: Internalizing Reflection for Efficient and High-Quality Machine Translation

author.name: Kunquan Li, Yingxue Zhang, Fandong Meng, Jinsong Su

entry.summary: Proposes ReflectMT, a two-stage approach to machine translation that internalizes reflection capability through RL, using a 'translate-first-think-later' paradigm to reduce inference costs while maintaining quality.

entry.title: Are Large Language Models Economically Viable for Industry Deployment?

author.name: Abdullah Mohammad, Sushant Kumar Ray, Pushkar Arora, Rafiq Ali, Ebad Shabbir, Gautam Siddharth Kashyap, Jiechao Gao, Usman Naseem

entry.summary: Presents EDGE-EVAL, an industry-oriented benchmarking framework evaluating LLMs across their full lifecycle on legacy NVIDIA T4 GPUs, addressing the deployment-evaluation gap between accuracy and operational/economic metrics.

entry.title: Beyond Rating: A Comprehensive Evaluation and Benchmark for AI Reviews

author.name: Bowen Li, Haochen Ma, Yuxin Wang, Jie Yang, Xinchi Chen, Xuanjing Huang, Yining Zheng, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: Proposes 'Beyond Rating,' a holistic framework for evaluating AI-generated peer reviews across five dimensions including argumentative alignment and question constructiveness, rather than just rating prediction. Introduces Max-Recall strategy for handling expert disagreement.

entry.title: Discovering a Shared Logical Subspace: Steering LLM Logical Reasoning via Alignment of Natural-Language and Symbolic Views

author.name: Feihao Fang, My T. Thai, Yuanyuan Lei

entry.summary: Uses Canonical Correlation Analysis to discover a shared logical subspace in LLMs that aligns natural-language and symbolic-language reasoning. Steering activations toward this subspace improves logical reasoning performance.

entry.title: Can We Build Scene Graphs, Not Classify Them? FlowSG: Progressive Image-Conditioned Scene Graph Generation with Flow Matching

author.name: Xin Hu, Ke Qin, Wen Yin, Yuan-Fang Li, Ming Li, Tao He

entry.summary: Proposes FlowSG, recasting scene graph generation as continuous-time transport using flow matching on a hybrid discrete-continuous state. Progressively grows image-conditioned scene graphs through constraint-aware refinements using VQ-VAE tokenization.

entry.title: Volume Transformer: Revisiting Vanilla Transformers for 3D Scene Understanding

author.name: Kadir Yilmaz, Adrian Kruse, Tristan H\"ofer, Daan de Geus, Bastian Leibe

entry.summary: Adapts vanilla Transformer encoders to 3D scene understanding with minimal modifications—volumetric patch tokens, full global self-attention, and 3D rotary positional embeddings. The Volume Transformer (Volt) achieves competitive results on 3D semantic segmentation.

entry.title: Opus 4.7 Part 2: Capabilities and Reactions

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's detailed analysis of Claude Opus 4.7's capabilities, covering benchmarks, general reactions, prompt injection issues, thinking behavior, and instruction following. Concludes it's the most intelligent model in its class with substantial improvements.

entry.title: ClawNet: Human-Symbiotic Agent Network for Cross-User Autonomous Cooperation

author.name: Zhiqin Yang, Zhenyuan Zhang, Xianzhang Jia, Jun Song, Wei Xue, Yonggang Zhang, Yike Guo

entry.summary: Proposes ClawNet, a human-symbiotic agent paradigm for cross-user autonomous cooperation, arguing the next frontier is digitizing human collaborative relationships rather than improving individual agent capability.

entry.title: UAF: A Unified Audio Front-end LLM for Full-Duplex Speech Interaction

author.name: Yadong Li, Guoxin Wu, Haiping Hou, Biye Li

entry.summary: Proposes UAF, a unified audio front-end for full-duplex speech interaction that integrates VAD, turn-taking detection, and other front-end components into a single LLM-based system.

entry.title: Towards Optimal Agentic Architectures for Offensive Security Tasks

author.name: Isaac David, Arthur Gervais

entry.summary: Studies architecture families for offensive security agents, finding through 600 runs that multi-agent systems don't consistently outperform single agents, with best detection reaching 58% on 20 interactive targets.

entry.title: Semantic Needles in Document Haystacks: Sensitivity Testing of LLM-as-a-Judge Similarity Scoring

author.name: Sinan G. Aksoy, Alexandra A. Sabrio, Erik VonKaenel, Lee Burke

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for testing LLM sensitivity to subtle semantic changes in document comparison by embedding altered sentences ('needles') in context ('hay'). Reveals positional bias in within-document comparison and other systematic LLM evaluation failures across five models.

entry.title: Regulating Artificial Intimacy: From Locks and Blocks to Relational Accountability

author.name: Henry Fraser, Jessica M. Szczuka, Raffaele F. Ciriello

entry.summary: Critically examines regulatory responses to companion chatbot tragedies across jurisdictions (Australia, California, New York), analyzing what and who is regulated. Identifies gaps between 'locks and blocks' approaches and proposes relational accountability framework.

entry.title: Decompose, Structure, and Repair: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Autoformalization via Operator Trees

author.name: Xiaoyang Liu, Zineng Dong, Yifan Bai, Yantao Li, Yuntian Liu, Tao Luo

entry.summary: Introduces DSR (Decompose, Structure, Repair), a neuro-symbolic framework for autoformalization that decomposes mathematical statements into logical components, maps them to operator trees, and uses this structure to localize and repair errors in formal translations.

entry.title: FedProxy: Federated Fine-Tuning of LLMs via Proxy SLMs and Heterogeneity-Aware Fusion

author.name: Tao Fan, Guoqiang Ma, Yuanfeng Song, Lixin Fan, Kai Chen, Qiang Yang

entry.summary: Proposes FedProxy for federated fine-tuning of LLMs, replacing weak adapters with a compressed Proxy Small Language Model to serve as a high-fidelity surrogate for collaborative training while protecting IP and privacy.

entry.title: CulturALL: Benchmarking Multilingual and Multicultural Competence of LLMs on Grounded Tasks

author.name: Peiqin Lin, Chenyang Lyu, Wenjiang Luo, Haotian Ye, Md Mehrab Hossain, Chunlan Ma, Shaoxiong Ji, Younes Samih, Bo Zeng, Fan Jiang, Yuanbin Cao, Dilda Duisenbek, Adrian Neo Sau Xun, Daria Pozdniakova, Liubou Misevich, Nevena Marinkovi\'c, Ngoc Gia Linh Nguyen, Thi Khanh Linh Do, Sarakmatak Sophy, Baotian Hu, Guanhua Chen, Gongbo Tang, Alham Fikri Aji, Longyue Wang, Weihua Luo

entry.summary: Presents CulturALL, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating LLMs' multilingual and multicultural competence on grounded tasks requiring real-world cultural reasoning, built via human-AI collaborative annotation framework.

entry.title: HalluAudio: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Hallucination Detection in Large Audio-Language Models

author.name: Feiyu Zhao, Yiming Chen, Wenhuan Lu, Daipeng Zhang, Xianghu Yue, Jianguo Wei

entry.summary: Introduces HalluAudio, the first large-scale hallucination benchmark for Large Audio-Language Models spanning speech, environmental sound, and music with 5K+ human-verified QA pairs across diverse task types.

entry.title: A neural operator framework for data-driven discovery of stability and receptivity in physical systems

author.name: Chengyun Wang, Liwei Chen, Nils Thuerey

entry.summary: Presents a data-driven framework using neural operators and automatic differentiation to discover stability properties and resolvent modes from observation data alone, without requiring governing equations.

entry.title: Detecting Hallucinations in SpeechLLMs at Inference Time Using Attention Maps

author.name: Jonas Waldendorf, Bashar Awwad Shiekh Hasan, Evgenii Tsymbalov

entry.summary: Proposes attention-derived metrics (AudioRatio, AudioConsistency, AudioEntropy, TextEntropy) for detecting hallucinations in Speech LLMs at inference time without gold-standard outputs, using lightweight logistic regression classifiers.

entry.title: Robust Continual Unlearning against Knowledge Erosion and Forgetting Reversal

author.name: Eun-Ju Park, Youjin Shin, Simon S. Woo

entry.summary: Identifies two critical phenomena in continual unlearning: Knowledge Erosion (progressive accuracy degradation) and Forgetting Reversal (previously unlearned data being re-memorized). Proposes a robust approach to address both.

entry.title: The Logical Expressiveness of Topological Neural Networks

author.name: Amirreza Akbari, Amauri H. Souza, Vikas Garg

entry.summary: Analyzes the logical expressiveness of Topological Neural Networks (TNNs) through isomorphism testing and first-order logic, characterizing precisely which binary classifiers TNNs can represent.

entry.title: Safe Continual Reinforcement Learning in Non-stationary Environments

author.name: Austin Coursey, Abel Diaz-Gonzalez, Marcos Quinones-Grueiro, Gautam Biswas

entry.summary: Studies the intersection of continual RL and safe RL in non-stationary environments, addressing the understudied problem of maintaining safety constraints while adapting to changing dynamics.

entry.title: Beyond Bellman: High-Order Generator Regression for Continuous-Time Policy Evaluation

author.name: Yaowei Zheng, Richong Zhang, Shenxi Wu, Shirui Bian, Haosong Zhang, Li Zeng, Xingjian Ma, Yichi Zhang

entry.summary: Studies continuous-time policy evaluation from discrete trajectories, using higher-order generator estimation from multi-step transitions to go beyond first-order Bellman recursion. Provides end-to-end error decomposition.

entry.title: Auditing LLMs for Algorithmic Fairness in Casenote-Augmented Tabular Prediction

author.name: Xiao Qi Lee, Ezinne Nwankwo, Angela Zhou

entry.summary: Audits algorithmic fairness of LLM-based tabular classification on a real housing placement task, finding that fine-tuned models with casenote summaries can improve both accuracy and fairness simultaneously.

entry.title: Phase Transitions in the Fluctuations of Functionals of Random Neural Networks

author.name: Simmaco Di Lillo, Leonardo Maini, Domenico Marinucci

entry.summary: Establishes central and non-central limit theorems for functionals of infinitely-wide random neural networks on spheres, identifying three distinct limiting regimes based on covariance function fixed points as depth increases.

entry.title: Investigating Counterfactual Unfairness in LLMs towards Identities through Humor

author.name: Shubin Kim, Yejin Son, Junyeong Park, Keummin Ka, Seungbeen Lee, Jaeyoung Lee, Hyeju Jang, Alice Oh, Youngjae Yu

entry.summary: Investigates counterfactual unfairness in LLMs through humor, examining how model responses change when swapping speaker/addressee identities across humor generation, intention inference, and impact prediction tasks.

entry.title: LogosKG: Hardware-Optimized Scalable and Interpretable Knowledge Graph Retrieval

author.name: He Cheng, Yifu Wu, Saksham Khatwani, Maya Kruse, Dmitriy Dligach, Timothy A. Miller, Majid Afshar, Yanjun Gao

entry.summary: Introduces LogosKG, a hardware-aligned framework for scalable k-hop knowledge graph retrieval that uses symbolic KG formulations with decomposed representations, scaling to billion-edge graphs with substantial efficiency gains.

entry.title: What Makes an LLM a Good Optimizer? A Trajectory Analysis of LLM-Guided Evolutionary Search

author.name: Xinhao Zhang, Xi Chen, Fran\c{c}ois Portet, Maxime Peyrard

entry.summary: Large-scale study of LLM-guided evolutionary search across 15 LLMs and 8 tasks, analyzing optimization trajectories. Finds strong LLM optimizers act as local refiners with incremental improvements rather than making large leaps, and zero-shot ability only partially explains optimization outcomes.

entry.title: Superficial Success vs. Internal Breakdown: An Empirical Study of Generalization in Adaptive Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Namyoung So (Department of Computer Science, Hanyang University, Seoul, Republic of Korea), Seokgyu Jang (Department of Computer Science, Hanyang University, Seoul, Republic of Korea), Taeuk Kim (Department of Computer Science, Hanyang University, Seoul, Republic of Korea)

entry.summary: Empirically studies generalization of adaptive multi-agent systems, revealing 'topological overfitting' (failure across domains) and 'illusory coordination' (surface accuracy without genuine agent coordination). Highlights fundamental limitations of current adaptive MAS.

entry.title: Toward Clinically Acceptable Chest X-ray Report Generation: A Qualitative Retrospective Pilot Study of CXRMate-2

author.name: Aaron Nicolson, Elizabeth J. Cooper, Hwan-Jin Yoon, Claire McCafferty, Ramya Krishnan, Michelle Craigie, Nivene Saad, Jason Dowling, Ian A. Scott, Bevan Koopman

entry.summary: Presents CXRMate-2, a chest X-ray report generation model combining multimodal conditioning with RL, achieving significant improvements over MedGemma. Includes a blinded radiologist evaluation comparing AI vs human reports.

entry.title: Unveiling Fine-Grained Visual Traces: Evaluating Multimodal Interleaved Reasoning Chains in Multimodal STEM Tasks

author.name: Jing Jin, Hao Liu, Yan Bai, Yihang Lou, Zhenke Wang, Tianrun Yuan, Juntong Chen, Yongkang Zhu, Fanhu Zeng, Xuanyu Zhu, Yige Xu

entry.summary: Introduces StepSTEM, a graduate-level benchmark of 283 STEM problems for evaluating fine-grained cross-modal reasoning in MLLMs. Enforces strict modality complementarity to prevent unimodal shortcuts and evaluates reasoning processes, not just final answers.

entry.title: Face Anything: 4D Face Reconstruction from Any Image Sequence

author.name: Umut Kocasari, Simon Giebenhain, Richard Shaw, Matthias Nie{\ss}ner

entry.summary: Presents Face Anything, a unified method for 4D facial reconstruction from any image sequence using canonical facial point prediction, enabling temporally consistent geometry and reliable correspondences in a single feed-forward model. From Matthias Nießner's group.

entry.title: Reflectively stable consequentialists are expected utility maximisers

author.name: Pedro Afonso

entry.summary: Presents a new coherence theorem showing that 'reflectively stable consequentialists'—agents whose decision procedure endorses itself—must be expected utility maximizers. Provides a formal justification for EU maximization from self-consistency.

entry.title: Towards Scalable Lifelong Knowledge Editing with Selective Knowledge Suppression

author.name: Dahyun Jung, Jaewook Lee, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: Proposes LightEdit for scalable lifelong knowledge editing of LLMs, selecting relevant knowledge from retrieved information to modify queries efficiently while avoiding catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: Reasoning-Aware AIGC Detection via Alignment and Reinforcement

author.name: Zhao Wang, Max Xiong, Jianxun Lian, Zhicheng Dou

entry.summary: Introduces REVEAL, a detection framework for AI-generated content that generates interpretable reasoning chains before classification, using SFT then RL. Also releases AIGC-text-bank, a multi-domain dataset.

entry.title: DT2IT-MRM: Debiased Preference Construction and Iterative Training for Multimodal Reward Modeling

author.name: Zhihong Zhang, Jie Zhao, Xiaojian Huang, Jin Xu, Zhuodong Luo, Xin Liu, Jiansheng Wei, Xuejin Chen

entry.summary: Proposes DT2IT-MRM for multimodal reward modeling with debiased preference construction, addressing granularity, textual style bias, and unreliable preference signals in existing datasets.

entry.title: Detecting Data Contamination in Large Language Models

author.name: Juliusz Janicki, Savvas Chamezopoulos, Evangelos Kanoulas, Georgios Tsatsaronis

entry.summary: Studies black-box membership inference attacks against LLMs for data contamination detection, compares SOTA methods under unified datasets, and proposes a new 'Familiarity Ranking' approach.

entry.title: Two-dimensional early exit optimisation of LLM inference

author.name: Jan H\r{u}la, David Adamczyk, Tom\'a\v{s} Filip, Martin Pavl\'i\v{c}ek, Petr Sos\'ik

entry.summary: Introduces a 2D early exit strategy for LLM inference that coordinates both layer-wise and sentence-wise exiting, achieving multiplicative speedups of 1.4-2.3x over layer-only early exit.

entry.title: Evaluating Answer Leakage Robustness of LLM Tutors against Adversarial Student Attacks

author.name: Jin Zhao, Marta Kne\v{z}evi\'c, Tanja K\"aser

entry.summary: Evaluates LLM tutor robustness against adversarial students trying to extract answers instead of learning, testing multiple model families and attack strategies.

entry.title: Experiments or Outcomes? Probing Scientific Feasibility in Large Language Models

author.name: Seyedali Mohammadi, Manas Gaur, Francis Ferraro

entry.summary: Evaluates LLMs on scientific feasibility assessment—predicting whether a claim is consistent with established knowledge. Tests under controlled conditions varying what context is provided (hypothesis-only, experiments, outcomes). Finds that outcome evidence is more reliable than experiment descriptions for improving accuracy.

entry.title: Self-Improving Tabular Language Models via Iterative Group Alignment

author.name: Yunbo Long, Tejumade Afonja, Alexandra Brintrup, Mario Fritz

entry.summary: Introduces TabGRAA, the first self-improving framework for tabular data generation using iterative group-relative advantage alignment. Addresses the limitations of static fine-tuning and autoregressive objectives that neglect global statistical properties of tabular data.

entry.title: RARE: Redundancy-Aware Retrieval Evaluation Framework for High-Similarity Corpora

author.name: Hanjun Cho, Jay-Yoon Lee

entry.summary: Introduces RARE, a redundancy-aware retrieval evaluation framework for corpora with high inter-document similarity (financial reports, legal codes). Shows standard QA benchmarks unfairly penalize retrievers that find sufficient but non-canonical evidence.

entry.title: LBLLM: Lightweight Binarization of Large Language Models via Three-Stage Distillation

author.name: Siqing Song, Chuang Wang, Yong Lang, Yi Yang, Xu-Yao Zhang

entry.summary: Presents LBLLM, a lightweight binarization framework for LLMs achieving W(1+1)A4 quantization through three-stage distillation: PTQ initialization, layer-wise weight binarization with full-precision activations, then learnable activation quantization.

entry.title: Lyapunov-Certified Direct Switching Theory for Q-Learning

author.name: Donghwan Lee

entry.summary: Analyzes Q-learning through a direct stochastic switching system representation, showing the Bellman maximization error can be represented as a stochastic policy. Derives tighter finite-time bounds using joint spectral radius and Lyapunov functions.

entry.title: Task Switching Without Forgetting via Proximal Decoupling

author.name: Pourya Shamsolmoali, Masoumeh Zareapoor, Eric Granger, William A. P. Smith, Yue Lu

entry.summary: Proposes an operator-splitting approach for continual learning that separates task learning from stability enforcement, using proximal operators to explicitly decouple these competing objectives.

entry.title: Accelerating trajectory optimization with Sobolev-trained diffusion policies

author.name: Th\'eotime Le Hellard, Franki Nguimatsia Tiofack, Quentin Le Lidec, Justin Carpentier

entry.summary: Proposes Sobolev training for diffusion policies used as warm-starters for trajectory optimization, where matching derivatives (not just function values) prevents small approximation errors from compounding during rollout.

entry.title: FG$^2$-GDN: Enhancing Long-Context Gated Delta Networks with Doubly Fine-Grained Control

author.name: Pingwei Sun, Yuxuan Hu, Jianchao Tan, Xue Wang, Jiaqi Zhang, Yifan Lu, Yerui Sun, Yuchen Xie, Xunliang Cai

entry.summary: FG²-GDN enhances Gated DeltaNet with channel-wise learning rates in the delta rule update, analogous to per-coordinate adaptive optimizers, improving long-context modeling capacity.

entry.title: Learning Posterior Predictive Distributions for Node Classification from Synthetic Graph Priors

author.name: Jeongwhan Choi, Jongwoo Kim, Woosung Kang, Noseong Park

entry.summary: Proposes learning posterior predictive distributions for universal node classification across diverse graphs by pre-training on synthetic graph priors, inspired by in-context learning in LLMs.

entry.title: Debiased neural operators for estimating functionals

author.name: Konstantin Hess, Dennis Frauen, Niki Kilbertus, Stefan Feuerriegel

entry.summary: DOPE introduces a semiparametric estimator for computing target functionals (e.g., total energy, time in range) from neural operator solutions, with debiasing to correct for neural operator errors.

entry.title: PREF-XAI: Preference-Based Personalized Rule Explanations of Black-Box Machine Learning Models

author.name: Salvatore Greco, Jacek Karolczak, Roman S{\l}owi\'nski, Jerzy Stefanowski

entry.summary: Proposes PREF-XAI, a framework for personalized explanations of black-box models that accounts for individual user preferences rather than providing one-size-fits-all explanations. Uses principled preference learning rather than heuristic adaptations.

entry.title: TrEEStealer: Stealing Decision Trees via Enclave Side Channels

author.name: Jonas Sander, Anja Rabich, Nick Mahling, Felix Maurer, Jonah Heller, Qifan Wang, Thomas Eisenbarth, David Oswald

entry.summary: Demonstrates side-channel attacks on decision trees running in trusted execution environments (TEEs), showing that TEEs don't prevent model extraction when cache-based and interrupt-based side channels are exploited.

entry.title: Trainability Beyond Linearity in Variational Quantum Objectives

author.name: Gordon Ma, Xiufan Li

entry.summary: Identifies the exact boundary of the barren plateau proof template for variational quantum algorithms, showing it applies if and only if the loss is affine in measured statistics. Provides structural characterization of trainability.

entry.title: Fast estimation of Gaussian mixture components via centering and singular value thresholding

author.name: Huan Qing

entry.summary: Proposes a simple method for estimating the number of Gaussian mixture components: center data, compute singular values, threshold. Proves consistency under mild separation conditions in high-dimensional settings.

entry.title: Model-Agnostic Meta Learning for Class Imbalance Adaptation

author.name: Hanshu Rao, Guangzeng Han, Xiaolei Huang

entry.summary: Introduces HAMR, a meta-learning framework that uses bi-level optimization to adaptively weight instances for class-imbalanced NLP tasks, with neighborhood-aware resampling to focus on hard examples. Validated across 6 datasets.

entry.title: HoWToBench: Holistic Evaluation for LLM's Capability in Human-level Writing using Tree of Writing

author.name: Andrew Zhuoer Feng, Cunxiang Wang, Yu Luo, Lin Fan, Yilin Zhou, Zikang Wang, Xiaotao Gu, Jie Tang, Hongning Wang, Minlie Huang

entry.summary: Proposes Tree-of-Writing (ToW) for LLM writing evaluation that explicitly models aggregation weights of sub-features in a tree structure, and HowToBench, a large-scale Chinese writing benchmark with 12 genres.

entry.title: VCE: A zero-cost hallucination mitigation method of LVLMs via visual contrastive editing

author.name: Yanbin Huang, Yisen Li, Guiyao Tie, Xiaoye Qu, Pan Zhou, Hongfei Wang, Zhaofan Zou, Hao Sun, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: Proposes Visual Contrastive Editing (VCE), a zero-cost post-hoc method to mitigate object hallucination in large vision-language models by analyzing model responses to contrastive visual perturbations and suppressing hallucination tendencies.

entry.title: CrossPan: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Cross-Sequence Pancreas MRI Segmentation and Generalization

author.name: Linkai Peng, Cuiling Sun, Zheyuan Zhang, Wanying Dou, Halil Ertugrul Aktas, Andrea M Bejar, Elif Keles, Tamas Gonda, Michael B Wallace, Zongwei Zhou, Gorkem Durak, Rajesh N Keswani, Ulas Bagci

entry.summary: Introduces CrossPan, a multi-institutional benchmark of 1,386 3D pancreas MRI scans across three sequences, revealing that cross-sequence domain shifts are far more severe than cross-center variability, with models collapsing from >0.85 to <0.02 Dice.

entry.title: Learning to Credit the Right Steps: Objective-aware Process Optimization for Visual Generation

author.name: Rui Li, Ke Hao, Yuanzhi Liang, Haibin Huang, Chi Zhang, YunGu, XueLong Li

entry.summary: Proposes objective-aware process optimization for visual generation using GRPO with step-specific credit assignment across multiple reward models, replacing uniform reward propagation across diffusion trajectories.

entry.title: Silicon Aware Neural Networks

author.name: Sebastian Fieldhouse, Kea-Tiong Tang

entry.summary: Proposes mapping Differentiable Logic Gate Networks directly to digital CMOS standard cell libraries, with a novel loss function optimizing circuit area and power consumption during training.

entry.title: GRAFT: Geometric Refinement and Fitting Transformer for Human Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Pradyumna YM, Yuxuan Xue, Yue Chen, Nikita Kister, Istv\'an S\'ar\'andi, Gerard Pons-Moll

entry.summary: Presents GRAFT, a learned human-scene interaction prior that predicts corrective parameter updates to iteratively refine human meshes by reasoning about 3D human-scene relationships. Achieves optimization-quality contact reasoning at feed-forward speed.

entry.title: InHabit: Leveraging Image Foundation Models for Scalable 3D Human Placement

author.name: Nikita Kister, Pradyumna YM, Istv\'an S\'ar\'andi, Jiayi Wang, Anna Khoreva, Gerard Pons-Moll

entry.summary: Introduces InHabit, a fully automatic pipeline for populating 3D scenes with interacting humans by transferring 2D foundation model knowledge to 3D via a render-generate-lift principle. From Gerard Pons-Moll's group.

entry.title: SpanVLA: Efficient Action Bridging and Learning from Negative-Recovery Samples for Vision-Language-Action Model

author.name: Zewei Zhou (Tony), Ruining Yang (Tony), Xuewei (Tony), Qi, Yiluan Guo, Sherry X. Chen, Tao Feng, Kateryna Pistunova, Yishan Shen, Lili Su, Jiaqi Ma

entry.summary: Proposes SpanVLA, an end-to-end autonomous driving framework integrating autoregressive VLM reasoning with flow-matching action generation. Includes negative-recovery sample learning for robustness and reduces latency via efficient action bridging.

entry.title: AnyRecon: Arbitrary-View 3D Reconstruction with Video Diffusion Model

author.name: Yutian Chen, Shi Guo, Renbiao Jin, Tianshuo Yang, Xin Cai, Yawen Luo, Mingxin Yang, Mulin Yu, Linning Xu, Tianfan Xue

entry.summary: Proposes AnyRecon, a scalable 3D reconstruction framework from arbitrary unordered sparse inputs using video diffusion, with a persistent global scene memory via capture view cache and removal of temporal compression for geometric fidelity.

entry.title: A taxonomy of barriers to trading with early misaligned AIs

author.name: Alexa Pan

entry.summary: Provides a detailed taxonomy of barriers to making deals with early misaligned AIs, covering insufficient gains from trade, counterparty risks from both sides, coordination failures, and practical implementation challenges.

entry.title: FB-NLL: A Feature-Based Approach to Tackle Noisy Labels in Personalized Federated Learning

author.name: Abdulmoneam Ali, Ahmed Arafa

entry.summary: Proposes FB-NLL, a feature-centric framework for personalized federated learning that decouples user clustering from training dynamics, making it robust to noisy labels by characterizing users through their local feature spaces.

entry.title: MMControl: Unified Multi-Modal Control for Joint Audio-Video Generation

author.name: Liyang Li, Wen Wang, Canyu Zhao, Tianjian Feng, Zhiyue Zhao, Hao Chen, Chunhua Shen

entry.summary: Presents MMControl for multi-modal control in joint audio-video generation, enabling visual and acoustic control signals (reference images, audio, depth maps, poses) via a dual-stream conditional injection mechanism in DiTs.

entry.title: SynAgent: Generalizable Cooperative Humanoid Manipulation via Solo-to-Cooperative Agent Synergy

author.name: Wei Yao, Haohan Ma, Hongwen Zhang, Yunlian Sun, Liangjun Xing, Zhile Yang, Yuanjun Guo, Yebin Liu, Jinhui Tang

entry.summary: Presents SynAgent, a framework for cooperative humanoid manipulation that transfers single-agent human-object interaction skills to multi-agent scenarios using an interaction-preserving retargeting method based on Delaunay tetrahedralization.

entry.title: Learning Lifted Action Models from Unsupervised Visual Traces

author.name: Kai Xi, Stephen Gould, Sylvie Thi\'ebaux

entry.summary: Proposes a deep learning framework that jointly learns state prediction, action prediction, and lifted action models from sequences of state images without action observation, using a MILP to prevent prediction collapse.
